<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">118th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">2d Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 10075</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20241029">October 29, 2024</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="O000175">Mr. Ogles</sponsor> (for himself and <cosponsor name-id="M001211">Mrs. Miller of Illinois</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HIF00">Committee on Energy and Commerce</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To prohibit an entity from receiving Federal funds if such entity provides to any person any medical or surgical intervention for the purpose of assisting an individual’s disassociation from his or her sex.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H45B743BB62094EC48FF1EC06EB6094AE" style="OLC"><section id="H11FF48C2CE9C4A33804C5E9930A379F9" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Stopping the Mutilation of Children Act of 2024</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="HBF00E96BFCC9411F9E9D5101582A4A9A" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2.</enum><header>Prohibition</header><subsection id="H33B880B6528F444C8AAC9A7D7DA841E9"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In General</header><text>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no Federal funds may be provided, directly or indirectly, to an entity which provides to any person any medical or surgical intervention for the purpose of assisting an individual’s disassociation from his or her sex.</text></subsection><subsection id="H06906F1BA63644D29BCC4F9EB22C3933"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Rule of Construction</header><text>Nothing in this Act shall be construed to prohibit funding to entities which provide medical or surgical intervention in response to a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident.</text></subsection></section><section id="HD567BE5B16144241986FDA125618BA0C"><enum>3.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="H3E0CB173F8BE4C959FEF1425DC800109"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Female</header><text>The term <term>female</term> refers to an individual who has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes eggs for fertilization.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H6BF40F363D7E4F65BA9296844D3BF875"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Male</header><text>The term <term>male</term> refers to an individual who has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H3100396AF1074DF8A8C98BEB980390A9"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Sex</header><text>The term <term>sex</term> refers to biological sex, either male or female.</text></paragraph></section></legis-body></bill>

<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code>
<congress display="yes">118th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">2d Session</session>
<legis-num display="yes">H. R. 10186</legis-num>
<current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber>
<action display="yes">
<action-date date="20241120">November 20, 2024</action-date>
<action-desc><sponsor name-id="M000194">Ms. Mace</sponsor> (for herself, <cosponsor name-id="R000619">Mr. Rulli</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="G000596">Ms. Greene of Georgia</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HGO00">Committee on Oversight and Accountability</committee-name></action-desc>
</action>
<legis-type>A BILL</legis-type>
<official-title display="yes">To prohibit individuals from accessing or using single-sex facilities on Federal property other than those corresponding to their biological sex, and for other purposes.</official-title>
</form>
<legis-body id="H8A5784A5C79045A58DA0F6FE39F60542">
<section id="HB4664670228B4867B26EC41A391348B7" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protecting Women’s Private Spaces Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="HCF5F2C77F9984EBCADB88892B81D35C6"><enum>2.</enum><header>Prohibition on the use of single-sex facilities on federal property other than those corresponding to the biological sex of an individual</header> <subsection id="H66950E05FCB84B4D8BA1FA3056DA3226"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, except as provided in subsection (c), no person may access or use a single-sex facility on Federal property, other than those corresponding to the biological sex of such person.</text></subsection>
<subsection id="H3B53692DBA29434E95C2488C0F968F36"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section—</text> <paragraph id="H0119D045EDC44338BD08547A8A38AB98"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Single-sex facility</header><text>The term <quote>single-sex facility</quote> means a space intended for the use of one biological sex (male or female), including a—</text>
<subparagraph id="H32D2CAF36C3D4A7787374F293E1954D3"><enum>(A)</enum><text>restroom;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H97D522342C1C47848A9DD0FC9C863169"><enum>(B)</enum><text>locker room; or</text></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HD89FA3E4241E4D7C9CDB7453AB8EEB93"><enum>(C)</enum><text>changing room.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDBBE755375714488A05CAE24C7A2FBF2"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Federal property</header><text>The term <quote>Federal property</quote> means any building, land, or other real property owned, leased, or occupied by any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States (including the Department of Defense and the United States Postal Service), or any other instrumentality wholly owned by the United States, or by any department or agency of the District of Columbia or any territory or possession of the United States.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H585F6532C1294E4A86FE8D212DEC8CE0"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Biological sex</header><text>The term <quote>biological sex</quote> means the biological determination as to whether an individual is male or female, as such terms are defined in this section.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H72779498D84449E3BB069BD79BD49090"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Female</header><text>The term <quote>female</quote> means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes eggs for fertilization.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H08E3E68C94EA49C29EF81EEDE2C661A5"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Male</header><text>The term <quote>male</quote> means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HE1C58085AB7F4A23A19093E52FAE2CF6"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The prohibition in subsection (a) shall not apply with respect to—</text>
<paragraph id="H00F2259416F345BA9359CDE02ECA225D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>emergency medical personnel responding to a medical emergency; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEC300C6C9F18481296A8A4E6F55FCA0C"><enum>(2)</enum><text>law enforcement officers in active pursuit of a suspect, or as part of an active investigation.</text></paragraph></subsection></section>
</legis-body>
</bill>

<dc:format>text/xml</dc:format>

<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">118th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 1064</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20230217">February 17, 2023</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="B001299">Mr. Banks</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HAS00">Committee on Armed Services</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To provide requirements related to the eligibility of transgender individuals from serving in the Armed Forces.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H8ACB90CB10A54742B0308DF346CD74A8" style="OLC"><section section-type="section-one" id="H2D1B55F175E5488190BB6FDD7143AD3C"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Ensuring Military Readiness Act of 2023</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section section-type="subsequent-section" id="H26853107D1B145C0AC4EE990D31E36D4"><enum>2.</enum><header>Limitations on military service by transgender individuals</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall prescribe regulations regarding transgender service as follows:</text><paragraph id="H825BF08510964F1F9CCE9E80E5175346"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Transgender persons with a history of diagnosis of gender dysphoria are disqualified from military service except under the following limited circumstances:</text><subparagraph id="H60EF76A395EE4240B2A1EB13EDDF32A8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Individuals may serve in the Armed Forces if they have been stable for 36 consecutive months in their biological sex prior to accession.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H2440E10014D14C2D8874FB27179B7947"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Members of the Armed Forces diagnosed with gender dysphoria after entering into service may be retained if they do not require a change of gender and remain deployable within applicable retention standards. </text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HC7F3FDB0E6734C758AF746F0A645C997"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Members of the Armed Forces serving as of the date of the enactment of this Act who have been diagnosed with gender dysphoria may continue to serve in their current gender marker in the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) and receive medically necessary treatment for gender dysphoria. Such treatment may not include gender reassignment surgery or the commencement of hormone therapy.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="HA0D9FBDFC70B429DA0A8A96D0A751156"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Transgender persons who require or have undergone gender transition are disqualified from military service.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HF577C420D1C54D5D8F0FD7E1D40D0168"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Transgender persons without a history or diagnosis of gender dysphoria, who are otherwise qualified for service and meet all physical and mental requirements, may serve in the Armed Forces in their biological sex. </text></paragraph></section></legis-body></bill>

regulations regarding service of individuals who identify as transgender as follows:</text><paragraph id="H822043D2D26B464482B4B322CA5BEC56"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Persons who identify as transgender with a history of diagnosis of gender dysphoria are disqualified from military service except under the following limited circumstances:</text><subparagraph id="H20AD2C1950644638AB57E763E6036F95"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Individuals may serve in the Armed Forces if they have been stable for 36 consecutive months in their biological sex prior to accession.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H73E9C1600037446286FAF30CDB4AFEF8"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Members of the Armed Forces diagnosed with gender dysphoria after entering into service may be retained if they do not undergo gender transition procedures and remain deployable within applicable retention standards for their biological sex. </text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H023D848E1BBA41989ABE12B916663B02"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Members of the Armed Forces serving as of the date of the enactment of this Act who have been diagnosed with gender dysphoria may continue to serve only in their biological sex, irrespective of any changes previously made to their gender marker in the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS), and receive medically necessary treatment for gender dysphoria. Such treatment may not include gender transition procedures.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H46DC6C9AA16844CA92C0218D3035504C"><enum>(2)</enum><text>Persons who identify as transgender who seek or have undergone gender transition are disqualified from military service.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HB42516986094477EAC7E173A0DC653DF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Persons who identify as transgender without a history or diagnosis of gender dysphoria, who are otherwise qualified for service and meet all physical and mental requirements, may serve in the Armed Forces in their biological sex.</text></paragraph></section><section id="H871BAD7FF08241658C4EB253C427E09C"><enum>3.</enum><header>Revised regulations regarding gender markings</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall prescribe regulations updating the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) to require the gender markers for members of the Armed Forces to match their biological sex, irrespective of any previous changes allowed. </text></section><section id="HB73AD223CD3F4865A57217E894E5CCC9"><enum>4.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="H2D97491550C04A2AB96324FBD0C24203"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Cross-Sex hormones</header><text>The term <term>cross-sex hormones</term> means testosterone or other androgens given to biological females at doses that are profoundly larger or more potent than would normally occur naturally in healthy biological females, or estrogen given to biological males at doses that are profoundly larger or more potent than would normally occur naturally in healthy biological males. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H364D48F6563B4FC297068F63FE654B6B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Gender</header><text>The term <term>gender</term> means the psychological, behavioral, social, and cultural aspects of being male or female.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HF90F6223C5A34A30805D567837970278" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Gender dysphoria</header><text>The term <term>gender dysphoria</term> means a marked incongruence between one’s experienced or expressed gender and biological sex. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H5DB8DB30B7174E03988EF8FDDCFC27DA"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Gender transition</header><text>The term <term>gender transition</term> means the process by which a person goes from identifying with and living as a gender that corresponds to his or her biological sex to identifying with and living as a gender different from his or her biological sex, and may involve social, legal, or physical changes. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="HEDABED6F4CC64D6A93867082141860AE"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Gender transition procedures</header><text>The term <term>gender transition procedures</term>—</text><subparagraph id="HEC8931CE23D446BA9AE5DBFF97ED9170"><enum>(A)</enum><text>means—</text><clause id="H1F3744558A4548AB916233C33F2C0CD6"><enum>(i)</enum><text>any medical or surgical intervention, including physician's services, inpatient and outpatient hospital services, or prescribed drugs related to gender transition, that seeks to alter or remove physical or anatomical characteristics or features that are typical for the individual’s biological sex or to instill or create physiological or anatomical characteristics that resemble a sex different from the individual’s birth sex, including medical services that provide puberty-blocking drugs, cross-sex hormones, or other mechanisms to promote the development of feminizing or masculinizing features (in the opposite sex); and</text></clause><clause id="H5360DB300826473489E371D3D3232596"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>genital or non-genital gender transition surgery performed for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition; and</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HE2E32A2EA5A74D758B93143B32B23631"><enum>(B)</enum><text>does not include—</text><clause id="HB25BF646EB8047AF811009F2B8295EA3"><enum>(i)</enum><text>services to those born with a medically-verifiable disorder of sex development, including a person with external biological sex characteristics that are irresolvably ambiguous, such as those born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or having both ovarian and testicular tissue;</text></clause><clause id="H5C22CA9EDDBC49BABD609B33B11F88D8"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>services provided when a physician has otherwise diagnosed a disorder of sexual development, in which the physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the person does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action for a biological male or biological female; or</text></clause><clause id="HADEACEA6EBE54B1D9F8CD09E5BDFB0F2"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused by or exacerbated by the performance of gender transition procedures, whether or not the gender transition procedure was performed in accordance with State and Federal law or whether or not funding for the gender transition procedure is permissible.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H1A575BF29F6142AB98AF2E468516423E"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Gender transition surgery</header><text>The term <term>gender transition surgery</term> means any medical or surgical service that seeks to surgically alter or remove healthy physical or anatomical characteristics or features that are typical for the individual’s biological sex in order to instill or create physiological or anatomical characteristics that resemble a sex different from the individual’s birth sex, including genital or non-genital gender reassignment surgery performed for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H80C3E240EBAD49099B8F814238005404"><enum>(7)</enum><header>Genital gender transition surgery</header><text>The term <term>genital gender transition surgery</term> includes surgical procedures such as penectomy, orchiectomy, vaginoplasty, clitoroplasty, or vulvoplasty for biologically male patients or hysterectomy, ovariectomy, reconstruction of the fixed part of the urethra with or without a metoidioplasty or a phalloplasty, vaginectomy, scrotoplasty, or implantation of erection or testicular prostheses for biologically female patients, when performed for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H17C830915F134DB9BDE9B5BF4E5B7826"><enum>(8)</enum><header>Non-genital gender transition surgery</header><text>The term <term>non-genital gender transition surgery</term>—</text><subparagraph id="HE7B4B8498ECA48F688A2BB643B8D2298"><enum>(A)</enum><text>includes, when performed for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition—</text><clause id="H66FD763BF2F64F54AA2B38E0F6EAA291"><enum>(i)</enum><text>surgical procedures such as augmentation mammoplasty, facial feminization surgery, liposuction, lipofilling, voice surgery, thyroid cartilage reduction, gluteal augmentation (implants or lipofilling), hair reconstruction, or various aesthetic procedures for biologically male patients; or</text></clause><clause id="HBC07821A79C84F8FBE325479F278BF8D"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>subcutaneous mastectomy, voice surgery, liposuction, lipofilling, pectoral implants or various aesthetic procedures for biologically female patients; and</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H66C702CB9B554ABFB89CCB3AE6780AA3"><enum>(B)</enum><text>does not include any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless surgery is performed, unless the procedure is for the purpose of a gender transition. </text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H90277928D8474ECB927FAAE3306CF1CD"><enum>(9)</enum><header>Puberty-Blocking drugs</header><text>The term <term>puberty-blocking drugs</term> means, when used to delay or suppress pubertal development in children for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition—</text><subparagraph id="HA6CA689B8F534427B8FCB12C8E247F85"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues or other synthetic drugs used in biological males to stop luteinizing hormone secretion and therefore testosterone secretion; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H73ECE0F467FE4E21AF8BC9BABCE4DAB9"><enum>(B)</enum><text>synthetic drugs used in biological females that stop the production of estrogen and progesterone. </text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="HC0391027C13D45F08855B5F3022FF5B3"><enum>(10)</enum><header>Sex; birth sex; biological sex</header><text>The terms <term>sex</term>, <term>birth sex,</term> and <term>biological sex</term> refer to the biological indication of male and female in the context of reproductive potential or capacity, such as sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, gonads, and non-ambiguous internal and external genitalia present at birth, without regard to an individual’s psychological, chosen, or subjective experience of gender.</text></paragraph></section></legis-body></bill>

R. 1276</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20230301">March 1, 2023</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="B001299">Mr. Banks</sponsor> (for himself, <cosponsor name-id="B001291">Mr. Babin</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="J000299">Mr. Johnson of Louisiana</cosponsor>, <cosponsor concerned</action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To protect children from medical malpractice in the form of gender transition procedures.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H9C2555E6D3264982A49A82116D02E9B7" style="OLC"><section id="H8D308743939846639FE42779984E73ED" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protect Minors from Medical Malpractice Act of 2023</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="H2D38165D4A464B23B32B014160614186"><enum>2.</enum><header>Private right of action for a gender-transition procedure performed on a minor</header><subsection id="HBC25AC2836554ED38077C2E3A695DCB8"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>A medical practitioner, in any circumstance described in subsection (c), who performs a gender-transition procedure on an individual who is less than 18 years of age shall, as described in subsection (b), be liable to the individual if injured (including any physical, psychological, emotional, or physiological harms) by such procedure, related treatment, or the after effects of the procedure or treatment.</text></subsection><subsection id="HB9D4DE5E704B41EFB52A2463E4BC5456"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Private right of action</header><text>An individual covered by subsection (a) who receives a gender-transition procedure from a medical practitioner (or a representative, including a legal guardian, on behalf of such individual) may, not later than the day that is 30 years after the date on which the individual turns 18 years of age, bring a civil action against such medical practitioner in a court of competent jurisdiction for—</text><paragraph id="H9FE0DA0BA1BE4CBB99D0D16D1CE8FBBA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>declaratory or injunctive relief;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H4FAB2CA64C0C4A188CC6F192A4E10D04"><enum>(2)</enum><text>compensatory damages;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HCB4539EF58F3407EAA522763DB999650"><enum>(3)</enum><text>punitive damages; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H0164AD49575B4864B2B454CA4B336F87"><enum>(4)</enum><text>attorney’s fees and costs.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H88C90C32991E4B159DFDFBA3C85E6575"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Circumstances</header><text>For the purposes of subsection (a), the circumstances described in this subsection are that—</text><paragraph id="HC8656BF7A795448384086932332874EC"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the medical practitioner or the individual receiving the gender-transition procedure traveled in interstate or foreign commerce, or traveled using a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HA5F9072CE1E140BF86C2065AA00F78DC"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the medical practitioner used a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H1D9BE3D71B0049CA916578A245D7CFB5"><enum>(3)</enum><text>any payment of any kind was made, directly or indirectly, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H537154598ED0440BA8E2F959C2B9BE61"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the medical practitioner transmitted in interstate or foreign commerce any communication relating to or in furtherance of the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means or in any manner, including by computer, mail, wire, or electromagnetic transmission;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H14780075E2C64F28AE498D0285D7E22A"><enum>(5)</enum><text>any instrument, item, substance, or other object that has traveled in interstate or foreign commerce was used to perform the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H14B3BA6A68414770B9AF5E297F383EFC"><enum>(6)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) occurred within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, or any territory or possession of the United States; or</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H1EEAF3505D3542F1B929D7950AD7C0F2"><enum>(7)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) otherwise occurred in or affected interstate or foreign commerce.</text></paragraph></subsection></section><section id="H6194B11F591E42DF85A6B8BD4E2D4E7C"><enum>3.</enum><header>Preserving freedom of conscience and medical judgement for medical providers</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no provision of Federal law shall require, or be construed to require, a medical practitioner to perform a gender-transition procedure.</text></section><section id="HC9AD3EF0D48B4701A5C4A0AA02EBAEBB"><enum>4.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for certain states</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any State that requires medical practitioners to perform any gender-transition procedure on an individual in the State shall be ineligible to receive any Federal funding from the Department of Health and Human Services.</text></section><section id="H938775D166BF4301AB2968A3194301A2"><enum>5.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="H25DF24C09F8F43ED906F50A6596D9103"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Biological sex</header><text>The term <term>biological sex </term> means the genetic classification of an individual as male or female, as reflected in the organization of the body of such individual for a reproductive role or capacity, such as through sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, and internal and external genitalia present at birth, without regard to the subjective sense of identity of the individual.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H7E013CA7AF454E36B393E60FD8A3A706"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Gender-transition procedure</header><subparagraph id="HFA0012AF9334493893F2AE97684D9DA0"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> means—</text><clause id="H081161A65685429BA9C0AB8D031C54DC"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of puberty-blocking drugs for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex;</text></clause><clause id="HD2A44AC1A35E4D14B0DF92B4CB27220A"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of cross-sex hormones for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex; or</text></clause><clause id="HE67C9B99F99646FBBA4FE4F34BA22649"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>a surgery to change the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex.</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H27EFA80F286F4B7FA4B84A6B75C12AE0"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> does not include—</text><clause id="H65E4B6B40CD74484A2B7F1898760CEF1"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an intervention described in subparagraph (A) that is performed on—</text><subclause id="HD8BBDE19997F43C889D0D91F28E765B3"><enum>(I)</enum><text>an individual with biological sex characteristics that are inherently ambiguous, such as those born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or having both ovarian and testicular tissue; or</text></subclause><subclause id="H356184C72058420E9B42B2DEBA2883CB"><enum>(II)</enum><text>an individual with respect to whom a physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action, for a biological male or biological female;</text></subclause></clause><clause id="HAC02EE8866034A73BEC19238DBD6EC07"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused or exacerbated by the performance of an intervention described in subparagraph (A) without regard to whether the intervention was performed in accordance with State or Federal law or whether the intervention is covered by the private right of action under section 2; or</text></clause><clause id="H838273CA964D420CA77458E5565813F4"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H0F6E64E64FCA428596D838CCEC5CDB98"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Medical practitioner</header><text>The term <term>medical practitioner</term> means a person who is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized by the laws of a State to administer health care in the ordinary course of the practice of the person’s profession.</text></paragraph></section><section id="H99058ADED0444574B8306242A3692B5F"><enum>6.</enum><header>Effective date</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act.</text></section></legis-body></bill>

<legis-type>A BILL</legis-type> 
<official-title display="yes">To amend <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/18/110">chapter 110</external-xref> of title 18, United States Code, to prohibit gender-affirming care on minors, and for other purposes.</official-title> 
</form> 
<legis-body id="H6138CFC949D34BACA82F9DE7CB780018" style="OLC"> 
<section id="HD4371DE988E94CA3A7C8B34186495F34" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protect Children’s Innocence Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <title id="H0CCE995BF4AE415691668913A112D9C2"><enum>I</enum><header>Gender-affirming care on minors prohibited</header> <section id="H85E77865CE204DC39FDF723232190134"><enum>101.</enum><header>Gender-affirming care on minors prohibited</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/18/110">Chapter 110</external-xref> of title 18, United States Code, is amended—</text> 
<paragraph id="H8F49B3CA374847CCA19851A8CC6AE6D3"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by adding at the end the following: </text> <quoted-block style="USC" id="H9CD70980F0864C53B38730F02864ADDA" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <section id="H2FD4E27E008B450F9F7F48F2CFE703DD"><enum>2260B.</enum><header>Gender-affirming care on minors</header> <subsection id="H5D5CF1E2BD52431799D0BE79214A61FB"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Whoever, in any circumstance described in subsection (e), knowingly performs any gender-affirming care on a minor is guilty of a class C felony.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H0202BF56243B4C51BCF6AB1515E6C262"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Prohibition on prosecution of person on whom intervention is performed</header><text>No person on whom the gender-affirming care under subsection (a) is performed may be arrested or prosecuted for an offense under this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H33E2C958183E4509BEE1379C928D91EC"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Civil action</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A person on whom gender-affirming care is performed under this section may bring a civil action for appropriate relief, including compensatory and punitive damages, against each person who performed the gender-affirming care.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8ED45820C52A45F6AB808AE88CA936DC"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> <paragraph id="HB433DC0B2A154725808767F0FD46908B"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Gender-affirming care</header> <subparagraph id="HF89D98F490C44BBCA30C22DE30E5BE68"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For purposes of this chapter, except as provided in subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender-affirming care</term> means, with respect to an individual, any of the following:</text> 
<clause id="H1F9F65EC9171406AB43F0DBE31DB32B7"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Performing any surgery for the purpose of changing the body of such individual to correspond to a sex that differs from their biological sex, including—</text> <subclause id="H6B17113B405E475F9C5E56509EA6CC68"><enum>(I)</enum><text>castration;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HA199D62528D94A049F86C7AC363FC383"><enum>(II)</enum><text>orchiectomy;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H05C11618A394495ABA7EADB79E003F59"><enum>(III)</enum><text>scrotoplasty;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HC8D8EA6D4F7D415EAE5D8A3AC6CB2C30"><enum>(IV)</enum><text>vasectomy;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H7A844DDF583849EC8D3BC924BF3E221E"><enum>(V)</enum><text>hysterectomy;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HC3EE907514DD419F837C1F537DA6FCA7"><enum>(VI)</enum><text>oophorectomy;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H30E7E54DAA8A4E8F816C3A8C13F5B1C6"><enum>(VII)</enum><text>ovariectomy;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HD57EC7D621FD4220990CA6A88A422EF9"><enum>(VIII)</enum><text>metoidioplasty; </text></subclause> <subclause id="H3B04D899D288467A91D30165642597D2"><enum>(IX)</enum><text>penectomy; </text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H04E0B90491E0421280AD93F91AAF9917"><enum>(X)</enum><text>phalloplasty; </text></subclause> <subclause id="H60EBACE5D04D4E0DA81CB0CDF70B9FA3"><enum>(XI)</enum><text>vaginoplasty; </text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H6D1E050274094644BE324A7FDD96BA0E"><enum>(XII)</enum><text>vaginectomy; </text></subclause> <subclause id="H48949869B3A84E43993188BAB86B17CC"><enum>(XIII)</enum><text>vulvoplasty; </text></subclause> 
<subclause id="HB2BBFC0827EA4BD3AA25C2E8013FACA8"><enum>(XIV)</enum><text>reduction thyrochondroplasty;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H88F715DB6A834A11BDFC94628EAB044B"><enum>(XV)</enum><text>chondrolaryngoplasty; and</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H1FAA08EE25A44D0AA4AC5E18F658B36A"><enum>(XVI)</enum><text>mastectomy.</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="H07E95F031FC04BEC949891EAA9EE8E3F"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>Any plastic surgery that feminizes or masculinizes the facial features for the purposes described in clause (i).</text></clause> 
<clause id="HCA95453149AE4EF5864E82FF71098725"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any placement of chest implants to create feminine breasts for the purposes described in clause (i).</text></clause> <clause id="H0A3DA48A293441B4BF353859A158219D"><enum>(iv)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any placement of fat or artificial implants in the gluteal region for the purposes described in clause (i).</text></clause> 
<clause id="HE1A823F9639C4CEFA557C2A8852B3157"><enum>(v)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Administering, supplying, prescribing, dispensing, distributing, or otherwise conveying to an individual medications for the purposes described in clause (i), including—</text> <subclause id="HD076C64B1BD4499EB7AC10272B974D64"><enum>(I)</enum><text>gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues or other puberty-blocking drugs to stop or delay normal puberty;</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H7B17F565ABAC4389BAFF71787B77D794"><enum>(II)</enum><text>testosterone or other androgens to biological females at doses that are supraphysiologic to the female sex; and</text></subclause> <subclause id="H21296292034145EB85739D7E4483C44D"><enum>(III)</enum><text>estrogen to biological males at doses that are supraphysiologic to the male sex.</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0F612985B24847D88DFF736343595C8F"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subparagraph (A) shall not apply to the following individuals:</text> <clause id="HB10A850F7FCD417D87E52294C9CA60F0"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An individual with both ovarian and testicular tissue.</text></clause> 
<clause id="HDE004BCB4CB54921ABF72D2376D341C2"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>An individual with respect to whom a physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action.</text></clause> <clause id="HABBE80ECD6FB46C9B7F2E88CDBAD8BB9"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>An individual experiencing infection, disease, injury, or disorder caused or exacerbated by previous gender transition procedures.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H3F80489420EE44039A2B8D8E47470C09"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>An individual suffering from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of a major bodily function unless the procedure is performed.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H49A7493EF0B44140ACE62E15FD94C0AE"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Biological sex</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>biological sex</term> means the indication of male or female sex by reproductive potential or capacity, sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, gonads, or internal or external genitalia present at birth.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HF11EDCC7FCCA4004B8CA7CDBC162FE09"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Minor</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>minor</term> means any person under the age of eighteen years. </text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HB4AC6BA0E19646B2B0D849F2FADA46A6" commented="no"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Circumstances described</header><text>For purposes of subsection (a), the circumstances described in this subsection are that—</text> 
<paragraph id="H62167EB8277846A49D2C8C1F7F709AC8" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the defendant or victim traveled in interstate or foreign commerce, or traveled using a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HAF46BCBF5AAC4285BE948CAB7BE21B98" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the defendant used a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H91232894407B4D71B27D6A223AAB22D2" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><text>any payment of any kind was made, directly or indirectly, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H201F52FB0F374523AEBBC7AB88034657" commented="no"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the defendant transmitted in interstate or foreign commerce any communication relating to or in furtherance of the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means or in manner, including by computer, mail, wire, or electromagnetic transmission;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HBE0218C0DD974105913DE48A979FF165" commented="no"><enum>(5)</enum><text>any instrument, item, substance, or other object that has traveled in interstate or foreign commerce was used to perform the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HEC4AF64410724CBABCC1ADA41B970FD7" commented="no"><enum>(6)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) occurred within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, or any territory or possession of the United States; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H856A8F83DCE44B308CB92C8A71C84275" commented="no"><enum>(7)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) otherwise occurred in or affected interstate or foreign commerce.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HE25421102A1447D5B0D68F6279407987"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in this section shall be construed as prohibiting provision of the medical services described in subsection (d)(1)(A) to address legitimate health issues, such as any male or female reproductive cancers, apart from changing the body to correspond to a sex that differs from one’s biological sex.</text></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>; and</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H8DF9AE5E1F28400498348779805C8832"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by amending the table of sections for such chapter by adding at the end the following:</text> <quoted-block style="USC" id="H63F5CA630D70483198DE71640F49D497" display-inline="no-display-inline"> <toc regeneration="no-regeneration"> <toc-entry level="section">2260B. Gender-affirming care on minors.</toc-entry></toc><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></paragraph></section></title> <title id="H170D152CAF8D4CBE960A5EDD7F5CB035"><enum>II</enum><header>Prohibiting Federally Funded Gender-Affirming Care</header> <section id="HF979018DA1624241A5383C28AE76FA39"><enum>201.</enum><header>Prohibiting taxpayer-funded gender-affirming care</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Title 1, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new chapter: </text> 
<quoted-block display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HF82193EFF75746E2B3867B75C6818B0F" style="USC"> 
<chapter id="H39DD071589B14FF4AC24BFEBE615D7DF"><enum>4</enum><header>Prohibiting taxpayer-funded gender-affirming care</header> 
<toc container-level="chapter-container" idref="H39DD071589B14FF4AC24BFEBE615D7DF" lowest-bolded-level="division-lowest-bolded" lowest-level="section" quoted-block="no-quoted-block" regeneration="yes-regeneration"> 
<toc-entry idref="HC0D0E4CFA1774AF580F5DE81A76B8713" level="section">301. Prohibition on funding for gender-affirming care.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="H0E2686DA27D14781A312F479DE79F137" level="section">302. Prohibition on funding for health benefits plans that cover gender-affirming care.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="H197C81D8D77744E997B6613FF5E56D41" level="section">303. Limitation on Federal facilities and employees, Federal lands and territories, and Tribal territories.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="H8C907ABA8150433BA2256CFA3BE0C0BC" level="section">304. Construction relating to separate coverage.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="H4D82C0550D30427FB13873BC1B164400" level="section">305. Construction relating to the use of non-Federal funds for health coverage.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="H18DECF912539404385BC0E009EAD230F" level="section">306. Construction relating to complications arising from gender-affirming care.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="H5D81A2C946F24EF1BB9CECBBBBA0E34E" level="section">307. Treatment of individuals born with medically verifiable disorder of sex development.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="H6EED0846721C4E5D90AD4A75F55A40CA" level="section">308. Gender-affirming care defined.</toc-entry> 
<toc-entry idref="HAA233D95114C4E959D178996542ED282" level="section">309. Rule of construction.</toc-entry></toc> 
<section id="HC0D0E4CFA1774AF580F5DE81A76B8713"><enum>301.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for gender-affirming care</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No funds authorized or appropriated by Federal law, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are authorized or appropriated by Federal law, including funds provided under titles XVIII, XIX, and XXI of the Social Security Act, shall be expended for any gender-affirming care.</text></section> <section id="H0E2686DA27D14781A312F479DE79F137"><enum>302.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for health benefits plans that cover gender-affirming care</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No funds authorized or appropriated by Federal law, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are authorized or appropriated by Federal law, shall be expended for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of gender-affirming care.</text></section> 
<section id="H197C81D8D77744E997B6613FF5E56D41"><enum>303.</enum><header>Limitation on Federal facilities and employees, Federal lands and territories, and Tribal territories</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No health care service furnished—</text> <paragraph id="H8F9A19204B7F4A4FB2E6109A337DE360"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by or in a health care facility owned or operated by the Federal Government, Federal land or territory, or a Tribal territory; or</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HB87014CDDF514118AE6A9215EE9A6AAB"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">by any physician or other individual employed by the Federal Government, Federal land or territory, or a Tribal territory to provide health care services within the scope of the physician’s or individual’s employment,</text></paragraph><continuation-text continuation-text-level="section">may include gender-affirming care. </continuation-text></section> <section id="H8C907ABA8150433BA2256CFA3BE0C0BC"><enum>304.</enum><header>Construction relating to separate coverage</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as prohibiting any individual, entity, or State or locality from purchasing separate coverage for gender-affirming care or health benefits coverage that includes gender-affirming care so long as such coverage is paid for entirely using only funds not authorized or appropriated by Federal law, federal programs, platforms, or infrastructure, such coverage does not cover any practice that would be subject to penalty under section 2260B of title 18, United States Code, and such coverage shall not be purchased using matching funds required for a federally subsidized program, including a State’s or locality’s contribution of Medicaid matching funds.</text></section> 
<section id="H4D82C0550D30427FB13873BC1B164400"><enum>305.</enum><header>Construction relating to the use of non-Federal funds for health coverage</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as restricting the ability of any non-Federal health benefits coverage provider from offering coverage for gender-affirming care, or the ability of a State or locality to contract separately with such a provider for such coverage, so long as only funds not authorized or appropriated by Federal law are used, such coverage does not cover any practice that would be subject to penalty under section 2260B of title 18, United States Code, and such coverage shall not be purchased using matching funds required for a federally subsidized program, including a State’s or locality’s contribution of Medicaid matching funds.</text></section> <section id="H18DECF912539404385BC0E009EAD230F"><enum>306.</enum><header>Construction relating to complications arising from gender-affirming care</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to apply to the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused by or exacerbated by the performance of a gender-affirming care. This rule of construction shall be applicable without regard to whether the gender-affirming care was performed in accord with Federal or State law, and without regard to whether funding for the gender-affirming care is permissible under section 307.</text></section> 
<section id="H5D81A2C946F24EF1BB9CECBBBBA0E34E"><enum>307.</enum><header>Treatment of individuals born with medically verifiable disorder of sex development</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">The limitations established in sections 301, 302, and 303 shall not apply with respect to an individual described in section 2260B(d)(1)(B) of title 18, United States Code.</text></section> <section id="H6EED0846721C4E5D90AD4A75F55A40CA"><enum>308.</enum><header>Gender-affirming care defined</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">For purposes of this chapter, the term <term>gender-affirming care</term> has the meaning given such term in section 2260B(d)(1) of title 18, United States Code.</text></section> 
<section id="HAA233D95114C4E959D178996542ED282"><enum>309.</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as prohibiting provision of the medical services described in section 2260B(d)(1)(A) of title 18, United States Code, to address any male or female reproductive cancers, apart from changing the body to correspond to a sex that differs from one’s biological sex.</text></section></chapter><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> <section id="H7992495B438C40E99A84A502FFA1048D"><enum>202.</enum><header>Amendment to table of chapters</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">The table of chapters for title 1, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new item:</text> 
<quoted-block display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5412E77CE6E24B84B34DC559911E585E" style="USC">

<title id="HECEFFDF5FF494551A0F26C2B38D86587"><enum>III</enum><header>Application under the Affordable Care Act</header> 
<section id="H2C1B94983C0C4F98BE544A344C19689E"><enum>301.</enum><header>Clarifying application of prohibition to premium credits and cost-sharing reductions under ACA</header> 
<subsection display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3D80A7EE1D7648FEA518FFD1F436A2B6"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header> 
<paragraph id="H8F8D70047BE7451383C70A41E2549431"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Disallowance of refundable credit and cost-sharing reductions for coverage under qualified health plan which provides coverage for gender-affirming care</header> 
<subparagraph id="H361999AC8A3541569B0D93D16B31E37D"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Subparagraph (A) of <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/26/36B">section 36B(c)(3)</external-xref> of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting before the period at the end the following: <quote>or any health plan that includes coverage for gender-affirming care (other than any gender-affirming care or treatment described in section 306 or 307 of title 1, United States Code)</quote>.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HD9AE43682A7B454CB7AEB055273FDE1F"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Option to purchase or offer separate coverage or plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Paragraph (3) of section 36B(c) of such Code is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:</text> 
<quoted-block display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB9E538ABB6AE4D549893325CB1A565F9" style="OLC"> 
<subparagraph id="H927E927DD3574DF7B31451A2D73CD285"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Separate coverage or plan for gender-affirming care allowed</header> 
<clause id="H7E09317F735D4C668671C544C7D9C1D4"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Option to purchase separate coverage or plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in subparagraph (A) shall be construed as prohibiting any individual from purchasing separate coverage for gender-affirming care described in such subparagraph, or a health plan that includes such gender-affirming care, so long as no credit is allowed under this section with respect to the premiums for such coverage or plan and such coverage or plan does not cover any practice that would be subject to penalty under section 2260B of title 18, United States Code.</text></clause> <clause id="HD8078F5AA2B941C582044B2E35EC9904"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Option to offer coverage or plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in subparagraph (A) shall restrict any non-Federal health insurance issuer offering a health plan from offering separate coverage for gender-affirming care described in such subparagraph, or a plan that includes such gender-affirming care, so long as premiums for such separate coverage or plan are not paid for with any amount attributable to the credit allowed under this section (or the amount of any advance payment of the credit under section 1412 of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act) and such coverage or plan does not cover any practice that would be subject to penalty under section 2260B of title 18, United States Code.</text></clause></subparagraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3FBE78E1C9A441ADB099CDD065DBB819"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Disallowance of small employer health insurance expense credit for plan which includes coverage for gender-affirming care</header><text>Subsection (h) of <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/26/45R">section 45R</external-xref> of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended—</text> <subparagraph display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H039252B567874040B23CA22521E438FC"><enum>(A)</enum><text>by striking <quote>Any term</quote> and inserting the following:</text> 
<quoted-block display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H77688ABAAFEA4CE1BE6C1A6075BF13A4" style="OLC"> 
<paragraph id="H80EA300A185C4AF0881BF8C4D34D73A9"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any term</text></paragraph><after-quoted-block>; and</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H1F850FF5140749E38C1AC4A35F44B0CB"><enum>(B)</enum><text>by adding at the end the following new paragraph:</text> 
<quoted-block display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H960B32381A5F479EA501AA3A62EB1BBA" style="OLC"> 
<paragraph id="H3B78CF0C247D4396B37B333FD3005ABB"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Exclusion of health plans including coverage for gender-affirming care</header> 
<subparagraph id="H2673DB69363B4F21A1CD52DF49EE4233"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>qualified health plan</term> does not include any health plan that includes coverage for gender-affirming care (other than any gender-affirming care or treatment described in section 306 or 307 of title 1, United States Code).</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H017EB389FA494226AA40EFD85ED9E11E"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Separate coverage or plan for gender-affirming care allowed</header> <clause display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H347C0C976A5F467C8973C5934122B136"><enum>(i)</enum><header>Option to purchase separate coverage or plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in subparagraph (A) shall be construed as prohibiting any employer from purchasing for its employees separate coverage for gender-affirming care described in such subparagraph, or a health plan that includes such gender-affirming care, so long as no credit is allowed under this section with respect to the employer contributions for such coverage or plan and such coverage does not cover any practice that would be subject to penalty under section 2260B of title 18, United States Code.</text></clause> 
<clause id="HC6EAB21E1582410E9FAAA53E48942AA1"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Option to offer coverage or plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in subparagraph (A) shall restrict any non-Federal health insurance issuer offering a health plan from offering separate coverage for gender-affirming care described in such subparagraph, or a plan that includes such gender-affirming care, so long as such separate coverage or plan is not paid for with any employer contribution eligible for the credit allowed under this section and such coverage or plan does not cover any practice that would be subject to penalty under section 2260B of title 18, United States Code.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H54A2554307454A31AAC7BDFD053B5DF2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Application to multi-State plans</header><text>Section 1334(a) of <external-xref legal-doc="public-law" parsable-cite="pl/111/148">Public Law 111–148</external-xref> (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/18054">42 U.S.C. 18054(a)</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:</text> 
<quoted-block display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H075E47E067764AD3A1EF88761A309A93" style="OLC"> 
<paragraph id="HA95E07383AB44B45BC75A48BC4F98505"><enum>(8)</enum><header>Coverage consistent with Federal policy regarding gender-affirming care</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In entering into contracts under this subsection, the Director shall ensure that no multi-State qualified health plan offered in an Exchange provides health benefits coverage for which the expenditure of Federal funds is prohibited under <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/1/4">chapter 4</external-xref> of title 1, United States Code.</text></paragraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection> <subsection id="H9EF6351EA8D24381A4CB6B5CF07EF2DF"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Effective date</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply to taxable years ending after the date that is one year after the date of enactment of this Act, but only with respect to plan years beginning after such date, and the amendment made by subsection (b) shall apply to plan years beginning after such date.</text></subsection></section></title> 
<title id="HE7D40762BAAC494F930CC79EF1CF6B16"><enum>IV</enum><header>Additional Provisions</header>

id="HD177EED91285420597C1C11E3E3D3AD4" style="OLC"><section id="HCEEF554B1CB941228B3AA5CF2442E69F" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text id="HB06029D9EFBE43A49812A7197FFC396A"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Parents are in the best position to know their own child’s needs and circumstances, and therefore they should maintain authority over all decisions that could impact the health and well-being of their children.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HDA74A618E0EC4FBA90AF78913F7E4085"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The fundamental rights of parents over the upbringing, education, and care of their children has been unequivocally established in the United States.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC5A66862263641759C126E055F34D4A4"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The fundamental right of parents to direct the education of their children, including the right to play a central role in what their children are learning shall be upheld.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HBA3B0D18B3944CDEBCB1E66C5BC137E5"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Academic success begins by embracing these fundamental parental rights in our educational institutions.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HCFE3F89B44BC4072BE54845E90E03DD8"><enum>(5)</enum><text>It is essential that parents’ voices are respected and incorporated into the development of academic curricula to ensure that their children are receiving an appropriate education.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H9EDE1381DCCB4267AEB554B0FFADB0AB"><enum>(6)</enum><text>Education must focus on academic subjects, and, without exception, should not include personal bias, personal political opinion, or indoctrination.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H146E7BD8B7C14845A8FC852B3E20126A"><enum>(7)</enum><text>A parent should have the right to opt-in review and evaluate all survey, data collection, and psychological profiling before it is administered to their students and parents should have the right to opt-out of all such testing, survey participation, or data collection.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HBE80149BC3FE40F4810EC412EBA7272B"><enum>(8)</enum><text>The traditional partnership between school employees, students, and parents by involving parents in the education of their children shall be upheld.</text></paragraph></section><section id="H6B646646C34C455E9AB8327957321C3B"><enum>3.</enum><header>State policy prohibiting certain social gender incongruent with their biological sex, without the consent of a custodial parent or legal guardian; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H3E6229781AD44B708B1D3808144F82B9"><enum>(3)</enum><text chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, gonads, and non-ambiguous internal and external genitalia present at birth, without regard to an individual’s psychological, chosen, or subjective experience of gender.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H8B409EA449F0480EBBAAC59E3403F932"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Gender</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term secondary school; or</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H64DB540ADC5C40F0A3D6C9EAD095BA1A"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">any other individual who, in the performance of pursuant to a contract with the public elementary or secondary school, State educational agency, or local educational agency.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph <distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">118th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 216</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20230109">January 9, 2023</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="V000133">Mr. Van Drew</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HED00">Committee on Education and the Workforce</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To prohibit Federal education funds from being provided to elementary schools that do not require teachers to obtain written parental consent prior to teaching lessons specifically related to gender identity, sexual orientation, or transgender studies, and for other purposes.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H90ACF74AA1784492BDED052F37B127FD" style="OLC"> 
<section id="H53FE48CD461E47B5973B8DB87E6CFA1C" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>My Child, My Choice Act of 2023</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="H3EC096638683419DABC694149F0D294C" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2.</enum><header>Written parental consent required for teaching of information related to gender identity, sexual orientation, or transgender studies</header> <subsection id="HC2ED98B168A249CAB09C6E48C61E2BEF"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">No funds under an applicable program may be provided to an elementary school determined by the Secretary of Education under subsection (c) to not be in compliance with subsection (b). </text></subsection>
<subsection id="HEE6D060A778947FBBCDF19B89EC4B244"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Written parental consent</header>
<paragraph id="HB11AD4959D3941B4AFFD9BBB10523622"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Consent required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A teacher employed by an elementary school shall, prior to teaching a lesson specifically related to gender identity, sexual orientation, or transgender studies, request written consent from the parent of each student enrolled in the class in which the teacher plans to teach such lesson. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2225289012CA4B38A2E075B2DF0B0864"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Timing</header> <subparagraph id="HCA79CD7372D84BA391695EEBD6B0D896"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A teacher shall request the written consent required under paragraph (1) not later than 30 days prior to the date on which the teacher plans to teach such lesson.</text></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HBA78ED46E7F44CD289290AE641572413"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Duration of consent</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A teacher shall request such written consent each such time the teacher plans to teach such lesson.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HFBF100E58B5E4AE58B5038364F9A8575"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Submission</header><text>A parent providing written consent shall submit such written consent to the principal of the school not later than the date described in paragraph (2)(A).</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H0EDA852162C14F479FA5A824486C4F03" commented="no"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Consent not obtained</header>
<subparagraph id="HD12BFE8EF4184E849A0357A9871EB190" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>In the case of a student whose parent does not submit written consent under paragraph (3), the school shall provide such student with an alternative period of learning or study hall.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H685973530C1246D08B64569780A636F6" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>50 percent required</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the principal does not receive written consent from the parents of at least 50 percent of the students enrolled in the class in which the teacher plans to teach such lesson, the teacher may not teach such lesson.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H4C9ACA3A193B42CA8B0A3699B48CFF23" commented="no"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Ensuring compliance</header>
<paragraph id="H7D841F75DDF84463B02D7382957DB8D9" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Students enrolled in an elementary school, parents of such students, and teachers employed by an elementary school may submit, to the Secretary, a report that such school was not in compliance with subsection (b).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3B3BFC6DB16A418C926085E402098FDD" commented="no"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Review</header><text>The Secretary shall review each such report and make a determination with respect to whether the elementary school identified in such report is in compliance with subsection (b).</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HDA30D481BB3B432C8B5BDE9F303AD2AC" commented="no"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Determination of compliance</header><text>If the Secretary makes a determination that the school is not in compliance with subsection (b), the Secretary shall—</text> <subparagraph id="H278016BEA2BF4C5CA51422FBC5E659C5" commented="no"><enum>(A)</enum><text>notify the school of such determination; </text></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HEE6D25899C9943378E07D84CC7CEB388" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>provide a period of 15 days after such notification for the school to—</text> <clause id="HB13AB75572454E6390168B10AF9DD02C"><enum>(i)</enum><text>comply with subsection (b); and</text></clause>
<clause id="H36156E600CA4493C8DF87D08C5B92BA6"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">submit to the Secretary a written confirmation of compliance with subsection (b), which shall include—</text> <subclause id="H32BA3AE36BC74E539502D84E2F62196F"><enum>(I)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">an identification of each requirement of subsection (b) with which the school was not in compliance; and</text></subclause>
<subclause id="H12713389A3CB420486EC97C827340396"><enum>(II)</enum><text>the plans and actions the school is taking to ensure that the school continues to be in such compliance; and</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H661C037B42E6464887762F32BA54BDCE"><enum>(C)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">evaluate the written confirmation submitted under subparagraph (B)(ii) and make a final determination with respect to whether the school is in compliance with subsection (b).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="HE78419C40C28424ABEB6BE3361C1FACD" commented="no"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Federal funds</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Secretary makes a final determination under subsection (c)(3)(C) that an elementary school is not in compliance with subsection (b), no funds under an applicable program may be provided to such school for the school year immediately following the school year in which such school is determined to be out of compliance.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HE232F08DB80D4F75846C453B0C5F85BD"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text>
<paragraph id="HA8DC2E6D46C64E5FA45F6FE7915FE4F6" commented="no"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Applicable program</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>applicable program</term> has the meaning given the term in section 400(c) of the General Education Provisions Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1221">20 U.S.C. 1221(c)</external-xref>). </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2FE26402A38C41B0A9DC40245E412D5A"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Biological sex</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>biological sex</term> means the biological indication of male or female in the context of reproductive potential or capacity, including sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, gonads, and nonambiguous internal and external genitalia present at birth.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF69F061B9B8E4C11A0AFC2E9F30FB64B"><enum>(3)</enum><header>ESEA terms</header><text>The terms <term>elementary school</term> and <term>parent</term> have the meanings given such terms in section 8101 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/7801">20 U.S.C. 7801</external-xref>).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H65E6783166BA407EAB2E159FA35B4C84" commented="no"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Gender identity</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>gender identity</term> means an individual’s perception of their own gender or claimed gender, regardless of the biological sex of the individual.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H1845CF00EB4D4901A8B4E398CDD53200"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Lesson</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>lesson</term> means a planned and structured period of learning. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD3BB75C260B1473D925AC27AD66BE96D"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Secretary</header><text>The term <term>Secretary</term> means the Secretary of Education. </text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H441B7ABC501C4BA9A1FF96F5255E820F"><enum>(7)</enum><header>Sexual orientation</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>sexual orientation</term> means an individual’s actual or perceived romantic, physical or sexual attraction to other individuals, or lack thereof, on the basis of gender.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBF5414EB1AB148D7A9BA4AB6CC57A851"><enum>(8)</enum><header>Transgender individual</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>transgender individual</term> means an individual whose gender identity or behavior does not conform to that typically associated with the biological sex of the individual.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6AD942F61525442DAB18DFBD56D47AA4"><enum>(9)</enum><header>Transgender studies</header><text>The term <term>transgender studies</term> means the study of transgender individuals. </text></paragraph></subsection></section> </legis-body></bill>

<legis-type>A BILL</legis-type>
<official-title display="yes">To prohibit the issuance of a passport with any gender designation other than <quote>male</quote> or <quote>female</quote>, and for other purposes.</official-title>
</form>
<legis-body id="HC3CDFCEE2C8E422A9AA808763952D8A1" style="OLC"> 
<section id="HFA5139AB17F743078024A17E926D5EB6" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Traditional Passport Act</short-title></quote> or the <quote><short-title>TPA Act</short-title></quote>. </text></section> <section id="H14091E01F5264B65B2FB0AF8C218B562" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2.</enum><header>Prohibition</header> <subsection id="H6AAFB7E3A8784033875C9505C86793E0"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of State may not issue any passport that contains a gender designation other than <quote>male</quote> or <quote>female</quote>, and may permit applicants for passports to select, between such designations, only the designation that matches the biological gender of the applicant.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HFA11D9944529400DA6BE6E46425793AA"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definition of biological gender</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">For purposes of the prohibition in this section, the biological gender of an individual means the biological classification of the individual as of the male or female sex in the context of reproductive potential or capacity, as indicated by sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, gonads, and nonambiguous internal and external genitalia present at birth.</text></subsection></section> </legis-body> </bill>

<bill bill-stage="Introduced-in-House" dms-id="HFC750A56E74846F68B11E5B5F55ECC18" public-private="public" key="H" bill-type="olc"><metadata xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">

<dc:title>118 HR 3328 IH: Protecting Children From Experimentation Act of 2023</dc:title>
<dc:publisher>U.S. House of Representatives</dc:publisher>
