<distribution-code display="yes">II</distribution-code><congress>118th CONGRESS</congress><session>2d Session</session><legis-num>S. 5424</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action><action-date date="20241204">December 4, 2024</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S411">Mr. Marshall</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSHR00">Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title>To prohibit gender transition procedures on minors, to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to impose civil penalties on persons who perform gender transition procedures on minors, and for other purposes.</official-title></form><legis-body><section id="S1" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Safeguarding The Overall Protection of Minors Act</short-title></quote> or the <quote><short-title>STOP Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="idb27c539ab4f745be8d257a37e72bac44"><enum>2.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="ida6c8900c6003426697e6ccdb45a05fd1"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Cross-sex hormones</header><text>The term <term>cross-sex hormones</term> means—</text><subparagraph id="id6ae14bd85a734597a1c95013b66301bc"><enum>(A)</enum><text>testosterone or other androgens given to females at doses that are profoundly larger or more potent than would normally occur naturally in healthy females; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id056771bcd63b48feb01ce7c2e6fb9f62" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text>estrogen given to males at doses that are profoundly larger or more potent than would normally occur naturally in healthy males.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id021e162a4aaf4de684056f5edd4a35f2"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Detransition</header><text>The term <term>detransition</term> means to halt or reverse gender transition procedures, including exploration and seeking medical advice about reversing gender transition procedures. </text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ideafd23022114496ebd253b7fc820d470"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Employer</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>employer</term> includes an individual or entity that engages a person in the performance of work as an independent contractor.</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idd02f8bf03fc547f3a7a97116373444a2"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Employment</header><text>The term <term>employment</term> includes work as an independent contractor.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="idaa6f0e4d8807479c855dfbde6d7d126f"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Female</header><text>The term <term>female</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a congenital anomaly or intentional or unintentional disruption, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes eggs for fertilization. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="idc3346cd937e448679ef694dd394b34de"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Gender</header><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id3af01b969b14407da1991e708b9f8ac3"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subject to subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender,</term> when used alone to refer to males, females, or the natural differences between males and females—</text><clause id="id1c531d528a2c42b889db569e7fd615e8"><enum>(i)</enum><text>is a synonym for sex; and</text></clause><clause id="idbcd8ae9a1133454ba6ac859669bc24ab"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>shall not be considered a synonym or short-hand expression for gender identity, experienced gender, gender expression, or gender role.</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id25aaadb00d9342d1b3480b81ecc10493"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Subparagraph (A) shall not apply when the term <term>gender</term> is used in conjunction with other words or as an adjective to modify other words, or when context or explicit definition in law indicates otherwise. </text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="ide7a8cc3a2b7f47e1abe6b0e3dfb2e4b6" commented="no"><enum>(7)</enum><header>Gender identity</header><text>The term <term>gender identity</term> does not mean sex or gender.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id1efd4e7c915f47b4bb6aec5e054b5771"><enum>(8)</enum><header>Gender transition</header><text>The term <term>gender transition</term> means the process in which an individual goes from identifying with or presenting as his or her sex to identifying with or presenting a self-proclaimed identity that does not correspond with or is different from his or her sex, and may be accompanied with social, legal, or physical changes. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="id33a80afcd82141e986eff5bd00f81c64"><enum>(9)</enum><header>Gender transition procedure</header><subparagraph id="id3c0c4d5f98bb4acb8b8c5bf385c00576"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> means any hormonal or surgical service that seeks—</text><clause id="ida39927a277884eaba461b16e4edc6ba7" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text>to alter or remove physical or anatomical characteristics or features that are typical for the individual’s sex, as determined by the sex organs, chromosomes, and endogenous profiles of the individual; or</text></clause><clause id="id978f0eb4f1e346c696b30a6899d2a498"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>to change the body of such individual to no longer correspond to their sex. </text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id8329bea07868457fb22d42c97ce104b0" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Inclusions</header><text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> includes the following:</text><clause id="idf2d2f2b9b0a143b4af54fcc161c917a1" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text>Providing, prescribing, administering, dispensing, or otherwise conveying any of the following prescription drugs that induce transient or permanent infertility:</text><subclause id="id6a6cd84b4cc44ea8b1953324238a3537" commented="no"><enum>(I)</enum><text>Puberty suppression drugs or puberty-blocking drugs to stop or delay normal puberty. </text></subclause><subclause id="id0ea296c2e70a41f480f2e516c4b4bab4" commented="no"><enum>(II)</enum><text>Cross-sex hormones, including supraphysiologic doses of testosterone to females or supraphysiologic doses of estrogen to males.</text></subclause></clause><clause id="id051efe537af945e58ea359773c3b5aab" commented="no"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>Genital gender transition surgery.</text></clause><clause id="id9504d9cc905d454db1e4e17de735fff8" commented="no"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>Non-genital gender transition surgery.</text></clause><clause id="id5bfb75a86b004bf08428fa57b5c6a15a" commented="no"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>The removal of any otherwise healthy or non-diseased body part or tissue. </text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="ida6ecdc46d20a48cc8752bcb9bd39b9eb"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Exclusions</header><text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> does not include—</text><clause id="id787efb7100074ffd9e64fb10deda7b32"><enum>(i)</enum><text>services to individuals born with a medically verifiable disorder of sex development, including an individual with external sex characteristics that are irresolvably ambiguous, such as an individual born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, an individual born with 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or an individual born having both ovarian and testicular tissue;</text></clause><clause id="id771aeaec4c0c44ea83c4fccc94a58d2c"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>services provided when a physician has otherwise diagnosed a disorder of sexual development in which the physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action for a male or female;</text></clause><clause id="id9501a8e7b56845bcb1922bcecd6378d4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused by or exacerbated by the performance of gender transition procedures, whether or not the gender transition procedure was performed in accordance with State and Federal law or whether or not funding for the gender transition procedure is permissible under this section;</text></clause><clause id="id713045bad369430f8701ab49e675bf8b"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function, unless surgery or treatment is performed for the purpose of a gender transition or for the alleviation of psychological, physical, or mental distress;</text></clause><clause id="id67955ba3109945a08721378b1555c4fb"><enum>(v)</enum><text>puberty suppression or blocking prescription drugs for the purpose of normalizing puberty for a minor experiencing precocious puberty; or</text></clause><clause id="id67705788dd0e4387afb6e8d4377f2746"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>male circumcision.</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="idd2432587098846aba144fe35d7541f03"><enum>(D)</enum><header>Genital gender transition surgery</header><text>For purposes of subparagraph (B), the term <term>genital gender transition surgery</term> means a surgical procedure performed for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition, including—</text><clause id="idc8f5af445ed94ba19695fcb15d4aa986"><enum>(i)</enum><text>for male patients, castration, a vasectomy, penectomy, orchiectomy, vaginoplasty, clitoroplasty, and vulvoplasty; and</text></clause><clause id="id39b79d31182c421aac1eeb4820fd7d33"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>for female patients, a mastectomy, hysterectomy/ovariectomy, reconstruction of the fixed part of the urethra with or without a metoidioplasty or a phalloplasty, vaginectomy, scrotoplasty, and implantation of erection or testicular prostheses.</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id36864ee3ab594214bf157cc4eced9f02"><enum>(E)</enum><header>Non-genital gender transition surgery</header><text>For purposes of subparagraph (B), the term <term>non-genital gender transition surgery</term> means a surgical procedure performed for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition, including—</text><clause id="idc55d00b258dd4ea986107435faa7eb53"><enum>(i)</enum><text>for male patients, augmentation mammoplasty, facial feminization surgery, liposuction, lipofilling, voice surgery, thyroid cartilage reduction, gluteal augmentation (implants/lipofilling), hair reconstruction, and various aesthetic procedures; and</text></clause><clause id="id9425c68cda704ee8a9b1bf945a58c350"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>for female patients, subcutaneous mastectomy, voice surgery, liposuction, lipofilling, pectoral implants, and various aesthetic procedures. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="ida3a97ada265d4a51b25710395071cae4"><enum>(10)</enum><header>Male</header><text>The term <term>male</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a congenital anomaly or intentional or unintentional disruption, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id23b39fb92b354ffe99181b79999bfad1"><enum>(11)</enum><header>Minor</header><text>The term <term>minor</term> means an individual under the age of 18. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="ide2f9eda06a864d47a4ca0cb1412882c7"><enum>(12)</enum><header>Puberty-blocking drugs</header><text>The term <term>puberty-blocking drugs</term> means—</text><subparagraph id="idb797ea2b026549378dbe4a3eff91772b"><enum>(A)</enum><text>gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues or other synthetic drugs used in males to stop luteinizing hormone secretion and therefore testosterone secretion; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id2cf092135e724f69a8f8560981089389" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text>synthetic drugs used in females that stop the production of estrogen and progesterone, when used to delay or suppress pubertal development in children for the purpose of assisting an individual with a gender transition. </text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id1dec96adb5ab4d848266f13d9f5dc221"><enum>(13)</enum><header>Secretary</header><text>The term <term>Secretary</term> means the Secretary of Health and Human Services.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="idefdc7474692943ab9ba44ef41f8d548c" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(14)</enum><header>Sex</header><text>The term <term>sex</term>, when referring to an individual’s sex, means to refer to either male or female, as biologically determined and defined in this section. </text></paragraph></section><section id="id011ecbb6b566414fa96c19a082afdecb"><enum>3.</enum><header>Gender transition procedures on minors</header><subsection id="id3072a471c65d4b159834d750e86ddcdc"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Prohibition</header><paragraph id="id6ea2d14b012f44fa8c162e7f3f0b0e39"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>No person may, in any circumstance described in paragraph (2), knowingly perform, attempt to perform, conspire to perform, or provide a referral for any gender transition procedure on a minor. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="id29b4460a6f144911a90cbd0445756e35"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Circumstances described</header><text>A circumstance referred to in paragraph (1) is any the following:</text><subparagraph id="id0d296330196a4eaea5240f56508574ff"><enum>(A)</enum><text>The person, or the minor on whom the gender transition procedure was performed, attempted to be performed, conspired to be performed, or for whom a referral for any gender transition procedure was provided, traveled in interstate or foreign commerce, or traveled using a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in paragraph (1).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id0e15012ff75a4649ace40cb61a879a84"><enum>(B)</enum><text>The person, or the minor on whom the gender transition procedure was performed, attempted to be performed, conspired to be performed, or for whom a referral for any gender transition procedure was provided, used a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in paragraph (1). </text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="idd9813624c8944c16879b06a1e9f838bd"><enum>(C)</enum><text>A payment of any kind was made, directly or indirectly, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in paragraph (1), using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="iddd79b942f6884c25b18d52b9541c457d"><enum>(D)</enum><text>The person, or the minor on whom the gender transition procedure was performed, attempted to be performed, conspired to be performed, or for whom a referral for any gender transition procedure was provided, transmitted in interstate or foreign commerce any communication relating to or in furtherance of the conduct described in paragraph (1) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means or in manner, including by computer, mail, wire, or electromagnetic transmission. </text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id54141b36c12c411ba45fec4571da42e3"><enum>(E)</enum><text>Any instrument, item, substance, or other object that has traveled in interstate or foreign commerce was used to perform the conduct described in paragraph (1).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id4fa90c2dbdf44fcc8ec6eedfbd7eb03e"><enum>(F)</enum><text>The conduct described in paragraph (1) occurred within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States or any territory or possession of the United States.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="idba0b4e3c102d4681b645b5e93cf50b0c" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(G)</enum><text>The conduct described in paragraph (1) otherwise occurred in or affected interstate or foreign commerce. </text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id94c505b776e94ed0a8c4e7ba010cd8a9"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Knowingly</header><text>For purposes of paragraph (1), a person acts knowingly when—</text><subparagraph id="id63b80bcc58304561874b7d989437b174"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the person has actual knowledge of the facts giving rise to the violation; or</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="idc6980421372348068ae55a59c20fdad7" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a reasonable person acting in the circumstances and exercising reasonable care would have that knowledge.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id1dd310cf05eb4dcfb0e93116410ba472"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Application to employers</header><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id8ce4133de12c433fadc440d04cb9ecfe"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A violation of paragraph (1) by a person acting in the scope of their employment for an employer shall also be considered a violation of such paragraph by such employer.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id279ce2c4e805434fb517aab3b4a583e1"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Liability</header><text>In the case of a violation described in subparagraph (A), the person and the employer shall be jointly and severally liable for any civil penalty under subsection (b) and any private right of action under subsection (c).</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id0a3d8d202e5843869a09f4218eca19d2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Civil penalties</header><paragraph id="id8d6cb1975c3447b0945b76287d355cfb"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary may impose a civil penalty on any person upon making a determination, after written notice and an opportunity for a hearing, that the person has violated a requirement of subsection (a)(1). </text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id375634a701024c3abb3548b7b9bc53ab"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Amount of civil penalties</header><subparagraph id="id297c14fb1a4d440790d425a24a0c2343"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The amount of a civil penalty under paragraph (1) shall be not less than $100,000 for each violation.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="idcfdd7f70a7174cad9e6b112adef36a74"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Penalty considerations</header><text>In determining the amount of a civil penalty under this subsection, the Secretary shall consider—</text><clause id="id56934a53313148a3b3175db9dae284fb"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the nature, circumstances, extent, and gravity of the violation;</text></clause><clause id="id572115c9046542ef97fa3be258f6ee73"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>with respect to the violator, the degree of culpability, any history of prior violations, and any effect on the ability to continue to do business; and</text></clause><clause id="idc00c3da7f4ff473ba87bc3ceca971cfa" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>other matters that justice requires. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id687a13f12bce41798a0efa7fd56f5920"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Civil action to collect</header><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idf792875412464b158c57c0002cb7cdcb"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Attorney General may bring a civil action in an appropriate district court of the United States to collect a civil penalty under this subsection and any accrued interest on the civil penalty as assessed by the Secretary. In such a civil action, the amount and appropriateness of the civil penalty shall not be subject to review.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id908e9f5e546a4d49808cfcc4577136c6" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Compromise</header><text>The Secretary may compromise the amount of a civil penalty imposed under this subsection before referral to the Attorney General under subparagraph (A), on the condition that such amount shall be not less than $100,000.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id14b511e711ee456b803ded7e672f9aaf"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Liability for procedures required as a matter of standard practice</header><text>It shall not be a defense in a hearing under this subsection that gender transition procedures are required as a matter of standard practice. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="id2a61c46c9dec49b7b2a212dbc6d1131a"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Prohibition on imposition of civil penalty on a person on whom procedures are performed</header><text>No person on whom a gender transition procedure is performed in violation of subsection (a)(1), and no parent, guardian, or caretaker of such a person, may be held liable for a civil penalty under this subsection.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id95913eb8694444d98bbf6f1b8ed54838" commented="no"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Depositing amounts collected</header><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id1025ded542f34d96935afab44c933a09"><enum>(A)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text>Amounts collected under this subsection shall be deposited in the fund established under subparagraph (B).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id127ada7779024a648d38cf5103c9b278"><enum>(B)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Establishment of Fund</header><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id252ca8f915024454bbef5009cc43d764"><enum>(i)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">There is established in the Treasury of the United States a fund, to be known as the <quote>Justice for Victims Fund</quote>, which shall consist of amounts deposited in the fund pursuant to subparagraph (A). </text></clause><clause id="id9f2889d013fc467c82a10837a4097312" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Availability of funds</header><text>Amounts in the fund established under clause (i) shall be made available for expenditure for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter, without further appropriation or fiscal year limitation for expenditure by the Secretary to carry out section 4. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="id5538c9113f634d8c8b515d9e61ea0d7a"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Private civil action</header><text>A person on whom a gender transition procedure is performed in violation of subsection (a)(1), or the parent, guardian, or caretaker of such a person if such person is a minor, may bring a civil action in an appropriate district court of the United States for appropriate relief against any person in violation of subsection (a)(1). </text></subsection><subsection id="id30bc8f2cdb4548b083b94fe5f946c734"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Penalty for obstruction of investigations</header><paragraph id="id68e3034a9be240059aa27f5eae88bba7"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Secretary may impose a civil penalty on any person who obstructs or prevents the Secretary from carrying out an investigation into an alleged violation of subsection (a)(1).</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id2860d34b81c64b18a60d9180f879055f"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Definition of obstruct</header><text>In this subsection, the term <term>obstruct</term> means to take an action that was known, or reasonably should have been known, to prevent, hinder, or impede an investigation.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="ided4caffcbb104dc98362a8907842c967"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Severability</header><text>If any provision of this Act, or the application of such provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be or made invalid, the remainder of this Act, and the application of the provision to any other person or circumstance, shall not be affected. </text></subsection></section><section id="id2ff1732b97684383a2fd4e2c7724334b"><enum>4.</enum><header>Opening avenues for victims</header><subsection id="id451f9206826147e38234d9514d2c8b50"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Purpose</header><text>The purpose of this section is to support, encourage, and assist individuals in their efforts to reverse gender transition procedures.</text></subsection><subsection id="id3e7b2a43f08a4e29891360893b8609f3"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Establishment of grant program</header><text>The Secretary shall establish a grant program under which the Secretary shall award grants to eligible entities to carry out the activities described in subsection (d).</text></subsection><subsection id="ida62dbd58dca84d2587b3e87e528f7785"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Eligibility</header><paragraph id="idadc0b47f511545c1b0ca7c0bd342e313"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Eligible entities</header><text>To be eligible for a grant under this section, an entity shall—</text><subparagraph id="id5d8d6e0c4d554eaab59744817c872f9f"><enum>(A)</enum><text>be a nonprofit organization;</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="ida9fe715bb7a74ebf8517ab614f95654f"><enum>(B)</enum><text>support, encourage, and assist individuals in their efforts to reverse gender transition procedures;</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id16878bcce6824546864db0c99a1842a5"><enum>(C)</enum><text>agree to be subject to such monitoring and review as the Secretary may require under subsection (g);</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="idfc634e9ff7af41678c6f2ed833b909ad"><enum>(D)</enum><text>agree to not charge individuals for services provided through the grant;</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id3a0c3693c5ad4edeaf60c1fd1d3654fd"><enum>(E)</enum><text>provide each individual counseled through the grant with accurate information on the proper medical procedures to reverse gender transition procedures; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id033c2a83669b4a0094b9d618bfe6d895"><enum>(F)</enum><text>have a privacy policy and procedures in place to ensure that—</text><clause id="idf9ddd66c68e949a680ab938ebcd56809"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the name, address, telephone number, or any other information that might identify any individual seeking services supported through the grant is not made public or shared with any other entity without the written consent of the individual; and </text></clause><clause id="id8e759396ecc849948b5b7038dbc17180"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the grantee adheres to requirements comparable to those applicable under the HIPAA privacy regulation (as defined in section 1180(b)(3) of the Social Security Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1320d-9">42 U.S.C. 1320d–9(b)(3)</external-xref>)) to covered entities (as defined for purposes of such regulation).</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id88ee34745c22478fa22d956200913edd"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Ineligible entities</header><text>An entity shall be ineligible to receive a grant under this section if the entity or any affiliate, subsidiary, successor, or clinic thereof—</text><subparagraph id="id9130310954d74779af1852ccd28d70e5"><enum>(A)</enum><text>performs, induces, refers for, or counsels in favor of gender transition procedures; or</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id21ed4beb6b094da196f04c4b2ba8a132"><enum>(B)</enum><text>provides financial support to any other entity that conducts any activity described in subparagraph (A).</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id68a05398ecfb452ca88aac77f38f8258"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Financial records</header><text>As a condition on receipt of a grant under this section, an eligible entity shall agree to maintain and make available to the Secretary records, including financial records, that demonstrate that the entity satisfies the requirements of paragraph (1) and is not ineligible by operation of paragraph (2).</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="id79a5cd32cffd4119bdc180841a8a4838"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Use of grant funds</header><paragraph id="id433ddba4bc684528802f72c8873085a7"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Required information and referral</header><text>For the purpose described in subsection (a), an eligible entity receiving a grant under this section shall use the grant funds to provide to individuals who are exploring detransition information on, and referral to, each of the following services:</text><subparagraph id="ida491841b02814380be1cc20b902942f8"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Medical advice and care.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id4509fa3fa22944059e363f2129c32739"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Nutritional services.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id7dd259e57aeb410ba448e831e2796aca"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Education and employment assistance, including services that support the continuation and completion of high school.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id1594875cb70a4f4589b81c3b7313fd3e"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Parenting education and support services.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id82c2aafa872e4018bea0cf6a0ce06845"><enum>(E)</enum><text>Voluntary substance abuse counseling and treatment.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id7e9dc50d7a9141b3b66b55995518f7e4"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Permissible direct provision of services</header><text>For the purpose described in subsection (a), in addition to using grant funds under this section as described in paragraph (1), an eligible entity receiving a grant under this section may use the grant funds for the direct provision of one or more services described in paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="idc4b9ce994ebf485484c17ffd0bd17edc"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Prohibited uses of funds</header><text>None of the funds made available under this section shall be used for gender transition procedures.</text></subsection><subsection id="id71aab9a38f7d4b798772908590aae177"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Consideration</header><text>In selecting the recipients of grants under this section, the Secretary shall consider each applicant’s demonstrated capacity in providing services to assist individuals who are exploring and seeking medical advice in their efforts to reverse gender transition procedures.</text></subsection><subsection id="idc63cf4377a484a0b8bb6cc1dc41acca3"><enum>(g)</enum><header>Monitoring and review</header><text>The Secretary shall—</text><paragraph id="id26dc28e78f2b4798b9cfbbb274466fc5"><enum>(1)</enum><text>monitor and review each program funded through a grant under this section to ensure that the grantee carefully adheres to—</text><subparagraph id="idd55947b5418a44c5b5da2cef2294379e"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the purpose described in subsection (a); and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id59461b6c021d496082d7e96a801e1f94"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the requirements of this section; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="id630d52eaccee41bda7981ed14ee699d7"><enum>(2)</enum><text>cease to fund a program under this section if the grantee fails to adhere to such purpose and requirements.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></legis-body></bill>

<dc:title>118 S635 IS: Protecting Minors from Medical Malpractice Act of 2023</dc:title>

<distribution-code display="yes">II</distribution-code><congress>118th CONGRESS</congress><session>1st Session</session><legis-num>S. 635</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action><action-date date="20230302">March 2, 2023</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S374">Mr. Cotton</sponsor> (for himself, <cosponsor name-id="S397">Mr. Braun</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S355">Mr. Cruz</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S375">Mr. Daines</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S378">Mr. Lankford</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S419">Mr. Mullin</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S350">Mr. Rubio</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="S421">Mr. Vance</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSJU00">Committee on the Judiciary</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title>To protect children from medical malpractice in the form of gender transition procedures.</official-title></form><legis-body display-enacting-clause="yes-display-enacting-clause"><section section-type="section-one" id="S1"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protecting Minors from Medical Malpractice Act of 2023</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="id485D8C8BF32746DAA7C880062F8856A1"><enum>2.</enum><header>Private right of action for a gender-transition procedure performed on a minor</header><subsection id="id20fdb775a39d4259bddbb91c15e65368"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>A medical practitioner, in any circumstance described in subsection (c), who performs a gender-transition procedure on an individual who is less than 18 years of age shall, as described in subsection (b), be liable to the individual if injured (including any physical, psychological, emotional, or physiological harms) by such procedure, related treatment, or the aftereffects of the procedure or treatment.</text></subsection><subsection id="id6940121aeffe47c5a8f86af59af2ed6b"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Private right of action</header><text>An individual covered by subsection (a) who receives a gender-transition procedure from a medical practitioner (or a representative, including a legal guardian, on behalf of such individual) may, not later than the day that is 30 years after the date on which the individual turns 18 years of age, bring a civil action against such medical practitioner in a court of competent jurisdiction for—</text><paragraph id="id01D37B9E8A7D424898A8498CBA8560D6"><enum>(1)</enum><text>declaratory or injunctive relief; </text></paragraph><paragraph id="idD29DF47597E44EEC85851B2B856D35D8"><enum>(2)</enum><text>compensatory damages;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id68D80CC376574457AA6B1CFB90A67100"><enum>(3)</enum><text>punitive damages; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id8A99349D16344BE79B327924A8C9E745"><enum>(4)</enum><text>attorney’s fees and costs.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="id86ea96df8e1d40259ce00342cf43fbe7"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Circumstances</header><text>For the purposes of subsection (a), the circumstances described in this subsection are that—</text><paragraph id="id74be3a36ace3459d8401b0d83e975aa8"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the medical practitioner or the individual receiving the gender-transition procedure traveled in interstate or foreign commerce, or traveled using a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a); </text></paragraph><paragraph id="id36e0aea52c4040439c0645fa0e8eae6f"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the medical practitioner used a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id6c20f0aa280d45f99f8846b9a877625c"><enum>(3)</enum><text>any payment of any kind was made, directly or indirectly, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id22bf8be8c72d4c6895dca9b7e0b5bfb2"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the medical practitioner transmitted in interstate or foreign commerce any communication relating to or in furtherance of the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means or in any manner, including by computer, mail, wire, or electromagnetic transmission;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="idee12c6a0a1924c7686b02612a1d18dd5"><enum>(5)</enum><text>any instrument, item, substance, or other object that has traveled in interstate or foreign commerce was used to perform the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id99b474a0c7d641e98b9b11371024fef8"><enum>(6)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) occurred within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, or any territory or possession of the United States; or</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ida11f5a96fa8543e8a825ea7fcc4ae14d"><enum>(7)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) otherwise occurred in or affected interstate or foreign commerce. </text></paragraph></subsection></section><section id="id158a7e039f8e4b51bd128c08f9854599"><enum>3.</enum><header>Preserving freedom of conscience and medical judgement for medical providers</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no provision of Federal law shall require, or be construed to require, a medical practitioner to perform a gender-transition procedure. </text></section><section id="idA12FD8ED4F6942A4A9FE5C69BBE9A64D"><enum>4.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for certain States</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any State that requires medical practitioners to perform any gender-transition procedure on an individual in the State shall be ineligible to receive any Federal funding from the Department of Health and Human Services. </text></section><section id="id34148F950343488B9FAE88D2B19B16B1"><enum>5.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="idcb2b7dd6d83e4231bd34de73b85efa83"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Biological sex</header><text>The term <term>biological sex</term> means the genetic classification of an individual as male or female, as reflected in the organization of the body of such individual for a reproductive role or capacity, such as through sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, and internal and external genitalia present at birth, without regard to the subjective sense of identity of the individual.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id4a713fe847e94d008d4f273d2584799a"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Gender-transition procedure</header><subparagraph id="id2f15d828e5bc46babc41ecc24d8f7cc7"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> means—</text><clause id="idd1d2df915af84a9dbd8de9d8e4c0ab3b"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of puberty-blocking drugs for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual's biological sex;</text></clause><clause id="id1b04d6b632714650a3e5b10ebdd5f1ff"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of cross-sex hormones for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex; or</text></clause><clause id="id24383c87a22441e1a6a4badcdd26d110"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>a surgery to change the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex. </text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id580f7edc518d467786c8459490f3bc1d"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> does not include— </text><clause id="id14127F619246495781A84D5D557BEA1A"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an intervention described in subparagraph (A) that is performed on—</text><subclause id="idAE793661CC0D4A8F9CB321D11D21F03C"><enum>(I)</enum><text>an individual with biological sex characteristics that are inherently ambiguous, such as those born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or having both ovarian and testicular tissue; or</text></subclause><subclause id="idE75844D2D6684793B79CBF3B59F49800"><enum>(II)</enum><text>an individual with respect to whom a physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action, for a biological male or biological female;</text></subclause></clause><clause commented="no" id="id0CD81E68602F4BD8BDF92DF53265B75C"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused or exacerbated by the performance of an intervention described in subparagraph (A) without regard to whether the intervention was performed in accordance with State or Federal law or whether the intervention is covered by the private right of action under section 2; or</text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idA850FF5304C848199CDFF1A1F3E31F39"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idA2D6CB19C0E94B6F8847F99CAE994C47"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Medical practitioner</header><text>The term <term>medical practitioner</term> means a person who is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized by the laws of a State to administer health care in the ordinary course of the practice of the person’s profession.</text></paragraph></section><section id="id31761657b89049cb949d34f643d3b578"><enum>6.</enum><header>Effective date</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act. </text></section></legis-body></bill>

<resolution public-private="public" resolution-stage="Introduced-in-Senate" resolution-type="senate-resolution" star-print="no-star-print" slc-id="S1-ELL23413-8LN-YN-NCT"><metadata xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">

<dc:title>118 SRES 267 IS: Supporting the designation of the week of June 18 through June 24, 2023, as “National Women’s Sports Week” to celebrate the anniversary of the enactment of title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 and the growth of women’s sports.</dc:title>
<dc:publisher>U.S. Senate</dc:publisher>
<dc:date>2023-06-22</dc:date>
<dc:format>text/xml</dc:format>
<dc:language>EN</dc:language>
<dc:rights>Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.</dc:rights>

</metadata>
<form>
<distribution-code display="yes">III</distribution-code><congress display="yes">118th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num>S. RES. 267</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20230622">June 22, 2023</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S376">Ms. Ernst</sponsor> (for herself, <cosponsor name-id="S318">Mr. Wicker</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S395">Mrs. Hyde-Smith</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S293">Mr. Graham</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S378">Mr. Lankford</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S404">Mr. Scott of Florida</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S396">Mrs. Blackburn</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S398">Mr. Cramer</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S350">Mr. Rubio</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S416">Mrs. Britt</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S397">Mr. Braun</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="S355">Mr. Cruz</cosponsor>) submitted the following resolution; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSCM00">Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>RESOLUTION</legis-type><official-title display="yes">Supporting the designation of the week of June 18 through June 24, 2023, as <quote>National Women’s Sports Week</quote> to celebrate the anniversary of the enactment of title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 and the growth of women’s sports.</official-title></form><preamble><whereas><text>Whereas title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1681">20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.</external-xref>) (referred to in this preamble as <quote>title IX</quote>) was enacted on June 23, 1972, to end unjust sex discrimination in education, including in athletics;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas title IX transformed sports by guaranteeing women and girls the right to equal athletic opportunities;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas the purposes and benefits of title IX are negated for women whenever men claiming to be women are granted access to female sports;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas title IX has resulted in a 545-percent increase in the percentage of women playing college sports and a 990-percent increase in the percentage of women playing high school sports;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas athletic participation helps women and girls develop confidence, initiative, and leadership skills;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas policies allowing for the inclusion of men in women’s sports have no basis in biological fact or valid medical research;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas providing equal athletic opportunities in sports to women is impossible without single-sex teams and competitions reserved exclusively for female athletes;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas, without separate single-sex teams and competitions based on biological sex for men and women, men will dominate competitive sports where size, strength, and speed are factors, depriving female athletes of athletic and academic opportunities;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas the biological differences between men and women have led to women being injured by men competing in women’s sports;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas, since 2017, men have won at least 24 professional women’s id="ide138e2f2316e4c28b74da94e06895c11"><enum>(1)</enum><text>observing <quote>National Women’s Sports Week</quote> as the week of June 18 through June 24, 2023, to recognize—</text><subparagraph id="id3d6909b5a103466ea5be165c9f28dd7a"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the incredible expansion of opportunities for female athletes since the enactment of title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 <resolution resolution-type="senate-resolution" star-print="no-star-print" public-private="public" resolution-stage="Introduced-in-Senate" slc-id="S1-LIP23117-MH6-RM-72W"><metadata xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">
<dublinCore>
<dc:title>118 SRES 53 IS: Establishing a Women’s Bill of Rights to reaffirm legal protections afforded to women under Federal law.</dc:title>
<dc:publisher>U.S. Senate</dc:publisher>
<dc:date>2023-02-09</dc:date>
<dc:format>text/xml</dc:format>
<dc:language>EN</dc:language>
<dc:rights>Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.</dc:rights>
</dublinCore>

<form>
<distribution-code display="yes">III</distribution-code><congress display="yes">118th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num>S. RES. 53</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20230209">February 9, 2023</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S395">Mrs. Hyde-Smith</sponsor> (for herself, <cosponsor name-id="S350">Mr. Rubio</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S355">Mr. Cruz</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S410">Ms. Lummis</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S346">Mr. Lee</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="S416">Mrs. Britt</cosponsor>) submitted the following resolution; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSJU00">Committee on the Judiciary</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>RESOLUTION</legis-type><official-title display="yes">Establishing a Women’s Bill of Rights to reaffirm legal protections afforded to women under Federal law.</official-title></form><preamble><whereas><text>Whereas males and females possess unique and immutable biological differences that manifest prior to birth and increase as they age and experience puberty;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas biological differences between the sexes mean that only females may get pregnant, give birth, and breastfeed children;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas biological differences between the sexes mean that males are, on average, larger in size and possess greater body strength than females;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas biological differences between the sexes can expose females to more harm than males from specific forms of violence, including sexual violence;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas women have achieved inspirational and significant accomplishments in education, athletics, and employment; and</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas recent misguided court rulings related to the definition of <quote>sex</quote> have led to endangerment of spaces and resources dedicated to women, thereby necessitating clarification of certain terms: Now, therefore, be it</text></whereas></preamble><resolution-body style="OLC" id="H42C4B47C4DAB44BC9C2C4CC87F3E855D"><section display-inline="yes-display-inline" section-type="undesignated-section" id="H2E2FB4B213214F4B87B7CFF43C3B1981"><text>That the Senate reaffirms that—</text><paragraph id="H77C2E1DE32F54B569E992CC7091ABB6C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>for the purposes of Federal law, the <quote>sex</quote> of an individual means his or her biological sex (either male or female) at birth;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC3F5FBCEE2C74BFCBD472B96B0FBFB97"><enum>(2)</enum><text>for the purposes of Federal laws addressing sex, the terms <quote>woman</quote> and <quote>girl</quote> refer to human females, and the terms <quote>man</quote> and <quote>boy</quote> refer to human males;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HBF55285C08234308A3AAFBCB7151672E"><enum>(3)</enum><text>for the purposes of Federal law, the word <quote>mother</quote> means a parent of the female sex and <quote>father</quote> is defined as a parent of the male sex;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H79128797E1A241028EEAE35B9B7E32C3"><enum>(4)</enum><text>there are important reasons to distinguish between the sexes with respect to athletics, prisons, domestic violence shelters, restrooms, and other areas, particularly where biology, safety, and privacy are implicated;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HD1CD20DAD50744C1AC8A3530BFEA0DCD"><enum>(5)</enum><text>policies and laws that distinguish between the sexes are subject to intermediate constitutional scrutiny and permitted when they serve an important governmental objective and are substantially related to achieving that objective; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC0F0F00D4C6C45748783ABA94D1ECD81"><enum>(6)</enum><text>for the purposes of complying with Federal laws that require State and local government agencies to collect or report data disaggregated by sex, such as Federal antidiscrimination laws, agencies are required to base such data on the biological sex of individuals at birth.</text></paragraph></section></resolution-body></resolution>

employee.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H3ED8E30BE3CC4DC3B3C69F012965F0BD"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>For purposes of this subsection—</text><subparagraph id="HC9B19C49A3244E03AA53782C9C706B53"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Gender transition procedure</header><clause id="H7BB4728BFDEF4670BFC36187EBAEED8A"><enum>(i)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> means any medical or surgical service which seeks to alter or remove physiological or anatomical characteristics or features which are typical for the individual's biological sex, or to instill or create physiological or anatomical characteristics which resemble a sex different from the individual's birth sex, for the purpose of gender transition, including—</text><subclause id="HAB80A3D52210441D987C4A35CB61C1A3"><enum>(I)</enum><text>physician's services and inpatient and outpatient hospital services, including gender transition surgery, id="H9E244E19A2A84089A2F9DDECF5F3FB39"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Exceptions</header><text>Such term does not include—</text><subclause id="HA20514EC21924246B39F58746423423E"><enum>(I)</enum><text>services for treatment of a medically verifiable disorder of sex development, including—</text><item sexual development, with respect to which the physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone any infection, injury, disease, or disorder caused or exacerbated by the performance of any gender transition procedure, whether or not the gender transition procedure was performed in accordance with State and Federal law or whether not a deduction for expenses in connection with the gender transition procedure is allowable under this chapter.</text></subclause></clause><clause id="HE40AC7D6543D4615828AFB3E92D9EF34"><enum>(iii)</enum><header>Gender</header><text>The term <term>gender</term> means the psychological, behavioral, social, and cultural aspects of being male or female.</text></clause><clause id="H4F4DD9AE130C40B6BEFC8E5DD57FCDC5"><enum>(iv)</enum><header>Gender transition</header><text>The term <term>gender transition</term> means the process in which an individual goes from identifying with and living as a gender that corresponds to his or her biological sex to identifying with and living as a gender different from his or her biological sex, and may involve social, legal, or physical changes. </text></clause><clause id="H93F921F39FB04E5493A34397397868E3"><enum>(v)</enum><header>Gender transition surgery</header><subclause id="H3269B714A77245A98B4366CB5FC1B4EA"><enum>(II)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>Such term does not include any service performed because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, <section id="HED8BC3B8B6684320BD039EE50A31AFEB" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Eliminate DEI in Colleges Act</short-title></quote>. </text></section> <section id="H86923049FCA1414187432C002A005823"><enum>2.</enum><header>Prohibition on Federal funding for institutions of higher education that carry out diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Part B of title I of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1011">20 U.S.C. 1011 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following:</text>
<quoted-block style="OLC" id="HB33917FC41B246D5ABEBEE2DF96AF1E5" display-inline="no-display-inline">
<section id="HB010C46EF52F442B9C108EDE21E72596"><enum>124.</enum><header>Prohibition on diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives</header>
<subsection id="HB629AF9BA76149C7AC2AABE5306E2F18"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Restriction on eligibility</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no institution of higher education shall be eligible to receive funds or any other form of financial assistance under any Federal program, including participation in any federally funded or guaranteed student loan program, unless the institution certifies to the Secretary that the institution—</text> <paragraph id="H7B1F2C284B624017A63233A8DBA0ED74"><enum>(1)</enum><text>does not and will not carry out any program, project, initiative, or other activity the primary purpose of which is to advocate, promote, or otherwise support diversity, equity, and inclusion; and</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H7E5C578661C94CB8BD022932F03CC322"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">does not and will not maintain any office or other entity within the institution to advocate, promote, or otherwise support diversity, equity, and inclusion.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H9FD165116E9449F697FC19912607EFFD"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Information availability</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each institution of higher education that provides the certification required by subsection (a) shall, upon request, make available to the Secretary any information needed by the Secretary to verify the truth and accuracy of the certification.</text></subsection>
<subsection id="H3DCD7882CD55425C88299B86EC66EF86"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Regulations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary shall publish regulations to implement and enforce the provisions of this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H329F4F01B6DA42D2ABB4261B4C0D06AD"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Appeals</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Upon determination by the Secretary to terminate financial assistance to any institution of higher education under this section, the institution may file an appeal with an administrative law judge before the expiration of the 30-day period beginning on the date such institution is notified of the decision to terminate financial assistance under this section. Such judge shall hold a hearing with respect to such termination of assistance before the expiration of the 45-day period beginning on the date that such appeal is filed. Such judge may extend such 45-day period upon a motion by the institution concerned. The decision of the judge with respect to such termination shall be considered to be a final agency action.</text></subsection>
<subsection id="H0CADD3ADA7A54A739FA92E54A81863F5"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Definition</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <quote>diversity, equity, and inclusion</quote> means the concept according to which individuals are—</text> <paragraph id="HAF7C539E5D5E4ABAB89E25405E600FC1"><enum>(1)</enum><text>classified on basis of race, color, sex, national origin, gender identity, or sexual orientation; and</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H647408094CE44DFA8D2CFAEDE153E9B9"><enum>(2)</enum><text>afforded differential or preferential treatment basis of such classification.</text></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> </legis-body></bill>

R. 2202</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250318">March 18, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="L000578">Mr. LaMalfa</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HIF00">Committee on Energy and Commerce</committee-name>, and in addition to the Committees on <committee-name committee-id="HJU00">the Judiciary</committee-name>, and <committee-name committee-id="HWM00">Ways and Means</committee-name>, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned</action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To prohibit taxpayer-funded gender transition procedures, and for other purposes.</official-title></form><legis-body id="HCD5404694642429394514F88D1DA358E" style="OLC">

<title id="HE63A1234D52D4552B63D09A1C57E4405"><enum>I</enum><header>Prohibiting federally funded gender transition procedures</header> 
<section id="H18F90CCF414B4DC58668F7CC9B95EE40"><enum>101.</enum><header>Prohibiting taxpayer-funded gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Title 1, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new chapter:</text> <quoted-block style="USC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H4A0F82BFF96549A7A5D25A282F096EAB"> <chapter id="HD76B892A3F064E9DBB8DDC51D3C50677"><enum>4</enum><header>Prohibiting taxpayer-funded gender transition procedures</header> <toc> <toc-entry level="section">Sec. </toc-entry> <toc-entry level="section" idref="H6BC6BABF204F469598A752966BA20B8D">301. Prohibition on funding for gender transition procedures. </toc-entry> <toc-entry level="section" idref="HA30B2619E6B14365962AEB06E3BCFB44">302. Prohibition on funding for health benefits plans that cover gender transition procedures. </toc-entry> <toc-entry level="section" idref="H54CFD9547BAF41B59113EBC723923D3D">303. Limitation on Federal facilities and employees. </toc-entry> <toc-entry level="section" idref="H6DCA1C541D5140D490532F205B6F8698">304. Construction relating to separate coverage. </toc-entry> <toc-entry level="section" idref="HF2F67173F4874E03ADFA50EC54AAD784">305. Construction relating to the use of non-Federal funds for health coverage. </toc-entry> <toc-entry level="section" idref="HC45E875822D64F959887F6CA27E223D7">306. Construction relating to complications arising from gender transition procedures. </toc-entry> <toc-entry level="section" idref="H5FB61401D756496D84B402CB3C339AF9">307. Definitions. </toc-entry></toc> <section id="H6BC6BABF204F469598A752966BA20B8D"><enum>301.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No funds authorized or appropriated by Federal law, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are authorized or appropriated by Federal law, shall be expended for any gender transition procedures.</text></section> 
<section id="HA30B2619E6B14365962AEB06E3BCFB44"><enum>302.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for health benefits plans that cover gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No funds authorized or appropriated by Federal law, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are authorized or appropriated by Federal law, shall be expended for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of gender transition procedures.</text></section> <section id="H54CFD9547BAF41B59113EBC723923D3D"><enum>303.</enum><header>Limitation on Federal facilities and employees</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No health care service furnished—</text> 
<paragraph id="HC42CC5A7DCF54F77B793E000C1994385"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by or in a health care facility owned or operated by the Federal Government; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H818E343665AF4AB194A57A3DFDCCCCA6"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by any physician or other individual employed by the Federal Government to provide health care services within the scope of the physician’s or individual’s employment,</text></paragraph><continuation-text continuation-text-level="section">may include gender transition procedures. </continuation-text></section> 
<section id="H6DCA1C541D5140D490532F205B6F8698"><enum>304.</enum><header>Construction relating to separate coverage</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as prohibiting any individual, entity, or State or locality from purchasing separate coverage for gender transition procedures or health benefits coverage that includes gender transition procedures so long as such coverage is paid for entirely using only funds not authorized or appropriated by Federal law and such coverage shall not be purchased using matching funds required for a federally subsidized program, including a State’s or locality’s contribution of Medicaid matching funds.</text></section> <section id="HF2F67173F4874E03ADFA50EC54AAD784"><enum>305.</enum><header>Construction relating to the use of non-Federal funds for health coverage</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as restricting the ability of any non-Federal health benefits coverage provider from offering coverage for gender transition procedures, or the ability of a State or locality to contract separately with such a provider for such coverage, so long as only funds not authorized or appropriated by Federal law are used and such coverage shall not be purchased using matching funds required for a federally subsidized program, including a State’s or locality’s contribution of Medicaid matching funds.</text></section> 
<section id="HC45E875822D64F959887F6CA27E223D7"><enum>306.</enum><header>Construction relating to complications arising from gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to apply to the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused by or exacerbated by the performance of a gender transition procedure. </text></section> <section id="H5FB61401D756496D84B402CB3C339AF9"><enum>307.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">For purposes of this chapter:</text> 
<paragraph id="HF73B48D257D14BC589D4E1314525DC48"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Female</header><text>The term <term>female</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a congenital anomaly, historical accident, or intentional or unintentional disruption, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes eggs for fertilization. </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H98A7FCC595AD449584576397F91E728B"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Gender transition</header><text>The term <term>gender transition</term> means the process in which an individual goes from identifying with or presenting as his or her sex to identifying with or presenting a self-proclaimed identity that does not correspond with or is different from his or her sex, and may be accompanied with social, legal, or physical changes. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA48EE228AB8F472B9CFCC915ADEE72B3"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Gender transition procedure</header> 
<subparagraph id="HFA63A41381C5416C8C307B9E7850DD52"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> means any hormonal or surgical intervention for the purpose of gender transition, including— </text> <clause id="H52ACFC1A90294D3A9334464314C1AA05" commented="no"><enum>(i)</enum><text>gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists or any other puberty-blocking or suppressing drugs to stop or delay normal puberty; </text></clause> 
<clause id="HB2A4791B88394C628897E7FE5358796D" commented="no"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>testosterone, estrogen, progesterone, or other androgens to an individual at doses that are supraphysiologic to what would normally be produced endogenously in a healthy individual of the same age and sex;</text></clause> <clause id="H3C54C6569A6241C3A75ADB1C7856A95E"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>castration;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H445A2F845C4D4C5EB5E5AB41383BCC69"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>orchiectomy;</text></clause> <clause id="H42773C5FAA114679B47A5923968631C8"><enum>(v)</enum><text>scrotoplasty;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H2A12D46D7A6A40B6B95C402B2B3F6FF8"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>implantation of erection or testicular prostheses;</text></clause> <clause id="HFF3F4C4F2D114086BAB29BEDDBCC5967"><enum>(vii)</enum><text>vasectomy;</text></clause>

<clause id="H935372F57ED649F8ADD3C1D11AB250FA"><enum>(xii)</enum><text>metoidioplasty;</text></clause> <clause id="H14A36D91FE6D4A3B9346E293A5E9B5A1"><enum>(xiii)</enum><text>penectomy;</text></clause>

<subparagraph id="HA06826B48920418386602150B46494EA"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exclusions</header><text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> does not include the following when furnished to an individual by a health care provider with the consent of such individual or, if applicable, such individual’s parents or legal guardian:</text> <clause id="HDBD2970CFB0D46BE97CE82AC178D8E15"><enum>(i)</enum><text>Services to individuals born with a medically verifiable disorder of sex development, including an individual with external sex characteristics that are irresolvably ambiguous, such as an individual born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, an individual born with 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or an individual born having both ovarian and testicular tissue.</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBFB5143E563749AB8C4578FE339A9A05"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>Services provided when a physician has otherwise diagnosed a disorder of sexual development in which the physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action for a healthy individual of the same sex and age.</text></clause> <clause id="HCCD39D113AA346A29B707B2A4F29CABB" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>The treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused by or exacerbated by the performance of gender transition procedures, whether or not the gender transition procedure was performed in accordance with State and Federal law or whether or not funding for the gender transition procedure is permissible under this section.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H9FD079211C1944AD8FD41DDB00CBE442"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>Any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness (but not claimed mental distress) that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function, unless the procedure is performed.</text></clause> <clause id="H13D3B57F1FF84AE2AD80D3C290C5EF0C"><enum>(v)</enum><text>Puberty suppression or blocking prescription drugs for the purpose of normalizing puberty for a minor experiencing precocious puberty.</text></clause> 
<clause id="H67FCEB51B3CE48A3B8ECE12E26EB2368"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>Male circumcision.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H11D51ADEF84E493F954DD3DCDAF92186"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Male</header><text>The term <term>male</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a congenital anomaly, historical accident, or intentional or unintentional disruption, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization. </text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HD0A959AEB00A4AD9A9929D8F7583F5BD" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Sex</header><text>The term <term>sex</term>, when referring to an individual’s sex, means to refer to either male or female, as biologically determined.</text></paragraph></section></chapter><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> <section id="H92FE0B61C6EF44F7A9F13920BA65D981"><enum>102.</enum><header>Amendment to table of chapters</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">The table of chapters for title 1, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new item:</text>

<section section-type="section-one" id="H6CF51DFA93E1457392BEA72646D0DF7A"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Defining Male and Female Act of 2025</short-title></quote>. </text></section> <section id="HB502D6E23C26433982CCAA934C22CD35"><enum>2.</enum><header>Definition of <quote>sex</quote>, <quote>male</quote>, <quote>female</quote>, and related terms</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline"><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/1/1">Chapter 1</external-xref> of title 1, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:</text>

<section id="H03A33BA6F3ED4AEE8A38C926E1689DCB"><enum>9. </enum><header>Definition of <quote>sex</quote>, <quote>male</quote>, <quote>female</quote>, and related terms</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In determining the meaning of any Act of Congress, or of any ruling, regulation, or interpretation of the various departments and Federal agencies of the United States, the term—</text> <paragraph id="H9EAA8B26BC3B4F87BEBC8394B1ED8458"><enum>(1)</enum><text><term>boy</term> means a minor human male;</text></paragraph>
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB6286089C8074D8985720FAC601072D7"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline"><term>father</term> means a male parent;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA9F1162A530D47B982734F15A40EEA24"><enum>(3)</enum><text><term>female</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means a person belonging, at conception, to the sex characterized by a reproductive system with the biological function of producing eggs (ova); </text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H79FBE88376CC4C04B6D29CA4C498B0FD"><enum>(4)</enum><text><term>gender identity</term> means an identity that reflects an internal and subjective sense of self, disconnected from biological reality and sex and existing on an indeterminate continuum, and, because such an identity does not provide a meaningful basis for identification for purposes of Federal law, the term shall not be recognized by the Federal Government as a replacement for sex; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H75805E076B5540299BB7864A9D3BE5F9"><enum>(5)</enum><text><term>girl</term> means a minor human female;</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H931D4754FD5B41CE8A1C3AC532EF4EFD"><enum>(6)</enum><text><term>male</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means a person belonging, at conception, to the biological sex characterized by a reproductive system with the biological function of producing sperm; </text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC28BFD68B92A4E7C9782DC3E9D7C2B06"><enum>(7)</enum><text><term>man</term>, except when used as a generic reference to human beings, means an adult human male; </text></paragraph>
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC2C8FAB2939C453E90498E45F2477D37"><enum>(8)</enum><text><term>mother</term> means a female parent;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H5675717DD8C94ED3854E7093957DB27F"><enum>(9)</enum><text><term>sex</term>, when referring to a natural person's individual’s sex, means the person’s immutable biological classification as either male or female, as biologically determined and defined by this section; and </text></paragraph>
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H2CB983F773444834AA728321B1554FC9"><enum>(10)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline"><term>woman</term> means an adult human female.</text></paragraph></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> </legis-body></bill>
