<section id="HB1B6BEB02A4C4457980E5D267072D5DB" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Defend Girls Athletics Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="H2419502B90EA4A358955ABF6EB1CD661"><enum>2.</enum><header>Elementary and secondary schools</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Title VIII of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/7801">20 U.S.C. 7801 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by inserting after section 8524 the following:</text> 
<quoted-block style="OLC" id="H1089BA3EDDA74CC6AFC2A896718561C3" display-inline="no-display-inline"> 
<section id="HB42F66836B7A4147BD1856E367D34229"><enum>8524A.</enum><header>Requirements relating to biological fairness in women’s sports</header> 
<subsection id="H85A8412340B54E9996991A90168BF802"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">As a condition of receiving funds under this Act, a local educational agency shall ensure that each school under the jurisdiction of such agency complies with the requirements of Executive Order 14201 (90 Fed. Reg 9279; relating to keeping men out of women’s sports), as in effect on the date of enactment of this section.</text> </subsection> <subsection id="H8BD76539495F482C883B93DE6F430C2C"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Certification</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">On an annual basis not later than August 15 of each year, each local educational agency subject to the requirements of this section shall certify in writing to the relevant State educational agency that the local educational agency is in compliance with such requirements and will remain in compliance with such requirements until August 15 of the following year. The State educational agency shall report to the Secretary by September 15 of each year a list of those local educational agencies that have not filed the certification or against which complaints have been made to the State educational agency that the local educational agencies are not in compliance with this section.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="H8D8EA9828F6143DD971C5A8E9FF2F3EE"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Enforcement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Secretary determines that a local educational agency has violated the requirements of this section or if a State educational agency does not submit the report required under subsection (b) by the deadline indicated in such subsection—</text> <paragraph id="H824A56CCF7AA43A2B3E6E5A2DC369D73"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Secretary shall direct the State or local educational agency (as the case may be) to return to the Secretary any funds received under this Act (whether directly or through a subgrant from another entity) that are unobligated as of the date of such determination; and</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H69F8E41F1D264B8FB4E4F13A35694C59"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">such agency shall be ineligible to receive funds under this Act until the agency complies with such requirements or submits such report, as determined by the Secretary.</text></paragraph></subsection> </section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section> <section id="H9CA61CBFE49248B89C0F205837E9F91B"><enum>3.</enum><header>Institutions of higher education</header> <subsection id="HF74F0D1FE0E64B668BA403A688EBED77"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Part B of title I of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1011">20 U.S.C. 1011 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following:</text> 
<quoted-block style="OLC" id="H331E231D0E824B92843743BCABBD1D18" display-inline="no-display-inline"> 
<section id="H64F974C27E5F4B54A840A27C42113B19"><enum>124.</enum><header>Requirements relating to biological fairness in women’s sports</header> 
<subsection id="HB1DE61D1903F4059A7D0097102017DE7"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no institution of higher education shall be eligible to receive funds or any other form of financial assistance under any Federal program, including participation in any federally funded or guaranteed student loan program, unless the institution certifies to the Secretary, not later than July 1 of each year, that the institution is in compliance and will remain in compliance with the requirements of Executive Order 14201 (90 Fed. Reg 9279; relating to keeping men out of women’s sports), as in effect on the date of enactment of this section.</text></subsection> <subsection id="H5F8558F865F4497CA43C9F9D30D632D9"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Enforcement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">If the Secretary determines that an institution of higher education has violated the requirements of subsection (a)—</text> 
<paragraph id="HE4BEF347BF7A42A1B057CF40FAD53890"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the Secretary shall direct the institution to return to the Secretary any funds received under this Act that are unobligated as of the date of such determination; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H32C5A8EA02964858ADB4EC94C6E9AA1C"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">such institution shall be ineligible to receive funds or otherwise participate in programs under this Act until the institution complies with such requirements, as determined by the Secretary.</text></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection>

R. 4512</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250717">July 17, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="M000194">Ms. Mace</sponsor> (for herself, <cosponsor name-id="G000565">Mr. Gosar</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="G000603">Mr. Gill of Texas</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="B000825">Ms. Boebert</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HSY00">Committee on Science, Space, and Technology</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To prohibit the availability of Federal funds for certain animal research, and for other purposes.</official-title></form><legis-body id="HE4290DC940034415972F89D1858498AA" style="OLC"> 
<section id="H7C765D52E2E742A5B02D805628FDDE5B" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header>
 <text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Transgender Research on Animals Now Stops and Money for Ideological Cruelty Eliminated Act</short-title></quote> or the <quote><short-title>TRANS MICE Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> 
<section id="H43C2C674040D49B49A1A46C99CC7CC73" section-type="subsequent-section"><enum>2.</enum><header>Prohibition on availability of Federal funds for certain animal research</header> 
<subsection id="H3A5C922B30FB4CB181FEF0C90D91D6D0"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no Federal funds may be made available to conduct, support, or fund (directly or indirectly) any covered research on a qualified animal.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HFCA0BD4A8BBD4C8E88832B31E2EC6CCC"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section:</text> 
<paragraph id="HBB44C95976244374A3C0C090FA11A872"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Covered research</header><text>The term <quote>covered research</quote> means any research to study the effects of drugs, hormones, surgery, or other interventions to alter the body of a qualified animal to no longer correspond to the biological sex of such animal, including by—</text> <subparagraph id="H95293029776841ED8E6AAA157CF47F8B"><enum>(A)</enum><text>disrupting the development of an animal’s body;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H44057D894A5948D1BCB97EAEDCD4CDDE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>inhibiting the natural functions of the animal’s body; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H2BBA4DEFECC447CCB8BBBDC62E4BDF89"><enum>(C)</enum><text>modifying the physical appearance of an animal.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HA4CEAF687D1B47C9BCA983BCD4440E84"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Excepted animal</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>excepted animal</quote> means any non-human vertebrate that—</text> <subparagraph id="H072B52D578C1443280A0F022273238D4"><enum>(A)</enum><text>changes sex during its lifetime; or</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H0C19FB85CDDF448C88D8F2FC777266E7"><enum>(B)</enum><text>naturally possesses both male and female reproductive organs.</text> </subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE25A22A6F0574F4091FEDE6D7CCC7EA5" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Qualified animal</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>qualified animal</quote> means any non-human vertebrate species (other than excepted animals). Such term includes mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, and amphibians.</text> </paragraph></subsection></section>

<section section-type="section-one" id="H1DCEA5B14191425583E86B6A7BE6B705"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Jamie Reed Protecting Our Kids from Child Abuse Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="H4CD5CAFB853346CC807271F57DA9C3F5"><enum>2.</enum><header>Federal tort for harm to children caused by gender-transition procedures</header> <subsection id="H60BFCCA5811547938D2BC1F7DAA36667"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text>
<paragraph id="H70DC85A097E7491B988FF0F57D1E465B"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Gender transition procedure</header>
<subparagraph id="HB9915040262D43B8A596ACC9E4E717AC"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> means—</text> <clause id="H83170A9258A244DB8C32102E86EDF331"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists or any other puberty-blocking drugs for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual's biological sex of male or female;</text></clause>
<clause id="HF79EB1CCAB6348E682A7404EF96B9BD3"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of testosterone (when prescribed to a female) or estrogen (when prescribed to a male) for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex of male or female; or</text></clause> <clause id="H34F997CC97B34269A243E37E9033AFD6"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>a surgery to change the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex of male or female.</text></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="HE5F1CA089E714FEAB6355D95355A4120"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> does not include—</text> <clause id="HE367CBBABD9349F39BF686663E500CC1"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an intervention described in subparagraph (A) that is performed on—</text>
<subclause id="HB90D0589A5AC4BF5B31A9D98BBDBA005"><enum>(I)</enum><text>an individual with biological sex characteristics that are inherently ambiguous, such as those born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or having both ovarian and testicular tissue; or</text></subclause> <subclause id="H9EC4AC3717EB4C7BA270DCFC38D29F14"><enum>(II)</enum><text>an individual with respect to whom a physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action, for a biological male or biological female;</text></subclause></clause>
<clause id="HD3EE33B02CDB473B8D1A36861DFFF2B8"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused or exacerbated by the performance of an intervention described in subparagraph (A) without regard to whether the intervention was performed in accordance with State or Federal law or whether the intervention is covered by the private right of action under subsection (c); or</text></clause> <clause id="H3C24AB8697E54E5DB8A14D74ABC456C4"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H3610771604194B7F90DBD04FF0249863"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Hospital</header><text>The term <term>hospital</term> has the meaning given such term in section 1861(e) of the Social Security Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1395x">42 U.S.C. 1395x(e)</external-xref>).</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H166DA55D5D72434F9066444B8FAD4824"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Institution of higher education</header><text>The term <term>institution of higher education</term> has the meaning given such term in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1001">20 U.S.C. 1001</external-xref>).</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H8FF1D4FD10BE48329D020E6C4EAF9449"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Medical practitioner</header><text>The term <term>medical practitioner</term> means a person who is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized by the laws of a State to administer health care in the ordinary course of the practice of the person’s profession.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H76D29B813F2149A7981D0C7757082BC2"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Minor</header><text>The term <term>minor</term> means an individual who has not yet reached 18 years of age.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H92A44B6851CC402B8A0CD9C177401181"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Pediatric gender clinic</header><text>The term <term>pediatric gender clinic</term> means a medical facility that specializes in the diagnosis or treatment of gender discordance and gender dysphoria in minors, including medical interventions such as therapeutic diagnosis of gender dysphoria and performance of (or referral for) gender-transition procedures on minors.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="HEFC7C125C14445B3892F0609BDEEB6B2"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Liability</header><text>The following individuals and entities shall be liable in accordance with this section to any individual who suffers bodily injury or harm to mental health (including any physical, psychological, emotional, or physiological harm) that is attributable, in whole or in part, to a gender-transition procedure performed on the individual when the individual was a minor:</text>
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB7A12D22BC6D4A678652A180E60B40B7"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H4101B642CA684DE094A7B4E61D7B35C8"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any medical practitioner who administered health care, at the time of the particular procedure, at the pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H086F323D19334C0FA602D8423428BA41"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An institution of higher education that hosts, operates, partners with, provides funding to, or is otherwise affiliated with the pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H3C0A766D37CA467D892D77979D1DF00E"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A hospital that hosts, operates, partners with, provides funding to, or is otherwise affiliated with the pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC7903F677F474D5296C7F21DAEE93AA0"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any medical practitioner who performed the gender-transition procedure on the individual.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H77DE3FC15AE04C01947322F65C1BCF74"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Private right of action</header><text>An individual who suffers bodily injury or harm to mental health that is attributable, in whole or in part, to a gender-transition procedure provided to the individual when the individual was a minor may, not later than 30 years after the date on which the individual turns 18 years of age, bring a civil action against an individual or entity described in subsection (b), in an appropriate district court of the United States or a State court of competent jurisdiction for—</text>
<paragraph id="H1ADAE75557944AECBCE7375A76A8075C"><enum>(1)</enum><text>compensatory damages;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC4741933624A48B4B81921C7E0DE4CE0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>punitive damages; and</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HF180502C23DC4D4A84398E617C760823"><enum>(3)</enum><text>attorney’s fees and costs.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H8181EB4035C3413E9DB391ADE9688FF2"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Affirmative defense</header><text>It shall be an affirmative defense to an action brought by or on behalf of an individual upon whom a gender-transition procedure was performed under subsection (c) that the pediatric gender clinic or medical practitioner who performed the gender-transition procedure on the individual, at all relevant times, did not know and had no reason to know that the individual in question was a minor.</text></subsection></section>
<section id="HFB9CF09D8D2C486FA501B9E6EEF282F5"><enum>3.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No Federal funds may be made available—</text> <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H5F495F2B0BDA40CF8EF94EF31282666C"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to a pediatric gender clinic;</text></paragraph>
<paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7F17D10D32FA4782A76A74F5166E0909"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to an institution of higher education or hospital that hosts, operates, partners with, provides funding to, or is otherwise affiliated with, a pediatric gender clinic; or</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H14C2A82E1B61460598D04DDB0A6ED676"><enum>(3)</enum><text>for any gender-transition procedure performed on a minor.</text></paragraph></section>
<section id="HE9B9A299A88E4FF28F814C064A3BFBE2"><enum>4.</enum><header>Effective date and retroactive application</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act shall—</text> <paragraph id="H4E2426E597204EDBACCDF6640B706331"><enum>(1)</enum><text>take effect on the date of enactment of this Act; and</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H9951FBA2F886496BA6BA196561C0227B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>apply to any gender-transition procedure that took place before, on, or after the effective date under paragraph (1).</text></paragraph></section> <section commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H8DFF219DE8A54322A350F1C0BEB52821"><enum>5.</enum><header>Severability</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">If any provision of this Act, or the application of such provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be unconstitutional, the remainder of this Act, and the application of the remaining provisions of this Act, to any person or circumstance, shall not be affected.</text></section> 
</legis-body></bill>

<bill bill-stage="Introduced-in-House" dms-id="H05A155C1EA9D4BF8918C00549379EB70" public-private="public" key="H" bill-type="olc"><metadata xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">

<dc:title>119 HR 4730 IH: Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History Act</dc:title>
<dc:publisher>U.S. House of Representatives</dc:publisher>
<dc:date>2025-07-23</dc:date>
<dc:format>text/xml</dc:format>

<form>
<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">119th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 4730</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250723">July 23, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S001224">Mr. Self</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HII00">Committee on Natural Resources</committee-name>, and in addition to the Committee on <committee-name committee-id="HHA00">House Administration</committee-name>, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned</action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To codify Executive Order 14253 relating to restoring truth and sanity to American history, and for other purposes.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H0F5DC07EE2244AC9A1BA1091D0DB9244" style="OLC"> 
<section id="H23CCE5463DE848F5819D2607627109C9" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="HCB8157141EC448C1A22DCD49EA045034"><enum>2.</enum><header>Codification of Executive Order 14253</header> <subsection id="H7D308961789845F291254CA6584D134A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Findings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Congress finds the following:</text>
<paragraph id="H48046205FD534A00A47E256CEEFA94A2"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Over the past decade, Americans have witnessed a concerted and widespread effort to rewrite our Nation's history, replacing objective facts with a distorted narrative driven by ideology rather than truth. This revisionist movement seeks to undermine the remarkable achievements of the United States by casting its founding principles and historical milestones in a negative light. Under this historical revision, our Nation's unparalleled legacy of advancing liberty, individual rights, and human happiness is reconstructed as inherently racist, sexist, oppressive, or otherwise irredeemably flawed. Rather than fostering unity and a deeper understanding of our shared past, the widespread effort to rewrite history deepens societal divides and fosters a sense of national shame, disregarding the progress America has made and the ideals that continue to inspire millions around the globe.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H8BDCAC8430454BFFB2D15F8BE51AACF6"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The prior administration advanced this corrosive ideology. At Independence National Historical Park in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania—where our Nation declared that all men are created equal—the prior administration sponsored training by an organization that advocates dismantling <quote>Western foundations</quote> and <quote>interrogating institutional racism</quote> and pressured National Historical Park rangers that their racial identity should dictate how they convey history to visiting Americans because America is purportedly racist.</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB4786ECD39244916BA2EAD0140501DE4"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Once widely respected as a symbol of American excellence and a global icon of cultural achievement, the Smithsonian Institution has, in recent years, come under the influence of a divisive, race-centered ideology. This shift has promoted narratives that portray American and Western values as inherently harmful and oppressive. For example, the Smithsonian American Art Museum today features <quote>The Shape of Power: Stories of Race and American Sculpture</quote>, an exhibit representing that <quote>[s]ocieties including the United States have used race to establish and maintain systems of power, privilege, and disenfranchisement.</quote> The exhibit further claims that <quote>sculpture has been a powerful tool in promoting scientific racism</quote> and promotes the view that race is not a biological reality but a social construct, stating <quote>Race is a human invention</quote>.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H36B2AE34469844909D2DA181AE80CFEB"> <enum>(4)</enum> <text>The National Museum of African American History and Culture has proclaimed that <quote>hard work</quote>, <quote>individualism</quote>, and <quote>the nuclear family</quote> are aspects of <quote>White culture</quote>. The forthcoming Smithsonian American Women's History Museum plans on celebrating the exploits of male athletes participating in women's sports. These are just a few examples.</text>
        </paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H4788729CE5404AF880101492CA08C1C6"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Policy statement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">It is the policy of this Act—</text> <paragraph id="H180FC51380814EB3A043DBECEF7E873C"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to restore Federal sites dedicated to history, including parks and museums, to solemn and uplifting public monuments that remind Americans of our extraordinary heritage, consistent progress toward becoming a more perfect Union, and unmatched record of advancing liberty, prosperity, and human flourishing;</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H6FC5B5378E274711BD6B3C2DA4A6B10B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>that Museums in our Nation's capital should be places where individuals go to learn—not to be subjected to ideological indoctrination or divisive narratives that distort our shared history; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD3E666CDF83844348AF441ECB2D5FA7F"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to restore the Smithsonian Institution to its rightful place as a symbol of inspiration and American greatness—igniting the imagination of young minds, honoring the richness of American history and innovation, and instilling pride in the hearts of all Americans.</text></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H8C04923FF6AB48A684CA655B57CBA17E"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Saving our Smithsonian</header>
<paragraph id="HFA80C204B8C54CAFACB4D7B6075AC399"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Vice President, in consultation with the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and the Special Assistant to the President and Senior Associate Staff Secretary, shall—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HADEAF7EA55934DEFB8E3324D40684B63"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">work to effectuate the policies of this Act through the Vice President's role on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution with respect to the Smithsonian Institution and its museums, education and research centers, and the National Zoo, including by seeking to remove from such properties anything that—</text>
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCC847317372B468D9AB816F47CD93E34"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">violates the policy of this Act as articulated in subsection (b) or Federal civil rights laws; or</text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H90F3B69944CC42A1A549EF6D0EFE5FB8"> <enum>(ii)</enum> <text display-inline="yes-display-inline">divides Americans based on race; and</text>
                        </clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD462FCE6B6024C64A3E6F6F06627A721"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">recommend to the President any additional actions necessary to fully effectuate such policies.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA8B04283B8AB48B5B51F8EE90055B867"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Future appropriations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Vice President and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall work with Congress to ensure that future appropriations to the Smithsonian Institution—</text>
<subparagraph id="H744896C4DAC94AE495A4FB9D02A2C322"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">prohibit expenditure on exhibits or programs that—</text> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCC80927F768343A48475E2AC1226A902"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">degrade shared American values;</text></clause>
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HBEC5B1D0575D43C2A07045A2BC0E9724"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">divide Americans based on race; or</text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H15665E67C97443D0BCDFE4356231B9C6"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">promote programs or ideologies inconsistent with Federal law, the policy of this Act as articulated in subsection (b), or Federal civil rights laws; and</text></clause></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H9C8BF99057644477BCA06AE897230379" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>celebrate the achievements of women in the American Women's History Museum and do not recognize men as women in any respect, including by—</text> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD43D40003D6C458486F0F5ED422DF59C"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">promoting, celebrating, or favorably depicting biological males competing in women’s sports, winning awards designated for women, dressing as women, or entering private facilities designated for women;</text></clause>
<clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H9B0A3845D8184D82BD006B214871C2A3"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">promoting, celebrating, or favorably depicting gender-affirming medicine, especially for minors; or</text></clause> <clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD22FAEF899D24D7B989C727792F57390"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">including any other material that degrades the biological nature of sex or violates Federal civil rights laws.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD1592F111D924ABAA1BC48B9729F886D"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Other measures to promote policy</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the Secretary of the Interior shall take any other measures within their authority to promote the policy of this Act.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD9EECA2EA2E6439AB75AC5FACF90F751"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">As appropriate, the Vice President shall, in consultation with the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and Special Assistant to the President and Senior Associate Staff Secretary, work with the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the Majority Leader of the Senate to seek the appointment of citizen members to the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution committed to advancing the policy of this Act.</text></paragraph></subsection>
<subsection id="H4BC1F0D992224210B6657E5630B07064"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Restoring Independence Hall</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of the Interior shall provide sufficient funding, as available, to improve the infrastructure of Independence National Historical Park, which shall be complete by July 4, 2026, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.</text></subsection> <subsection id="HF9C2D5E4C40A429EBD6DD884D491092C"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Restoring truth in American history</header><text>The Secretary of the Interior shall—</text>
<paragraph id="HAC8D47008472486D8B3F92F792FFAA92"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">determine whether, since January 1, 2020, public monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties within the Department of the Interior's jurisdiction have been removed or changed to perpetuate a false reconstruction of American history, inappropriately minimize the value of certain historical events or figures, divide Americans based on race, recognize men as women, or include any other improper partisan ideology;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF5492E246F29430FA8B15230AED576D0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>take action to reinstate the pre-existing monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties, as appropriate and consistent with section 437 of the Revised Statutes (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/43/1451">43 U.S.C. 1451</external-xref>), division A of subtitle I of title 54, United States Code, and other applicable law; and</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HD3588B0A88BE4F3ABBB3813DF4838097"><enum>(3)</enum><text>take action, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, to ensure that all public monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties within the Department of the Interior’s jurisdiction—</text> <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HC71CDAF3852E44EA9D7F5902367D2F58"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">do not contain descriptions, depictions, or other content that inappropriately disparage Americans past or living (including persons living in colonial times), divide Americans based on race, or recognize men as women; and</text></subparagraph>
<subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HCB185B2CA2ED4A9BA2C39457CE32C299"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">instead focus on the greatness of the achievements and progress of the American people or, with respect to natural features, the beauty, abundance, and grandeur of the American landscape.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H0EFCCC3043084D8EBEE6D940080EBAC1"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in this Act shall be construed to—</text>
<paragraph id="HE823FF177046453A92982A274C36D601"><enum>(1)</enum><text>impair or otherwise affect—</text> <subparagraph id="H13922A43B0C04B009376466850279003"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or</text></subparagraph>
<subparagraph id="H86BF23EB6B2B48AF8F4D4001D7ADC2A2"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals; or</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HC53F1D85D2CF4BC4B209511D5E99CDB8"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> 
</legis-body></bill>

<official-title display="yes">To authorize a civil right of action for individuals on whom gender-related medical treatment was performed while such individual was a minor, and for other purposes.</official-title>

<legis-body id="H130240B68B7A4D399413872C305840DD" style="OLC"> 
<section id="HBBDB983AAE704489A7AB9F291E6C92F4" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Gender-Affirming Child Abuse Prevention Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="H8E6B6631A8F14DBABB5A9B4AA967C185"><enum>2.</enum><header>Civil right of action related to gender-related medical treatment</header> <subsection id="H8AE0BC4B2D1747E9885C3BA4CCDD026C"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Civil action</header> <paragraph id="H6579D59F365E492B8B8801EF7AFF99F5"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Right of action</header> <subparagraph id="HA00B895276F947EF8B44D77B48153614"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Except as provided in paragraph (4), an individual on whom gender-affirming care was performed while such individual was a minor, in a circumstance described in paragraph (3) may bring a civil action in an appropriate district court of the United States against each person who performed the gender-affirming care for relief set forth in paragraph (2).</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCD5646E0858D46B4A24B928B48A95B5F"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Rights on behalf of certain individuals</header><text>In the case of an individual who is under 18 years of age, incompetent, incapacitated, or deceased, the legal guardian of the individual or representative of the individual’s estate, another family member, or any other person appointed as suitable by the court, may assume the individual’s rights under this section.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="H2A40D49F891E4FBFBBE9A79E0A59B924"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Relief</header><text>An individual may recover the actual damages sustained by the individual or liquidated damages in the amount of $250,000 for each instance of gender affirming care being performed on the individual while such individual was a minor, and the cost of the action, including reasonable attorney’s fees and other litigation costs reasonably incurred.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H3B7E22EA62EF47328E807C6CB4D432E5"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Circumstances described</header><text>For the purposes of paragraph (1), the circumstances described in this paragraph are that—</text> <subparagraph id="H222248C8E6C54A3891305394582470A6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the defendant or victim traveled in interstate or foreign commerce, or traveled using a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in paragraph (1);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4041C4AA6A2A487F9DFA29CF72ABFAD7"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the defendant used a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in paragraph (1);</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5B9083661EDE4B1298B445E462539BF6"><enum>(C)</enum><text>any payment of any kind was made, directly or indirectly, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in paragraph (1) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce;</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H08D8A0C827FE4DE19C4739ACB130268C"><enum>(D)</enum><text>the defendant transmitted in interstate or foreign commerce any communication relating to or in furtherance of the conduct described in paragraph (1) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means or in manner, including by computer, mail, wire, or electromagnetic transmission;</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H5A8DA207306F4B638EFE320D1C9DF275"><enum>(E)</enum><text>any instrument, item, substance, or other object that has traveled in interstate or foreign commerce was used to perform the conduct described in paragraph (1);</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H9DEE276AEBB148F89C8BA65C614A777F"><enum>(F)</enum><text>the conduct described in paragraph (1) occurred within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, or any territory or possession of the United States; or</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H59830938B5B645B385138FF354A33421"><enum>(G)</enum><text>the conduct described in paragraph (1) otherwise occurred in or affected interstate or foreign commerce.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection> 
<subsection id="H29082126E9C04D978D634DD1B80CAFBA"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section—</text> <paragraph id="H341F0D62E6F4406781666C26570C684A"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Gender-related medical treatment</header><text>The term <quote>gender-related medical treatment</quote>—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H42299C00418E463AA4A23EFE0A88E0ED"><enum>(A)</enum><text>means—</text> <clause id="HA7C311F5DE64464F8409CF1693B6FF4F"><enum>(i)</enum><text>with respect to a female individual, medical treatments provided for purposes of addressing the perception of such individual that the gender or sex of such individual is not female, including—</text> 
<subclause id="H4EC614896CB54DF4B5802103FC05ACF7"><enum>(I)</enum><text>surgical procedures, including—</text> <item id="HCB8EC432221B448FACEB8206D9D7FD36"><enum>(aa)</enum><text>vaginectomy;</text></item> 
<item id="H2405D20F09A64116A6296795DF6062E4"><enum>(bb)</enum><text>hysterectomy;</text></item> <item id="H45AC6234A43A4A808688264FCBC96A04"><enum>(cc)</enum><text>oophorectomy;</text></item> 
<item id="HBCBD4A9CF51E411BA5D001830CD4926A"><enum>(dd)</enum><text>reconstruction of the urethra;</text></item> <item id="H1699D549ECCD469EBD3484F5C8B2C74E"><enum>(ee)</enum><text>metoidioplasty;</text></item> 
<item id="H2FA47637E3434974A29E1EED1508AE51"><enum>(ff)</enum><text>phalloplasty;</text></item> <item id="H8F01B37B6A5A461F82F758206874895D"><enum>(gg)</enum><text>salpingo-oophorectomy;</text></item> 
<item id="H7D17A14F7C244D43B238E5A4E0249B26"><enum>(hh)</enum><text>scrotoplasty;</text></item> <item id="H423E6F21EAE14CECBDD1497F945F73C2"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>implantation of erection or testicular protheses;</text></item> 
<item id="H83D99679BA96474DB183AAEED8393871"><enum>(jj)</enum><text>subcutaneous mastectomy;</text></item> <item id="H0A70D90848164C82AAF8CE6BCD25189B"><enum>(kk)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">vocal cord surgery;</text></item> 
<item id="HD41B44CE2C7E4933A4606AE49AE48BB4"><enum>(ll)</enum><text>pectoral implants; and</text></item> <item id="HC5FC011CA8374724AF4FDD07C7B0C84B"><enum>(mm)</enum><text>penile transplantation;</text></item></subclause> 
<subclause id="HBF0DBA259FB644A7BE71A7D61E353D7F"><enum>(II)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">exogenous doses of testosterone or other androgens;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H7670DEF3B3EE4F1097B4FBC7C8300588"><enum>(III)</enum><text>puberty blockers, including—</text> 
<item id="H4461A320E10246DBBE3DB523E3751490"><enum>(aa)</enum><text>GnRH agonists; and</text></item> <item id="H98D94AC4700D4C68B323713D4DA0CF4A"><enum>(bb)</enum><text>synthetic drugs that suppress the production of estrogen and progesterone or delay or suppress pubertal development in female individuals; and</text></item></subclause> 
<subclause id="HFBB6C98C5F294BD894FF735658EAC32C"><enum>(IV)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">such other medical treatment, identified by the Secretary of Health and Human Services, that may be provided for purposes of addressing the perception of such individual that the gender or sex of such individual is not male.</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="H9F4C863B9F20409CB92A6804B3F5083C"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>with respect to a male individual, medical treatments provided for purposes of addressing the perception of such individual that the gender or sex of such individual is not male, including—</text> 
<subclause id="HE08783CD4D414D55AB0D542319F8CB29"><enum>(I)</enum><text>surgical procedures, including—</text> <item id="H743E7C34040D43ADA129FDB2229FF70C"><enum>(aa)</enum><text>penectomy;</text></item> 
<item id="HA8ED603FB1E644F2ABB140E27AB2825F"><enum>(bb)</enum><text>orchiectomy;</text></item> <item id="H83265C4825154EA9A8A6C44908257787"><enum>(cc)</enum><text>vaginoplasty;</text></item> 
<item id="H9DF59FC93F854F6ABB6276A3384B5C57"><enum>(dd)</enum><text>clitoroplasty;</text></item> <item id="HD7EEB06898DA445685029563D313B48A"><enum>(ee)</enum><text>vulvoplasty;</text></item> 
<item id="H12393F63C03D440FA23515ADFE54379A"><enum>(ff)</enum><text>augmentation mammoplasty;</text></item> <item id="H8AAD42038E2D41949658667662BD1F3F"><enum>(gg)</enum><text>facial feminization surgery;</text></item> 
<item id="H4F84ACA4CAFF4E90A25BB4C564E70E31"><enum>(hh)</enum><text>vocal cord surgery;</text></item> <item id="H4BB4EA88E6EC4B2286F1C67BD5D3FB39"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">chondrolaryngoplasty;</text></item> 
<item id="HA5A2EAADDF82486C8B750BC958BA6F4C"><enum>(jj)</enum><text>gluteal augmentation; and</text></item> <item id="HEF7987A5CCA3452492DABD809ED1BB29"><enum>(kk)</enum><text>uterine transplantation;</text></item></subclause> 
<subclause id="H3BF5DEC8B02F45B39CA38E1A7A642B91"><enum>(II)</enum><text>exogenous doses of estrogen;</text></subclause> <subclause id="HBF435C058CE24EC893A558BFEB1EBC25"><enum>(III)</enum><text>puberty blockers, including—</text> 
<item id="H483C5AEE6B294BBD8043BA71E9E48051"><enum>(aa)</enum><text>GnRH agonists; and</text></item> <item id="HE1E940BF376942A4B228413F5CB92545"><enum>(bb)</enum><text>synthetic drugs that suppress the production of testosterone or delay or suppress pubertal development in male individuals; and</text></item></subclause> 
<subclause id="HA36861BA42AC4F43BBFD34347FF644FE"><enum>(IV)</enum><text>such other medical treatment, identified by the Secretary of Health and Human Services, that may be provided for purposes of addressing the perception of such individual that the gender or sex of such individual is not male.</text></subclause></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H97564A81F8724EC496B9332AB51A6260"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">does not include any medical treatment performed on an individual for the purposes of treating—</text> 
<clause id="H030A089D71FD4137AE247701172FC27A"><enum>(i)</enum><text>a disorder of sex development, diagnosed by a physician after such physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that such individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action;</text></clause> <clause id="H6270AF7778144C1FA961AE7A23F17F36"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>irresolvably ambiguous biological sex characteristics of such individual, including the presence of—</text> 
<subclause id="HB8E89F9D2A4B43E7A9916DEC9E77550B"><enum>(I)</enum><text>46 XX chromosomes with virilization;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H20FC9FCAE3CB41E095233FEF107CDAD6"><enum>(II)</enum><text>46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization; or</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H12E4ED1275EE458B9F42558B699B714E"><enum>(III)</enum><text>both ovarian and testicular tissue; or</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="HE409BCDC7A4F4ABEB9EA90B2E768CBA2"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>an infection, injury, disease, or disorder caused or exacerbated by gender-related medical treatment that was furnished to an individual.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H7EF2C30D30EA4865A1C3FE3E36DAE208"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Sex</header><text>The term <quote>sex</quote> means the biological determination as to whether an individual is male or female, as such terms are defined in this section.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF24B768CC0D741DC8AC8CF484C47F2E0"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Gender</header><text>The term <quote>gender</quote>—</text> 
<subparagraph id="HB41490DFC9EE4C16B325FED61AC47D64"><enum>(A)</enum><text>means—</text> <clause id="HDB762B91A7AB4F218DA5FB08A4B12F7A"><enum>(i)</enum><text>males, females, or the natural differences between males and females, unless such term is otherwise specified or used alone (rather than with or as an adjective modifying other words); and</text></clause> 
<clause id="H020966C1CF804CDE8ED65D27877A2CBD"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>a synonym for sex; and</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HA425B4BD59D440A8B48098F7EB2E7B59"><enum>(B)</enum><text>does not mean a synonym for terms or ideas such as gender identity, experienced gender, gender expression, or gender roles.</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCAEF0F35D49444B589315D60AE47B36E"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Female</header><text>The term <quote>female</quote> means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes eggs for fertilization.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H3CA4244CF11D4D58A4A9F330D544D945"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Male</header><text>The term <quote>male</quote> means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization.</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCB7748EFE6BB4EAA978FE7BF25E72F17"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Minor</header><text>The term <quote>minor</quote> means an individual under the age of 18.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> </legis-body> </bill>

developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization.</text></clause></subparagraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection></section></legis-body></bill>

<bill bill-stage="Introduced-in-House" dms-id="H019AC8819942477A9A48010D70519C3A" public-private="public" key="H" bill-type="olc"><metadata xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">

<dc:title>119 HR 650 IH: Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act</dc:title>
<dc:publisher>U.S. House of Representatives</dc:publisher>

<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">119th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 650</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250123">January 23, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="F000450">Ms. Foxx</sponsor> (for herself, <cosponsor name-id="W000814">Mr. Weber of Texas</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="R000612">Mr. Rose</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="M001211">Mrs. Miller of Illinois</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="B001257">Mr. Bilirakis</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="H001077">Mr. Higgins of Louisiana</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="G000558">Mr. Guthrie</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="F000475">Mr. Finstad</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="L000583">Mr. Loudermilk</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="M001218">Mr. McCormick</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="H001099">Mr. Haridopolos</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HJU00">Committee on the Judiciary</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To protect the right of parents to direct the upbringing of their children as a fundamental right.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H2E096C5B97094DEF94497361C563FC0D" style="OLC"><section id="H44482939E5EB433FA74DD4434C75AD53" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="H77B4A1E1DA454E64BD4060D390C40185"><enum>2.</enum><header>Congressional findings and declaration of purposes</header><subsection id="HC81556516ACE49C98C556CD9B3156FDF"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Findings</header><text>Congress finds the following:</text><paragraph id="H0C9282C8C6AD4CADA9D859F469459B8B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The nature of the parent-child relationship endows parents with the primary responsibility and obligation to care for their child.</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7D7268450FBF49CDB3C4C904E06C0E1D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>From these responsibilities and obligations comes the pre-political, natural right of parents to care for their children. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H333F4F9F631440FCBD24505EFBC581C3"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The role of parents in the raising and rearing of their children is of inestimable value and deserving of both praise and protection by all levels of government.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H584651EF3145427AB5F063C03AE51BEA"><enum>(4)</enum><text>This right as recognized in the traditions of western civilization recognizes that parents have the responsibility to love, nurture, raise, and protect their children.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H6EDD29E60CE04925B3EE9B2EA6FB7ABB"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The right encompasses the authority of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children according to the dictates of their conscience, to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children in their own beliefs and religion, and to be the primary decision maker for their child until the child reaches adulthood.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H7850BB5D96274821AE42FA8DBCDE0699"><enum>(6)</enum><text>The Supreme Court has consistently recognized the primary role of parents in caring for children, concluding the following: </text><subparagraph id="HB3AC37B397654A29BD17CB35B0B9014C"><enum>(A)</enum><text><quote>[T]he child is not the mere creature of the state; those who nurture him and direct his destiny have the right, coupled with the high duty, to recognize and prepare him for additional obligations.</quote> Pierce v. Soc’y of the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus &amp; Mary, 268 U.S. 510, 535 (1925).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H6A506652BB594641A37C7377CE25A135"><enum>(B)</enum><text><quote>[I]t is the natural duty of the parent to give his children education suitable to their station in life.</quote> Meyer v. Nebraska, 262 U.S. 390, 400 (1923).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HA23016F69E074D55890C23758B4D6EE8"><enum>(C)</enum><text><quote>It is plain that the interest of a parent in the companionship, care, custody, and management of his or her children comes to this Court with a momentum for respect lacking when appeal is made to liberties which derive merely from shifting economic arrangements.</quote> Stanley v. Illinois, 405 U.S. 645, 651 (1972).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H19DD7750FFBE44F6BACE7A2F3F12F71E"><enum>(D)</enum><text><quote>The history and culture of Western civilization reflect a strong tradition of parental concern for the nurture and upbringing of their children. This primary role of the parents in the upbringing of their children is now established beyond debate as an enduring American tradition.</quote> Wisconsin v. Yoder, 406 U.S. 205, 232 (1972).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H5AA0C302B8FD4DCC93419C256C28EEB2"><enum>(E)</enum><text><quote>Our jurisprudence historically has reflected Western civilization concepts of the family as a unit with broad parental authority over minor children. Our cases have consistently followed that course.</quote> Parham v. J. R., 442 U.S. 584, 602 (1979).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HC2C41C3044AF47049058F0D0C8131A00"><enum>(F)</enum><text><quote>We have recognized on numerous occasions that the relationship between parent and child is constitutionally protected.</quote>Quilloin v. Walcott, 434 U.S. 246, 255 (1978).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HC107775396104F76B4187E6D98AD5A81"><enum>(G)</enum><text>The Supreme Court has explained that the liberty specially protected by the Due Process Clause includes the right <quote>to direct the education and upbringing of one’s children.</quote> Washington v. Glucksberg, 521 U.S. 702, 720 (1997).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H6D7900639D7F4ECCBB82EA6AC1054EB4"><enum>(H)</enum><text><quote>[W]e have recognized the fundamental right of parents to make decisions concerning the care, custody, and control of their children . . . In light of this extensive precedent, it cannot now be doubted that the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment protects the fundamental right of parents to make decisions concerning the care, custody, and control of their children.</quote> Troxel v. Granville, 530 U.S. 57, 66 (2000) (plurality op.).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H6BDE361BF8AF4F89A4ECA9E23BAF9527"><enum>(I)</enum><text><quote>[T]he Due Process Clause does not permit a State to infringe on the fundamental right of parents to make child rearing decisions simply because a state judge believes a <quote>better</quote> decision could be made.</quote> Troxel, 530 U.S. at 72–73 (plurality op.).</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H8489B6B6255A415CB0E7A2C6BD81596B"><enum>(7)</enum><text>Some decisions of Federal courts have failed to recognize the fundamental right of parents, resulting in an improper standard of judicial review being applied to government conduct that adversely affects parental rights and prerogatives.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H00AF3764BA674E90801E6DF91781F3E0"><enum>(8)</enum><text>Government agencies have increasingly intruded into the legitimate decisions and prerogatives of parents in situations that do not involve abuse or neglect but simply an agency’s disagreement with parenting choices based on decent and honorable religious or philosophical premises.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H29E81BC981A344FB862C11C7FEAD3297"><enum>(9)</enum><text>Government’s involvement in parenting should prioritize the parent’s role as the child’s primary educator and should support, not supplant, the parent’s rights and responsibilities.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HE8C3A526D23448F9A198A006DFC0978C"><enum>(10)</enum><text>Government should not interfere in the decisions and actions of parents without compelling justification.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC1536C42BFFC4C0FB74CD7420CCC3EFF"><enum>(11)</enum><text>The strict scrutiny test used by courts to evaluate cases concerning fundamental rights is the correct standard of review for government actions that interfere with the right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children, and it appropriately balances the interests of parents, children, and government.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="HE9AAB80AD2514231B06ED275DF54BD12"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Purposes</header><text>The purposes of this Act are—</text><paragraph id="H1C3B7B207CC840B1AAD7C1AB0F4210FB"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to protect the right of parents to direct the upbringing of their children as a fundamental right; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H0CD0F34E044E4BD48D46BB380BEB221A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>while protecting the right of parents, to acknowledge that the rights involve responsibilities and specifically that parents have the responsibility for the education, nurture, and upbringing of their children as specified by the Supreme Court in Meyer v. Nebraska, 262 U.S. 390, 400 (1923), Wisconsin v. Yoder, 406 U.S. 205, 232 (1972), and Washington v. Glucksberg, 521 U.S. 702, 720 (1997), and have the high duty to recognize and prepare their children for additional obligations as specified by the Supreme Court in Pierce v. Soc’y of the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus &amp; Mary, 268 U.S. 510, 535 (1925).</text></paragraph></subsection></section><section id="H962403E2B9F54068BFDA37A8227509DB"><enum>3.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="HF68E6DB3C5594158BDDA5A3A2E8038BC"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Government</header><text>The term <term>government</term> includes a branch, department, agency, instrumentality, and official (or other person acting under color of law) of the United States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and each territory and possession of the United States.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H491547237B6D49049C66D68F559240B7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Parent</header><text>The term <term>parent</term> means a biological parent of a child, an adoptive parent of a child, or an individual who has been granted exclusive right and authority over the welfare of a child under State law.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HDF4995FDA2A14FADB5C95A99C3683314"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Child</header><text>The term <term>child</term> means an individual who has not attained 18 years of age.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC1B7A5D1F5AE43CE8111CD3D98D0662C"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Substantial burden</header><text>The term <term>substantial burden</term>—</text><subparagraph id="H7671614BFD4B4866B2953AEEA7CA59C6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>means any action that directly or indirectly constrains, inhibits, curtails, or denies the right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their child or compels any action contrary to the right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their child; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H62A9A578286B433FA7AA6A4CAE7DF399"><enum>(B)</enum><text>includes withholding benefits, assessing criminal, civil, or administrative penalties or damages, or exclusion from governmental programs.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></section><section id="HD934DA7CB6A6498B9DB22A4519E76DFC"><enum>4.</enum><header>Protection of parental rights</header><subsection id="H0D12920312D942CB9D97E217A2532533"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><paragraph id="HF983780211F1461880B29F854E9DDCA0"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Fundamental right</header><text>The liberty of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children is a fundamental right.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H54115A144E7C4C4BA9552893F1A6BF38"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Limits on government interference</header><text>Government shall not substantially burden the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children without demonstrating that the infringement is required by a compelling governmental interest of the highest order as applied to the parent and the child and is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest. The fundamental rights protected include, without limitation, the following rights and responsibilities:</text><subparagraph id="HBED458004721443DA8F3F73380E19471"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To direct the education of the child.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H7F2C25CA0F7241A3B1194EAF6C3A7464"><enum>(B)</enum><text>To direct the moral or religious upbringing of the child.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HE8A0BADA9619423EB6BD3E01C0B5B31A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>To access and review all medical records of the child and to make and consent to all physical and mental health care decisions for the child.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H4C4A2E8A020A4A29B22E6A7AD017D84C"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Effect of this Act on other rights</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Unless legally waived or legally terminated, parents have inalienable rights that are more comprehensive than those listed in this section. This Act does not prescribe all rights of parents, nor does it preempt or foreclose claims or remedies in support of parental rights that are available under any other Federal law, State law, the United States Constitution, or a State constitution.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H826F8603402349DCB8C2EE2C3ACFF021"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exceptions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This section does not apply to a parental action or decision that would result in serious physical injury to the child or that would end life.</text></subsection><subsection id="HF5C3DE6A5AF9403DBF342A7462383D46"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Judicial remedy</header><text>Any parent may raise a violation of this Act as a claim or a defense in an action in a Federal or State court or before an administrative tribunal and obtain appropriate relief against a government. Standing to assert a claim or defense under this section shall be governed by the general rules of standing under article III of the Constitution. </text></subsection></section><section id="HCF504A6A48DF4A05BBB624F9AE9313B4"><enum>5.</enum><header>Attorneys fees</header><subsection id="HE6D05361B32F43BE8FF8430C6346DD6F"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Judicial Proceedings</header><text>Section 722(b) of the Revised Statutes (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1988">42 U.S.C. 1988(b)</external-xref>) is amended by inserting <quote>the Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act,</quote> before <quote>title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964</quote>.</text></subsection><subsection id="HAB7190D937584F5E95A5E4F7C7DC01E3" commented="no"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Administrative Proceedings</header><text>Section 504(b)(1)(C) of title 5, United States Code, is amended by striking <quote>the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993</quote> and inserting <quote>any adjudication under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993 or the Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act</quote>. </text></subsection></section><section id="H86938AEFD08E447EB101311D3DE8848A"><enum>6.</enum><header>Applicability</header><subsection id="H2895FAEF3D504894851F3E894B0F9C6D"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In General</header><text>This Act applies to each Federal law, and the implementation of any such law, whether statutory or otherwise, and whether adopted before or after the date of enactment of this Act.</text></subsection><subsection id="HF3CF8FF41FE54AD186839110C22492AB"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><paragraph id="HC98CF8DD11D64BD8AA4BF9DC7DCB8804"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Additional rights</header><text>The protections of the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children afforded by this Act are in addition to the protections provided under Federal law, State law, and the State and Federal constitutions.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HA8010FF4A17E43B6977B751311CDB35C"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Broad protection</header><text>This Act shall be construed in favor of a broad protection of the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H7B5F4870FF014CF39A410605DBCDDA2F"><enum>(3)</enum><header>No government burden</header><text>Nothing in this Act shall be construed to authorize any government to burden the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H92CEEBB8F8124529ABB9DCFB02EF2CFE" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Subsequently enacted laws</header><text>Federal statutory law adopted after the date of the enactment of this Act is subject to this Act, unless such law explicitly excludes such application by reference to this Act.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></legis-body></bill>

<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">119th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 653</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250123">January 23, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="B001291">Mr. Babin</sponsor> (for himself and <cosponsor name-id="M001218">Mr. McCormick</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HIF00">Committee on Energy and Commerce</committee-name>, and in addition to the Committees on <committee-name committee-id="HJU00">the Judiciary</committee-name>, <committee-name committee-id="HED00">Education and Workforce</committee-name>, <committee-name committee-id="HII00">Natural Resources</committee-name>, and <committee-name committee-id="HWM00">Ways and Means</committee-name>, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned</action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To protect children from medical malpractice in the form of gender transition procedures.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H27940D71FABE44B8836EDC85FB5933A7" style="OLC"> 
<section id="HD3EA7590CC2B401590AE8F102588F280" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protect Minors from Medical Malpractice Act of 2025</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="HFD39D99AAD7E4FA3848ED3AE50B0C4E5"><enum>2.</enum><header>Private right of action for a gender-transition procedure performed on a minor</header> <subsection id="H7CF4E14E0498454BA00FE8EBFC295DF5"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>A medical practitioner, in any circumstance described in subsection (c), who performs a gender-transition procedure on an individual who is less than 18 years of age shall, as described in subsection (b), be liable to the individual if injured (including any physical, psychological, emotional, or physiological harms) by such procedure, related treatment, or the after effects of the procedure or treatment.</text></subsection>
<subsection id="HE327216F71694405A3795ECC184198C6"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Private right of action</header><text>An individual covered by subsection (a) who receives a gender-transition procedure from a medical practitioner (or a representative, including a legal guardian, on behalf of such individual) may, not later than the day that is 30 years after the date on which the individual turns 18 years of age, bring a civil action against such medical practitioner in a court of competent jurisdiction for—</text> <paragraph id="HA88B39A6531E4D8CB001B60238B3B8FE"><enum>(1)</enum><text>declaratory or injunctive relief;</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H160949F9D8AE4EBCBAD99516A3102B6D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>compensatory damages;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HDA4E336064DE40EEA9682FCF0E2E92BE"><enum>(3)</enum><text>punitive damages; and</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H25C8F21A3D7341208F008A18C180187A"><enum>(4)</enum><text>attorney’s fees and costs.</text></paragraph></subsection> <subsection id="H2B1FA293E47B4BDB98AA8A75D54D6CE1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Circumstances</header><text>For the purposes of subsection (a), the circumstances described in this subsection are that—</text>
<paragraph id="HA40B46F0A2B3422295462FC7B258C081"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the medical practitioner or the individual receiving the gender-transition procedure traveled in interstate or foreign commerce, or traveled using a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HBB0ACE695BF3405CBE982B3DC7B989C0"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the medical practitioner used a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H04188E2E98934FF183A466F9FEAC1803"><enum>(3)</enum><text>any payment of any kind was made, directly or indirectly, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="HE5982FC882234CEFBD9D603F717E4FD0"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the medical practitioner transmitted in interstate or foreign commerce any communication relating to or in furtherance of the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means or in any manner, including by computer, mail, wire, or electromagnetic transmission;</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="HB01F05B4DE614CEB8A9252AE346B68F8"><enum>(5)</enum><text>any instrument, item, substance, or other object that has traveled in interstate or foreign commerce was used to perform the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H299AE6B3F66947FE911F30690927EFDB"><enum>(6)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) occurred within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, or any territory or possession of the United States; or</text></paragraph>
<paragraph id="H62C9BF02191D4727A595651DD6ACA55C"><enum>(7)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) otherwise occurred in or affected interstate or foreign commerce.</text></paragraph></subsection></section> <section id="H2506940322384399BF4D69EF2822F244"><enum>3.</enum><header>Preserving freedom of conscience and medical judgement for medical providers</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no provision of Federal law shall require, or be construed to require, a medical practitioner to perform a gender-transition procedure.</text></section>
<section id="H5CE3AADA1A814156A42F53F332DCDA8A"><enum>4.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for certain states</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any State that requires medical practitioners to perform any gender-transition procedure on an individual in the State shall be ineligible to receive any Federal funding from the Department of Health and Human Services.</text></section> <section id="H77211BC5E50F4E72BB5B3F3A83DF9890"><enum>5.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text>
<paragraph id="H9BF2E226B114441884685A5F1697E6F6"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Biological sex</header><text>The term <term>biological sex </term> means the genetic classification of an individual as male or female, as reflected in the organization of the body of such individual for a reproductive role or capacity, such as through sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, and internal and external genitalia present at birth, without regard to the subjective sense of identity of the individual.</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H19AA7E6FD20F46D29135331AA50747A9"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Gender-transition procedure</header> <subparagraph id="H8888AAB2E87A43A5987508474B98B5A8"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> means—</text>
<clause id="H27AE8E2EFDAC4EFCB6F0235509669690"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of puberty-blocking drugs for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex;</text></clause> <clause id="H48B4E2DBBC2D4836AD4491510CCE30B2"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of cross-sex hormones for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex; or</text></clause>
<clause id="H3DA833C69606467EA5DF46D66CA98A3B"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>a surgery to change the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H1EE6A88D9C804DDD8A79D0FB769063B3"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> does not include—</text>
<clause id="H91AB844452A244C2B98A8486144F4221"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an intervention described in subparagraph (A) that is performed on—</text> <subclause id="HA9767BC64F5A4BA381613EA5CEA66C1A"><enum>(I)</enum><text>an individual with biological sex characteristics that are inherently ambiguous, such as those born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or having both ovarian and testicular tissue; or</text></subclause>
<subclause id="HCF73F3DDD8C74B3EBEB57BED2FF178A0"><enum>(II)</enum><text>an individual with respect to whom a physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action, for a biological male or biological female;</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="H6BB82A94AC3547378EA3F838DE7E8019"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused or exacerbated by the performance of an intervention described in subparagraph (A) without regard to whether the intervention was performed in accordance with State or Federal law or whether the intervention is covered by the private right of action under section 2; or</text></clause>
<clause id="H02FD453A709B43C7AF874C9DDB879B18"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HA423A8593AC448609D7EEB8D23DEC50D"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Medical practitioner</header><text>The term <term>medical practitioner</term> means a person who is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized by the laws of a State to administer health care in the ordinary course of the practice of the person’s profession.</text></paragraph></section>
<section id="H45172D3333CD41D59F2D08C07F4A08FE"><enum>6.</enum><header>Effective date</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act.</text></section> </legis-body></bill>
