<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">119th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 742</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250128">January 28, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="M001218">Mr. McCormick</sponsor> (for himself, <cosponsor name-id="C001116">Mr. Clyde</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="L000596">Mrs. Luna</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="F000472">Mr. Scott Franklin of Florida</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="V000134">Ms. Van Duyne</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="F000246">Mr. Fallon</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="C001129">Mr. Collins</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="W000814">Mr. Weber of Texas</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="H001052">Mr. Harris of Maryland</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="G000576">Mr. Grothman</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="G000591">Mr. Guest</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="Z000018">Mr. Zinke</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="B001291">Mr. Babin</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="M001235">Mr. Moore of West Virginia</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="E000071">Mr. Ellzey</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="N000190">Mr. Norman</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="W000806">Mr. Webster of Florida</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="A000375">Mr. Arrington</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="W000829">Mr. Wied</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="R000612">Mr. Rose</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S001189">Mr. Austin Scott of Georgia</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="H001098">Mr. Hamadeh of Arizona</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="B001307">Mr. Baird</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="O000086">Mr. Owens</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="G000589">Mr. Gooden</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="J000304">Mr. Jackson of Texas</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="F000475">Mr. Finstad</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="M001239">Mr. McGuire</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="J000301">Mr. Johnson of South Dakota</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="O000175">Mr. Ogles</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="G000565">Mr. Gosar</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HIF00">Committee on Energy and Commerce</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To prohibit Federal funds from being used to provide certain gender transition procedures to minors.</official-title></form><legis-body id="H00EEC0A23DA540B3BFAD073990144694" style="OLC"> 
<section id="HA3C2542BA51741FFBB51A92E2142C00B" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protecting Resources Of Taxpayers to Eliminate Childhood Transgender Surgeries Act of 2025</short-title></quote> or the <quote><short-title>PROTECTS Act of 2025</short-title></quote>.</text></section> <section id="H0DAA8ABD056A47F099ABDC40DDA2F4AA"><enum>2.</enum><header>Prohibiting Federal funds from being used to provide certain gender transition procedures to minors</header> <subsection id="HD7E2F5EAD68C4FD5AFA0D2B533AAAF31"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no Federal funds may be used or otherwise made available to provide or refer for a specified gender transition procedure to an individual under the age of 18 or to reimburse any entity for providing such a procedure to such an individual.</text></subsection> 
<subsection id="HEBA78E7E8FDE40519B91B1F23C8DDF76"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Specified gender transition procedure defined</header> 
<paragraph id="HB6BB4DE6DB324937B12248B3DA1EBA51"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>For purposes of this paragraph, except as provided in paragraph (2), the term <quote>specified gender transition procedure</quote> means, with respect to an individual, any of the following when performed for the purpose of intentionally changing the body of such individual to no longer correspond to their sex:</text> <subparagraph id="HD75B553BA0FC48ACA74EBE5440531918"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Performing any surgery, including—</text> 
<clause id="HC8920BA970E64F3BAE33CC36DE42DA4E"><enum>(i)</enum><text>castration;</text></clause> <clause id="H65AFCCA27F1440D1A9A21385BBF44110"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>orchiectomy;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HA8F18B4E1529402BBFB77E99CA3511ED"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>scrotoplasty;</text></clause> <clause id="H136FCD860FB04FDE9DC02FC7EAB30F15"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>vasectomy;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H3AEF65A88D9E490B9EC859FF62502402"><enum>(v)</enum><text>hysterectomy;</text></clause> <clause id="H139D76980C3342198422A00A4CB62730"><enum>(vi)</enum><text>oophorectomy;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBC5EF019BCD44B4F86C11D1590E1246E"><enum>(vii)</enum><text>ovariectomy;</text></clause> <clause id="HDDA9796FF8324DB29FE8BCFEBFB8A72A"><enum>(viii)</enum><text>metoidioplasty;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H8964335681C94894B0D28A73C3ADEAA6"><enum>(ix)</enum><text>penectomy;</text></clause> <clause id="H1FDA38EE83BB4856A0468B5D87EC6F4E"><enum>(x)</enum><text>phalloplasty;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HD60855FC024548C2BDF663CABD79B820"><enum>(xi)</enum><text>vaginoplasty;</text></clause> <clause id="H0B88E2E7EBA5460CA62D7E6FAE4FF35A"><enum>(xii)</enum><text>vaginectomy;</text></clause> 
<clause id="H9157675A1C934A00BDAD24935B10DAEE"><enum>(xiii)</enum><text>vulvoplasty;</text></clause> <clause id="HFEFDB03E110D46F3A5B91B5AB279E650"><enum>(xiv)</enum><text>reduction thyrochondroplasty;</text></clause> 
<clause id="HCB191FD9D76442C59959660666BA576B"><enum>(xv)</enum><text>chondrolaryngoplasty;</text></clause> <clause id="H5028AAC2D1A74BFD81DA3ABC11C6C555"><enum>(xvi)</enum><text>mastectomy; and</text></clause> 
<clause id="HBDAE2AC5AF5D408EA37619FED0774351"><enum>(xvii)</enum><text>any plastic, cosmetic, or aesthetic surgery that feminizes or masculinizes the facial or other body features of an individual.</text></clause></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9D1A89A3C07E4849AC9E44C8AA50F1C3"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Any placement of chest implants to create feminine breasts.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H4E1674B40F1D46ACB349F3E0F03436C6"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Any placement of fat or artificial implants in the gluteal region.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H9BD547A0978A46ED9FCF6DD18D828CAF"><enum>(D)</enum><text>Administering, supplying, prescribing, dispensing, distributing, or otherwise conveying to an individual medications, including—</text> 
<clause id="HB56FC87762B142DD96AAED8076CC0562"><enum>(i)</enum><text>gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues or other puberty-blocking drugs to stop or delay normal puberty; and</text></clause> <clause id="H5C4401AA439949B485BA8334C22CEE6E"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">testosterone, estrogen, or other androgens to an individual at doses that are supraphysiologic than would normally be produced endogenously in a healthy individual of the same age and sex.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="HCB7D453F77C64F6A95512FEB84A6F572"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>Paragraph (1) shall not apply to the following when furnished to an individual by a health care provider with the consent of such individual’s parent or legal guardian:</text> <subparagraph id="H01F51F7E003A43BAA02A9415B65E396F"><enum>(A)</enum><text>Puberty suppression or blocking prescription drugs for the purpose of normalizing puberty for an individual experiencing precocious puberty.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="H56D7ED7CF40E42D58848855ACF3DB960"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Appropriate and medically necessary procedures or treatments to correct for—</text> <clause id="H0C5D3A8CEAEA4FBAA29166D25BA5233D"><enum>(i)</enum><text>a medically verifiable genetic disorder of sex development, including—</text> 
<subclause id="H6AC41C382EC546B9A244393EA4E6993B"><enum>(I)</enum><text>46,XX chromosomes with virilization;</text></subclause> <subclause id="H2A356157BA0D4DEAB4780FBE10CBEA1A"><enum>(II)</enum><text>46,XY chromosomes with undervirilization; and</text></subclause> 
<subclause id="H64A5D11DD7F34F6B9CC5F9F9E20E3FA4"><enum>(III)</enum><text>both ovarian and testicular tissue;</text></subclause></clause> <clause id="H6B952D2F0D3F44FFA333275C6A8422EE"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex hormone action, if determined to be abnormal by a physician through genetic or biochemical testing; or</text></clause> 
<clause id="HD3F04AB2F323409099CBA71D4F017879"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>infection, disease, injury, or disorder caused or exacerbated by a previous procedure described in paragraph (1), or a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of a major bodily function unless the procedure is performed, not including procedures performed for the alleviation of mental distress.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HF8A9C19DE52B4FB89E68B052BACB6A50"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Certain terms</header><text>For purposes of this section:</text> 
<subparagraph id="H42496E2FBA8E4F01B0152DFB788B2179"><enum>(A)</enum><header>Sex</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>sex</quote>, when referring to individual’s sex, shall be understood to refer to either male or female, as biologically determined.</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="HF78E69C9E14C466BB531B00442C3F28A"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Female</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>female</quote>, when referring to a natural person, means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes eggs for fertilization.</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HD01782E4CA16401BADA2717FF14E65A5"><enum>(C)</enum><header>Male</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <quote>male</quote>, when referring to a natural person, means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section> </legis-body></bill>

<distribution-code display="yes">I</distribution-code><congress display="yes">119th CONGRESS</congress><session display="yes">1st Session</session><legis-num display="yes">H. R. 800</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250128">January 28, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="M001216">Mr. Mills</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HGO00">Committee on Oversight and Government Reform</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title display="yes">To enact into law the executive order relating to ending diversity, equity, and inclusion programs in the Federal Government, and for other purposes.</official-title></form><legis-body id="HD782A11A28A74CFB93EFE857365EFBED" style="OLC"><section id="H29E9E5BDB60647389B491645EF7994E6" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>DEI to DIE Act</short-title></quote>. </text></section><section id="H08A1C82B29694E569784BD424277326B"><enum>2.</enum><header>Elimination of diversity, equity, and inclusion in Federal Government</header><subsection id="H7DC4BE0F93C14153A151C718835AA4DA"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Findings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Congress finds the following:</text><paragraph id="H7D6D7C520B8E4996A62F30B0BF5B344D"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The Biden Administration forced illegal and immoral discrimination programs, going by the name <quote>diversity, equity, and inclusion</quote> (in this Act referred to as <quote>DEI</quote>), into virtually all aspects of the Federal Government, in areas ranging from airline safety to the military.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H067137D22F9A426282C845E1570DBCA1"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This was a concerted effort stemming from President Biden’s first day in office, when he issued Executive Order 13985, <quote>Advancing Racial Equity and Support for Underserved Communities Through the Federal Government</quote>.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HFD99FE6BCF5D4E5F815900D68EF63E03"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Pursuant to Executive Order 13985 and follow-on orders, nearly every Federal agency and entity submitted <quote>Equity Action Plans</quote> to detail the ways that they have furthered DEIs infiltration of the Federal Government.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HEA8D245D816B45BB8B25843E9D7B063B"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The public release of these plans demonstrated immense public waste and shameful discrimination.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HB145AE4933644BEF893B6B15D1952B90"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">That ends today. Americans deserve a Government committed to serving every person with equal dignity and respect, and to expending precious taxpayer resources only on making America great.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H0C113FB10C564C27B5BFB044A9414105"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Elimination</header><paragraph id="H1D79597AC3DB4C3BB1B4E2AF80F925E2"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>The Director of the Office of Management and Budget (in this Act referred to as <quote>OMB</quote>), assisted by the Attorney General and the Director of the Office of Personnel Management (in this Act referred to as <quote>OPM</quote>), shall coordinate the termination of all discriminatory programs, including illegal diversity, equity, and inclusion (in this Act referred to as <quote>DEI</quote>) and diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (in this Act referred to as <quote>DEIA</quote>) mandates, policies, programs, preferences, and activities in the Federal Government, under whatever name they appear.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HF58552256F664D17A115724B72CBB96D"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Application</header><text>To carry out paragraph (1), the Director of OPM, with the assistance of the Attorney General as requested, shall review and revise, as appropriate, all existing Federal employment practices, union contracts, and training policies or programs to comply with this Act. Federal employment practices, including Federal employee performance reviews, shall reward individual initiative, skills, performance, and hard work and shall not under any circumstances consider DEI or DEIA factors, goals, policies, mandates, or requirements.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H2C072A1463A2412A970A60C34542875B"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Required actions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Each agency, department, or commission head, in consultation with the Attorney General, the Director of OMB, and the Director of OPM, as appropriate, shall take the following actions not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act:</text><paragraph id="H7CEF62F0DC554E4097C8F66D1D117087"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Terminate, to the maximum extent allowed by law, all DEI, DEIA, and <quote>environmental justice</quote> offices and positions (including <quote>Chief Diversity Officer</quote> positions); all <quote>equity action plans</quote>, <quote>equity</quote> actions, initiatives, or programs, <quote>equity-related</quote> grants or contracts; and all DEI or DEIA performance requirements for employees, contractors, or grantees.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H5E8F808B25524537AF268E1C7ADD42F4"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Provide the Director of the OMB with a list of all—</text><subparagraph id="H2D2E7D9E7457485989E718A943624CD6"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">agency or department DEI, DEIA, or <quote>environmental justice</quote> positions, committees, programs, services, activities, budgets, and expenditures in existence on November 4, 2024, and an assessment of whether these positions, committees, programs, services, activities, budgets, and expenditures have been misleadingly relabeled in an attempt to preserve their pre-November 4, 2024 function; </text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H6EA2659CCAB14012B21957B39795C479"><enum>(B)</enum><text>Federal contractors who have provided DEI training or DEI training materials to agency or department employees; and </text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HF058546D729C4CDDB40AFF845A35FDB9"><enum>(C)</enum><text>Federal grantees who received Federal funding to provide or advance DEI, DEIA, or <quote>environmental justice</quote> programs, services, or activities since January 20, 2021.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H0297CFD0401E4C26A50DD25B581BCE18"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Direct the deputy agency or department head to—</text><subparagraph id="H679998F437A443C39C40A8212F1AAEFA"><enum>(A)</enum><text>assess the operational impact (including the number of new DEI hires) and cost of the prior administration’s DEI, DEIA, and <quote>environmental justice</quote> programs and policies; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H0C03BF8894F243D5B4A9F5D919F7E4B6"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">recommend actions, such as congressional notifications under section 530D of title 28, United States Code, to align agency or department programs, activities, policies, regulations, guidance, employment practices, enforcement activities, contracts (including set-asides), grants, consent orders, and litigating positions with the policy of equal dignity and respect identified in subsection (a) of this Act. The agency or department head and the Director of OMB shall jointly ensure that the deputy agency or department head has the authority and resources needed to carry out this Act.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H4147FE9693D3482494D21AB7FC13553E"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Meetings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To inform and advise the President, so that he may formulate appropriate and effective civil-rights policies for the Executive Branch, the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy shall convene a monthly meeting attended by the Director of OMB, the Director of OPM, and each deputy agency or department head to—</text><paragraph id="HD4AE63EB87824F1D8639B6E36F5E5B94" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(1)</enum><text>hear reports on the prevalence and the economic and social costs of DEI, DEIA, and <quote>environmental justice</quote> in agency or department programs, activities, policies, regulations, guidance, employment practices, enforcement activities, contracts (including set-asides), grants, consent orders, and litigating positions;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HE98107C62E7C45188C43A89BCE313217"><enum>(2)</enum><text>discuss any barriers to measures to comply with this Act; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H2F1CC9C88BFD4185B08DB2AB05A8D187"><enum>(3)</enum><text>monitor and track agency and department progress and identify potential areas for additional Presidential or legislative action to advance the policy of equal dignity and respect.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H5CE33264A41847B2929C9D0550AE61B0"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Severability</header><text>If any provision of this Act, or the application of any provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, the remainder of this Act and the application of its provisions to any other persons or circumstances shall not be affected.</text></subsection></section></legis-body></bill>

display-inline="no-display-inline">The Civil Rights Act of 1964 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2000a">42 U.S.C. 2000a et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following:</text><quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H786B0961BDAB48B1A9335B89103285E0"><title id="HEE7EA20FFAFD4AA6B2CBF6A0839E4E87" style="OLC"><enum>XII</enum><header>Prohibited diversity, equity or inclusion practice defined</header><section display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H124845855287474DBC13EA2BE6C7772F"><enum>1201.</enum><header>Prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">For purposes of references to this section, the term <quote>prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice</quote> means—</text><paragraph id="H11C0E277584243019E2D35FDAE3CB5E1"><enum>(1)</enum><text>discriminating for or against any person on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, religion, biological sex, or national origin;</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" id="HB3A837B107B54C50A1EF9E08C5CF0C67"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">requiring as a condition of employment, as a condition for promotion or advancement, or as a condition for speaking, making a presentation, or submitting written materials, that an employee undergo training, education, or coursework, or other pedagogy, that asserts that a particular race, color, ethnicity, religion, biological sex, or national origin is inherently or systemically superior or inferior, oppressive or oppressed, or privileged or unprivileged; or</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H1310A9DB5F7A4055981BC9013C8BBF92" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">requiring as a condition of employment, as a condition for promotion or advancement, or as a condition for speaking, making a presentation, or submitting written materials, the signing of or assent to a statement, code of conduct, work program, or plan, or similar device that requires assent by the employee that a particular race, color, ethnicity, religion, biological sex, or national origin is inherently or systemically superior or inferior, oppressive or oppressed, or privileged or unprivileged.</text></paragraph></section></title><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section><title id="H54BABF8CCBD4414CAB18853FC571521D"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text><external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" parsable-cite="usc-chapter/5/10">Chapter 10</external-xref> of title 5, United States Code (commonly known as the <quote>Federal Advisory Committee Act</quote>), is amended by adding at the end the following:</text><quoted-block style="OLC" id="H0E4211F79B5E4CF0A6AEEB37A0D3B377"><section id="H97F42039DBA9447AB94D8DA722CD9FD4"><enum>1015.</enum><header>Diversity, equity, and inclusion practices</header><subsection id="H0BED112B23404612B7BC95EC829D5622"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Prohibited diversity, equity, and inclusion practice defined</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In this section, the term <term>prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice</term> has the meaning that term has in section 1201 of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. </text></subsection><subsection id="H8C5BCD0B244545C4809C0D80018979F0"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Prohibition</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The following may not authorize, permit, or implement a prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice with respect to any advisory committee established by the head of an agency:</text><paragraph id="H2B7CD9706AD9484EBC823F74935C02F4"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Administrator.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HB03D1DA4041A4F22884E2760F7D4C49B"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The agency head.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HFD0EAF9FAD99401B93510250F92EE6BF"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The chair of the advisory committee. </text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1BD118F5B00A458E91BEF7605039F2F6"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The advisory committee.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H66E38CD0122B4C618CA8852F07A7C349"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Termination of committee</header><paragraph id="H5EEDCB42CA5A4D6BA942477033D022FE"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Finding by Administrator</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">With respect to an advisory committee, if the Administrator finds that the applicable agency head, chair of the advisory committee, or the advisory committee authorized, permitted, or implemented a prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice, then the advisory committee shall terminate not later than 30 days after the Administrator makes such finding.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H85CF252843D94937BE2867317A9B8E60"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Finding by Inspector General</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">With respect to an advisory committee, if the Inspector General for the agency that established the advisory committee finds that the applicable agency head, chair of the advisory committee, or the advisory committee authorized, permitted, or implemented a prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice, then the advisory committee shall terminate not later than 30 days after the Inspector General makes such finding.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="HB7C820BFDF20493EBDE96A54A7E9B5F3"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Action</header><paragraph id="H7FEB01F8B1854440A2B757664A230873"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Any person may bring an action in any United States district court seeking a determination that the Administrator, any agency head, any chair of an advisory committee, or any advisory committee authorized, permitted, or implemented a prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice with respect to an advisory committee.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H25F628CBE840408AA9ED8FBA74E46ED9"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Order directing termination of advisory committee</header><text>If after an evidentiary hearing, a court determines that the defendant authorized, permitted, or implemented a prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice, the court shall issue an order directing the Administrator to immediately terminate that advisory committee.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H1C34E489E0794731BA3B6D0E59E21E2A"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Additional awards</header><text>In an action brought under this subsection in which the plaintiff prevails, the court may award—</text><subparagraph id="HAE8F7CE7BC6A454CAF98DF39E0926388"><enum>(A)</enum><text>a Writ of Mandamus or other equitable or declaratory relief;</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HF002FE1DF6DD4A61977E46D4E509A5D6"><enum>(B)</enum><text>a minimum of $1,000 per violation per day;</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HEFF6ABA4F7F84B4D9CBD1BFA1ED0A5E0"><enum>(C)</enum><text>reasonable attorney’s fees and litigation costs;</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H4349E3DAC0E5463BAB72C81BEEFAE046"><enum>(D)</enum><text>compensatory damages; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H07AB879EA4D44099AFC8BDCFB0BF278F"><enum>(E)</enum><text>all other appropriate relief.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subsection><subsection commented="no" RES. 224</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250314">March 14, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="M001211">Mrs. Miller of Illinois</sponsor> (for herself, <cosponsor name-id="H001052">Mr. Harris of Maryland</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="L000578">Mr. LaMalfa</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="O000175">Mr. Ogles</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="B001291">Mr. Babin</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="R000612">Mr. Rose</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="C001120">Mr. Crenshaw</cosponsor>) submitted the following resolution; which was referred to the <committee-name committee-id="HIF00">Committee on Energy and Commerce</committee-name>, and in addition to the Committee on <committee-name committee-id="HJU00">the Judiciary</committee-name>, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned</action-desc></action><legis-type>RESOLUTION</legis-type><official-title display="yes">Expressing support for the recognition of <quote>Detransition Awareness Day</quote>.</official-title></form><preamble> 
<whereas><text>Whereas many individuals who have undergone sex trait modification interventions later regret such interventions;</text></whereas> <whereas><text>Whereas the number of individuals seeking to reverse such interventions has risen significantly, highlighting a need for greater understanding and support;</text></whereas> 
<whereas><text>Whereas many individuals who have undergone sex trait modification interventions face irreversible physical changes and suffer from a range of health complications, including genital mutilation, sexual dysfunction, infertility, osteoporosis, and psychological distress;</text></whereas> <whereas><text>Whereas there is a critical need for comprehensive, noninvasive, and evidence-based care for individuals experiencing discomfort with their sex that focuses on mental health support rather than solely on physiological interventions; and</text></whereas> 
<whereas><text>Whereas individuals who have undergone sex trait modification interventions and have returned to living in the reality of their sex often encounter retribution and hateful rhetoric for publicly announcing regret and face barriers to receiving appropriate medical, psychological, and social support after making the choice to detransition, including lack of insurance coverage for corrective or reparative treatments: Now, therefore, be it </text></whereas> </preamble><resolution-body style="traditional" id="H09D97D7F55A14E469C2BDDA8F4B6D73C"> <section display-inline="yes-display-inline" section-type="undesignated-section" id="H4051871DE175422890E0CA5FC73C2A80"><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">That the House of Representatives—</text> 
<paragraph id="HD9EA1F1D1EDF4013A2EFAA6E7967CC88"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">supports the recognition of <quote>Detransition Awareness Day</quote> to acknowledge the experiences of individuals who have detransitioned, or are in the process of detransitioning, and have returned to living in the reality of their sex, and to foster public and legislative understanding of the challenges of such individuals;</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H30E17E92A0C244D1A0447A9C6F85EFC6"><enum>(2)</enum><text>urges the development and implementation of policies that—</text> 
<subparagraph id="H553200DB58BA4A2C9CEA85FCDFEF0662"><enum>(A)</enum><text>ensure comprehensive mental health services are available for individuals who experience discomfort with their sex; and</text></subparagraph> <subparagraph id="H4C03FFD173504890A54FC3B42E24950C"><enum>(B)</enum><text>advocate for informed consent processes that fully disclose the risks of sex trait modification interventions, including the potential for regret and the irreversible nature of such interventions;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H65DA777650864F6D9618CE69B30AD4C8"><enum>(3)</enum><text>calls for legislative action to—</text> <subparagraph id="H985F7C0467A2444CAC38C575362E3AE6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>extend the statute of limitations for claims related to medical malpractice or negligence in providing sex trait modification interventions to recognize the delayed realization of harm in many cases; and</text></subparagraph> 
<subparagraph id="HCE693BF2372A4A6EA38EA4CF25878447"><enum>(B)</enum><text>remove any existing caps on damages for individuals harmed by sex trait modification interventions to ensure adequate compensation for both physical and psychological injuries;</text></subparagraph></paragraph> <paragraph id="HD3C490774B364237B34B53D8A8FD3D75"><enum>(4)</enum><text>requests that the Department of Health and Human Services conduct a review of current literature regarding care for individuals struggling with discomfort due to their sex, promulgate new guidelines, as determined necessary, to promote ethical medical standards and practices that do not involve physiologically invasive practices that attempt to alter the sex traits of an individual, and revise guidelines to better protect patient rights and health;</text></paragraph> 
<paragraph id="H23584F0991944681B258181D585D2BFC"><enum>(5)</enum><text>commends individuals who have detransitioned, or are in the process of detransitioning, and have returned to living in the reality of their sex for their courage in sharing their stories and working towards better care and understanding for those in similar situations; and</text></paragraph> <paragraph id="H7D8B6CA52A534CA3B2C32C84DD6F0CC2"><enum>(6)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">encourages all States to adopt similar resolutions and initiatives to support such individuals and to ensure that all medical interventions are conducted according to the highest ethical standards.</text></paragraph> </section> 
</resolution-body></resolution>

skills;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas policies allowing for the inclusion of men in women’s sports have no basis in biological fact or valid medical research;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas providing equal athletic opportunities in sports to women is impossible without single-sex teams and competitions reserved exclusively for female athletes;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas, without separate single-sex teams and competitions based on biological sex for men and women, men will dominate competitive sports where size, strength, and speed are factors, depriving female athletes of athletic and academic opportunities;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas the biological differences between men and women have led to women being injured by men competing in women’s sports;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas, since 2017, men have won at least 24 professional women’s sports titles and an innumerable number of unreported titles at the middle school, high school, and collegiate levels;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas, in 2018, at least 300 high school-aged boys in the United States ran the 400-meter dash faster than the most decorated female Olympic champion in the world has run it in her lifetime;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas Executive Order 14201 (90 Fed. Reg. 9279; relating to keeping men out of women’s sports) emphasizes opposition to male competitive participation in women’s sports as <quote>a matter of safety, fairness, dignity, and truth</quote>; and</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas the week of June 22 through June 28 is <quote>National Women’s Sports Week</quote>: Now, therefore, be it</text></whereas></preamble><resolution-body style="traditional" id="HA295CA4147CD47DEA2F60DB244D6331B"><section display-inline="yes-display-inline" section-type="undesignated-section" id="H965BA8AE63B348F9B0AFFB95239725D7"><enum/><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">That the House of Representatives supports—</text><paragraph id="HA1163F63E6DD43B2AF2F6EA09A8F8C62"><enum>(1)</enum><text>observing <quote>National Women’s Sports Week</quote> to recognize—</text><subparagraph id="H76757A8C9DB7412B8BD9882F50DFA321"><enum>(A)</enum><text>the incredible expansion of opportunities for female athletes since the enactment of title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1681">20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.</external-xref>); and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HDF373653C0EB4A8382F1E54737D07BCE"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the role of the provisions of law described in subparagraph (A) in guaranteeing equal athletic opportunities for members of both sexes; and</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="HF175EDDD36C94D4C87109494B08D8F16"><enum>(2)</enum><text>marking the observance of National Women’s Sports Week with—</text><subparagraph id="HF96F047FBFF34B228724F71D3600F3EE"><enum>(A)</enum><text>appropriate programs and activities that—</text><clause id="H255C729F7BA8464291FE376F3BB3B250"><enum>(i)</enum><text>celebrate the contributions of individual female athletes in the United States;</text></clause><clause id="H12B785079FBB4B0DB2E9249889994305"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>honor the coaches and parents who support female athletes in the United States;</text></clause><clause id="H6401E63EA8E54CC093244EB8418EA162"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>promote equal access to athletic opportunities for members of both sexes; and</text></clause><clause id="HEA5204BC2F394D5F96F52FC48FA549BF"><enum>(iv)</enum><text>support the commitment of the United States to supporting female athletes; and</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HF534271A6FF54D5AA0CEA965B0F46A3E"><enum>(B)</enum><text>legislative efforts to protect single-sex sports.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></section></resolution-body></resolution>

    <legis-body display-enacting-clause="yes-display-enacting-clause">
        <section id="id13A01D313E5349C0BCC08347D735015F" section-type="section-one">
            <enum>1.</enum>
            <header>Short title</header>
 <text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>No Subsidies for Gender Transition Procedures Act</short-title></quote>.</text>
        </section>
        <section section-type="subsequent-section" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id19291ee0de2443a28babe6c4de2b6bcf">
            <enum>2.</enum>
            <header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Denial of medical expense tax
                deduction</header>
            <subsection id="idF34A1C336D0B484F8C49A68610370432">
                <enum>(a)</enum>
                <header>In general</header>
 <text>Subsection (d) of <external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/26/213">section 213</external-xref> of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:</text>
                <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id2BD1676B54A24E9EB38734E74C2E2857">
                    <paragraph id="idA2C1CA87D39D4B7ABFE37490E6F19A10">
                        <enum>(12)</enum>
                        <header>Expenses relating to gender transition</header>
                        <subparagraph id="id77A796402AC44581ABB3AA467BBF6BE2">
                            <enum>(A)</enum>
                            <header>In general</header>
 <text>The term <term>medical care</term> does not include any gender transition procedure.</text>
                        </subparagraph>
                        <subparagraph id="idB8729B7351D5444F92DE4B7B4B7D7D7D">
                            <enum>(B)</enum>
                            <header>Definitions</header>
 <text>For purposes of this paragraph—</text> <clause id="id33a80afcd82141e986eff5bd00f81c64"> <enum>(i)</enum> <header>Gender transition procedure</header> <subclause id="id3c0c4d5f98bb4acb8b8c5bf385c00576"> <enum>(I)</enum> <header>In general</header> <text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> means any hormonal or surgical intervention for the purpose of gender transition, including—</text>
                                    <item id="id9d7fdcc8cc45472494bb835c8d05e5e1">
                                        <enum>(aa)</enum>
 <text>the provision of gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists or other puberty-suppression drugs or puberty-blocking drugs to stop or delay normally-timed puberty in an individual who does not identify as his or her sex,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id2d293ba613144a97a87b874a37e55033">
                                        <enum>(bb)</enum>
 <text>the provision of testosterone, estrogen, progesterone, or other androgen blockers to an individual at doses which are supraphysiologic to what would normally be produced endogenously in a healthy individual of the same age and sex, with the intent to align an individual's physical appearance with an identity that differs from his or her sex,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ided1dd0c3581a481d9ca33995141d5d6d">
                                        <enum>(cc)</enum>
 <text>surgical procedures that attempt to transform an individual's physical appearance to align with an identity that differs from his or her sex or that attempt to alter or remove an individual's sexual organs to minimize or destroy their natural biological functions,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item id="idc8f5af445ed94ba19695fcb15d4aa986">
                                        <enum>(dd)</enum>
 <text>castration, vasectomy, penectomy, orchiectomy, vaginoplasty, clitoroplasty, vulvoplasty, mastectomy, hysterectomy, oophorectomy, ovariectomy, reconstruction of the fixed part of the urethra with or without metoidioplasty or phalloplasty, metoidioplasty, phalloplasty, vaginectomy, scrotoplasty, implantation of erection or testicular prostheses, reduction thyrochondroplasty, chondrolaryngoplasty, tubal ligation, sterilization, augmentation mammoplasty, placement of chest implants to create feminine breasts, placement of fat or artificial implants in the gluteal region, liposuction, lipofilling, voice surgery, hair reconstruction, pectoral implants, any plastic, cosmetic, or aesthetic surgery which feminizes or masculinizes the facial or other physiological features of an individual, and any removal of any otherwise healthy or non-diseased body part or tissue.</text>
                                    </item>
                                </subclause>
                                <subclause id="ida6ecdc46d20a48cc8752bcb9bd39b9eb">
                                    <enum>(II)</enum>
                                    <header>Exclusions</header>
 <text>The term <term>gender transition procedure</term> does not include, when furnished to an individual by a health care provider with the consent of such individual (or, if applicable, such individual’s parents or legal guardian)—</text>
                                    <item id="id787efb7100074ffd9e64fb10deda7b32">
                                        <enum>(aa)</enum>
 <text>services to individuals born with a medically verifiable disorder of sex development, including an individual with external sex characteristics which are irresolvably ambiguous, such as an individual born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, an individual born with 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or an individual born having both ovarian and testicular tissue,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item id="id771aeaec4c0c44ea83c4fccc94a58d2c">
                                        <enum>(bb)</enum>
 <text>services relating to any other physician-diagnosed disorder of sexual development with respect to which the physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action for a healthy male or female of the same age,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item id="id9501a8e7b56845bcb1922bcecd6378d4" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline">
                                        <enum>(cc)</enum>
 <text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder caused or exacerbated by the performance of gender transition procedures, without regard to whether the gender transition procedure was performed in accordance with State and Federal law or whether the gender transition procedure is treated as medical care under this section,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item id="id713045bad369430f8701ab49e675bf8b">
                                        <enum>(dd)</enum>
 <text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness (but not mental, behavioral, or emotional distress or a mental, behavioral, or emotional disorder) which would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed to alleviate said physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id7cfcd18752084de0b79356ac01442010">
                                        <enum>(ee)</enum>
 <text>procedures to restore or reconstruct the body of the individual in order to correspond to the individual's sex after one or more previous gender transition procedures, which may include the removal of a pseudo phallus or breast augmentation,</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item id="id67955ba3109945a08721378b1555c4fb">
                                        <enum>(ff)</enum>
 <text>puberty suppression or puberty-blocking prescription drugs for the purpose of normalizing puberty for a minor experiencing precocious puberty, or</text>
                                    </item>
                                    <item id="id67705788dd0e4387afb6e8d4377f2746">
                                        <enum>(gg)</enum>
 <text>male circumcision.</text> </item> </subclause> </clause> <clause id="id1efd4e7c915f47b4bb6aec5e054b5771"> <enum>(ii)</enum> <header>Gender transition</header> <text>The term <term>gender transition</term> means the process by which an individual goes from identifying with or presenting as his or her sex to identifying with or presenting as a self-proclaimed identity which does not correspond with or is different from his or her sex, and may be accompanied by social, legal, or physical changes. </text>
                            </clause>
                            <clause id="idefdc7474692943ab9ba44ef41f8d548c" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline">
                                <enum>(iii)</enum>
                                <header>Sex</header>
 <text>The term <term>sex</term>, when referring to an individual’s sex, means either male or female, as biologically determined. </text>
                            </clause>
                            <clause id="idaa6f0e4d8807479c855dfbde6d7d126f">
                                <enum>(iv)</enum>
                                <header>Female</header>
 <text>The term <term>female</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means a person belonging, at conception, to the sex characterized by a reproductive system with the biological function of producing eggs (ova). </text>
                            </clause>
                            <clause id="ida3a97ada265d4a51b25710395071cae4">
                                <enum>(v)</enum>
                                <header>Male</header>
 <text>The term <term>male</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means a person belonging, at conception, to the biological sex characterized by a reproductive system with the biological function of producing sperm.</text>
                            </clause>
                        </subparagraph>
                    </paragraph>
                    <after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block>
                </quoted-block>
            </subsection>
            <subsection id="id734CE60FBECB4CC9B10D120FAF0DC64D">
                <enum>(b)</enum>
                <header>Effective date</header>
 <text>The amendment made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after the date of the enactment of this Act.</text>
            </subsection>

        <section id="id6fe43a07cd7e4c37a04a56888b0572be">
            <enum>3.</enum>
            <header>Prohibiting Federal medicaid funding for gender transition procedures</header>
            <subsection id="id9a18e85b409f4b95a09653ea7f7d6018">
                <enum>(a)</enum>
                <header>In general</header>
 <text>Section 1903(i) of the Social Security Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1396b">42 U.S.C. 1396b(i)</external-xref>) is amended—</text>
                <paragraph id="ide45fdf456bf148e884ed7febfad8be44">
                    <enum>(1)</enum>
 <text>in paragraph (26), by striking <quote>; or</quote> and inserting a semicolon;</text>
                </paragraph>
                <paragraph id="id68d317ab32a04d98acfdcc07086bb3cb">
                    <enum>(2)</enum>
 <text>in paragraph (27), by striking the period at the end and inserting <quote>; or</quote>;</text>
                </paragraph>
                <paragraph id="id438b4c3da6624fdaa0c37b6744a62299">
                    <enum>(3)</enum>
 <text>by inserting after paragraph (27) the following new paragraph:</text> <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id5c69e8929e534c519e364a7d6f5e16f6"> <paragraph id="ida303edb580654443b5f6ab9aebc6dc75"> <enum>(28)</enum> <text>with respect to any amounts expended for any specified gender transition procedure (as defined in section 1905(kk)) to an individual enrolled in a State plan under this title (or a waiver of such plan), including any amounts expended for the administration of a State program that furnishes any such procedure.</text>
                        </paragraph>
                        <after-quoted-block>; and</after-quoted-block>
                    </quoted-block>
                </paragraph>
                <paragraph id="id37342b9ad1ce4645b786d15ce0c6212a">
                    <enum>(4)</enum>
 <text>in the flush left matter at the end, by striking <quote>and (18),</quote> and inserting <quote>(18), and (28)</quote>.</text>
                </paragraph>
            </subsection>
            <subsection id="idef5e44f2ea1a47f49d2ce7b8332a3a32">
                <enum>(b)</enum>
                <header>Prohibiting Federal medicaid funding for gender transition
                    procedures</header>
 <text>Section 1905 of the Social Security Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1396d">42 U.S.C. 1396d</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:</text>
                <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id5F04DE6F4DC54B22B063C08AB4F9BB85">
                    <subsection id="id2fd0d010e4aa48e0b0a7836d669749c5">
                        <enum>(kk)</enum>
                        <header>Prohibiting Federal medicaid funding for specified gender transition
                            procedures</header>
                        <paragraph id="ide946fead5b164f07a84cca7e808cb21e">
                            <enum>(1)</enum>
                            <header>Specified gender transition procedures defined</header>
 <text>For purposes of section 1903(i)(28), except as provided in paragraph (2), the term <term>specified gender transition procedure</term> means, with respect to an individual, any hormonal or surgical intervention for the purpose of gender transition, including—</text>
                            <subparagraph id="idb40c6658f4144805aa3c0861a1d14ada">
                                <enum>(A)</enum>
 <text>the provision of gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists or other puberty suppression drugs or puberty-blocking drugs to stop or delay normally timed puberty in an individual who does not identify as his or her sex;</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id41da1a9d19e04a0fae205825def5a068">
                                <enum>(B)</enum>
 <text>the provision of testosterone, estrogen, progesterone, or other androgen blockers to an individual at doses which are supraphysiologic to what would normally be produced endogenously in a healthy individual of the same age and sex, with the intent to align an individual’s physical appearance with an identity that differs from his or her sex;</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id3d194c9ddb2944388e08e5d11718b267">
                                <enum>(C)</enum>
 <text>surgical procedures that attempt to transform an individual’s physical appearance to align with an identity that differs from his or her sex or that attempt to alter or remove an individual’s sexual organs to minimize or destroy their natural biological functions; or</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id64068d1e36a748a3884819c8cf40ac10">
                                <enum>(D)</enum>
 <text>castration, vasectomy, penectomy, orchiectomy, vaginoplasty, clitoroplasty, vulvoplasty, mastectomy, hysterectomy, oophorectomy, ovariectomy, reconstruction of the fixed part of the urethra with or without metoidioplasty or phalloplasty, metoidioplasty, phalloplasty, vaginectomy, scrotoplasty, implantation of erection or testicular prostheses, reduction thyrochondroplasty, chondrolaryngoplasty, tubal ligation, sterilization, augmentation mammoplasty, placement of chest implants to create feminine breasts, placement of fat or artificial implants in the gluteal region, liposuction, lipofilling, voice surgery, hair reconstruction, pectoral implants, any plastic, cosmetic, or aesthetic surgery which feminizes or masculinizes the facial or other physiological features of an individual, and any removal of any otherwise healthy or non-diseased body part or tissue.</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                        </paragraph>
                        <paragraph id="id979f1235f1ae48f5b4ebac3a8f0e83e2">
                            <enum>(2)</enum>
                            <header>Exclusions</header>
 <text>The term <term>specified gender transition procedure</term> shall not include, when furnished to an individual by a health care provider with the consent of such individual (or, if applicable, the parents or legal guardian of such individual)—</text>
                            <subparagraph id="id1d217dcbbd60427c9a7d01c056f5ab42">
                                <enum>(A)</enum>
 <text>services to individuals born with a medically verifiable disorder of sex development, including an individual with external sex characteristics which are irresolvably ambiguous, such as an individual born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, an individual born with 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or an individual born having both ovarian and testicular tissue;</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="idb011337378e844a8b9e3258865d5ec80">
                                <enum>(B)</enum>
 <text>services relating to any other physician-diagnosed disorder of sexual development with respect to which the physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action for a healthy male or female of the same age;</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id1db5cfb29481483c8d453cfd6dd8e8b1">
                                <enum>(C)</enum>
 <text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder caused or exacerbated by the performance of gender transition procedures, without regard to whether the gender transition procedure was performed in accordance with State and Federal law or whether the gender transition procedure is treated as medical care under this section;</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id694b2284fc7f4874bad8d57fc34a58a8">
                                <enum>(D)</enum>
 <text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness (but not mental, behavioral, or emotional distress or a mental, behavioral, or emotional disorder) which would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed to alleviate said physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness;</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="idfd930908cdc34d90a8f0401117ace39b">
                                <enum>(E)</enum>
 <text>any procedure to restore or reconstruct the body of the individual in order to correspond to the individual’s sex after 1 or more previous gender transition procedures, which may include the removal of a pseudo phallus or breast augmentation;</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id23770cda298f4fff9ef72c4e83493de2">
                                <enum>(F)</enum>
 <text>puberty suppression or puberty-blocking prescription drugs for the purpose of normalizing puberty for an individual experiencing precocious puberty; or</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id3b746153a26d46b28e5878fa3e063054">
                                <enum>(G)</enum>
 <text>male circumcision.</text> </subparagraph> </paragraph> <paragraph id="iddedb3da8891e4022b1ea1759b7e6cb0c"> <enum>(3)</enum> <header>Additional definitions</header> <text>For purposes of this subsection:</text>
                            <subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ide6d97e56aff2423a87ad2ce73c34cf2d">
                                <enum>(A)</enum>
                                <header display-inline="yes-display-inline">Gender
                                    transition</header>
 <text>The term <term>gender transition</term> means the process by which an individual goes from identifying with or presenting as his or her sex to identifying with or presenting as a self-proclaimed identity which does not correspond with or is different from his or her sex, and may be accompanied by social, legal, or physical changes.</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="idf263978c0688464aa8be2c585437db6e">
                                <enum>(B)</enum>
                                <header>Sex</header>
 <text>The term <term>sex</term>, when referring to an individual’s sex, means either male or female, as biologically determined, including as described in subparagraphs (C) and (D).</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id2c1f61a0899947649255021d4571adc9">
                                <enum>(C)</enum>
                                <header>Female</header>
 <text>The term <term>female</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means an individual belonging, at conception, to the sex characterized by a reproductive system with the biological function of producing eggs (ova).</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="id59a2a27d4f5f4c80b878646f1555510d">
                                <enum>(D)</enum>
                                <header>Male</header>
 <text>The term <term>male</term>, when used to refer to a natural person, means an individual belonging, at conception, to the biological sex characterized by a reproductive system with the biological function of producing sperm.</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                        </paragraph>
                    </subsection>
                    <after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block>
                </quoted-block>
            </subsection>
            <subsection id="ide23a59cb59e3400caf377637d0827efd">

            </subsection>

id="HFDA5F162266C463F8F344D97362A7503"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section:</text><paragraph id="HED410B686A06429FA91A2A51A0CAE5EE"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Diversity, including any division, unit, or center of such an institution, that is responsible for directing or compelling faculty, staff, or students to state, pledge, recite, assert, or otherwise express ideas as a precondition of receiving any benefit, program access, instruction, privilege, employment, admission, or other such matter in violation of title IV or title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2000c">42 U.S.C. 2000c et seq.</external-xref>; 2000d et seq.).</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H22C75154E3F94599A09266C12D542335"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Diversity statement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>diversity statement</term> means any written or oral statement that—</text><subparagraph id="HCC9F7C0614EF4BC5B67ECC6096F4819C"><enum>(A)</enum><text>asserts that individuals of any race, sex, ethnicity, color, or national origin are inherently superior or inferior;</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H60930160BF6C43558F0EE33709B661CD"><enum>(B)</enum><text>asserts that individuals should be adversely or advantageously treated on the basis of their race, sex, ethnicity, color, or national origin; or</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H5830A962F7584890BD20207AD20C458A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>asserts that individuals, by virtue of race, sex, ethnicity, color, or national origin, bear collective guilt and are inherently responsible for actions committed in the past by other members of the same race, ethnicity, color, or national origin.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H1F2B5703ADF84CD1B14E5472C2834C70"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Institution of higher education</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The term <term>institution of higher education</term> has the meaning given that term in section 102.</text></paragraph></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section><section id="H0A89A96D651E4E3F8E61877FD53A7BD2"><enum>3.</enum><header>Conforming requirements for accrediting agencies and associations</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 496(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1099b">20 U.S.C. 1099b(a)</external-xref>) is amended—</text><paragraph id="H7F157979331B4137BD4E8F91B08C3B10"><enum>(1)</enum><text>in paragraph (7), by striking <quote>and</quote> at the end;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H819432B6C70844778D1B6927FCD0DDC6"><enum>(2)</enum><text>in paragraph (8), by striking the period at the end and inserting <quote>; and</quote>; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H5CE5858363E645AC8A5D8901E930D210"><enum>(3)</enum><text>by adding at the end the following:</text><quoted-block style="OLC" association has or seeks to include within its scope of recognition the evaluation of the quality of institutions or programs offering graduate medical education, such agency or association shall, in addition to meeting the other requirements of this subpart, demonstrate to the Secretary that the agency or association does not require an institution or program to adopt any policies or other requirements in contravention of section 124 as a condition of receiving accreditation from the agency or <dc:title>119 S1988 IS: To prohibit the participation of males in athletic programs or activities at the military service academies that are designated for women or girls.</dc:title>

<distribution-code display="yes">II</distribution-code><congress>119th CONGRESS</congress><session>1st Session</session><legis-num>S. 1988</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action><action-date date="20250609">June 9, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S412">Mr. Tuberville</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSAS00">Committee on Armed Services</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title>To prohibit the participation of males in athletic programs or activities at the military service academies that are designated for women or girls.</official-title></form><legis-body><section id="id000db31914eb4062bb567f176a66c9c6" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Prohibition on participation of males in athletic programs or activities at the military service academies that are designated for women or girls</header><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idfc483f616b07475b975b4090551ba4f7"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of Defense shall ensure that the United States Military Academy, the United States Naval Academy, and the United States Air Force Academy do not permit a person whose sex is male to participate in an athletic program or activity that is designated for women or girls.</text></subsection><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id7898e6d39eec482788b3c2eef14270e3"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit a recipient from permitting males to train or practice with an athletic program or activity that is designated for women or girls so long as no female is deprived of a roster spot on a team or sport, opportunity to participate in a practice or competition, scholarship, admission to an educational institution, or any other benefit that accompanies participating in the athletic program or activity. </text></subsection><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id8fd72ca11b704fdb9e5ec6084677e540"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section—</text><paragraph id="ida12f915a16da4c979d24c69ec5214cba"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the term <term>athletic programs and activities</term> includes all programs or activities that are provided conditional upon participation with any athletic team; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="ida441abc0afcd49b7b490d6ce533f9714"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the term <term>sex</term> means a person’s reproductive biology and genetics at birth.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></legis-body></bill>

                    <enum>(1)</enum>

                </paragraph>
                <paragraph id="ID15B5E05321AD4A69922E4CA97346E14A">

                </paragraph>

 <text>by inserting after paragraph (27) the following new paragraph:</text> <quoted-block id="IDC7FC44FD3636413EB86420600FE569EA" display-inline="no-display-inline" style="OLC"> <paragraph id="ID2CD7663FE9E9442FBCD18387FDE1CDBE"> <enum>(28)</enum> <text>with respect to any amount expended for specified gender transition procedures (as defined in section 1905(kk)) furnished to an individual enrolled in a State plan (or waiver of such plan).</text>

            <subsection id="ID6D43F4EB9F65480095204C42D6DAB9AC">
                <enum>(c)</enum>
                <header>Specified gender transition procedures defined</header>
 <text>Section 1905 of the <act-name parsable-cite="SSA">Social Security Act</act-name> (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1396d">42 U.S.C. 1396d</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:</text>
                <quoted-block id="ID26F3835D04EC4B45AB89E1FC7414077C" display-inline="no-display-inline" style="OLC">
                    <subsection id="ID951DEB9AC264478790F379D03FA9B97C">
                        <enum>(kk)</enum>
                        <header>Specified gender transition procedures</header>
                        <paragraph id="IDB58061B28BA0486D8DA6E63C14D5E69A">
                            <enum>(1)</enum>
                            <header>In general</header>
 <text>For purposes of section 1903(i)(28), except as provided in paragraph (2), the term <term>specified gender transition procedure</term> means, with respect to an individual, any of the following when performed for the purpose of intentionally changing the body of such individual (including by disrupting the body's development, inhibiting its natural functions, or modifying its appearance) to no longer correspond to the individual's sex:</text>
                            <subparagraph id="ID19F506AD7F6848D195D6D1B86C77427E">
                                <enum>(A)</enum>
 <text>Performing any surgery, including—</text> <clause id="ID8E94773F3C8749C9BF4392EC81EED5AE"> <enum>(i)</enum> <text>castration;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="ID7751A99CB00B4EB4A2364280E89A2872">
                                    <enum>(ii)</enum>
 <text>sterilization;</text> </clause> <clause id="ID4EA1C923B3FE43ECBE53F1F4A383E6AD"> <enum>(iii)</enum> <text>orchiectomy;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="ID93510C2F5B6043FA9BDEE71242440CA3">
                                    <enum>(iv)</enum>
 <text>scrotoplasty;</text> </clause> <clause id="ID49DF4D7617294E169DAAE795072A29B9"> <enum>(v)</enum> <text>vasectomy;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="ID6076D33D0D3D40F48077AAFC7817B522">
                                    <enum>(vi)</enum>
 <text>tubal ligation;</text> </clause> <clause id="ID19FEDDDDA74A4BDB892B18CA9A3360A4"> <enum>(vii)</enum> <text>hysterectomy;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="IDFB25BA0E40E244D1B72FA57777457E36">
                                    <enum>(viii)</enum>
 <text>oophorectomy;</text> </clause> <clause id="IDFDCC71FFFF36418BBE85E4211B399F25"> <enum>(ix)</enum> <text>ovariectomy;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="ID69A5584996E1480BA8EA6F75CA334532">
                                    <enum>(x)</enum>
 <text>metoidioplasty;</text> </clause> <clause id="IDFD09C39AEC574BAB95B13F07FD66A814"> <enum>(xi)</enum> <text>clitoroplasty;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="ID36A3C383307A4F64BAD92682362AE05F">
                                    <enum>(xii)</enum>
 <text>reconstruction of the fixed part of the urethra with or without a metoidioplasty or a phalloplasty;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="ID7A0DB611D78D4462A9AFE9C7D9A87ADA">

 <text>penectomy;</text> </clause> <clause id="IDC486CB310F9D4E7CB2AFDD5042B439A8"> <enum>(xiv)</enum> <text>phalloplasty;</text>
                                </clause>

 <text>vaginoplasty;</text> </clause> <clause id="ID285171C08D3C42EF9FB26660044245DA"> <enum>(xvi)</enum> <text>vaginectomy;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="IDC5B8ECB736434A7A9C68E8B35A302556">

 <text>vulvoplasty;</text> </clause> <clause id="ID0D14B59362A24F5AA08B5D6C79A7E20B"> <enum>(xviii)</enum> <text>reduction thyrochondroplasty;</text>

 <text>chondrolaryngoplasty;</text> </clause> <clause id="IDFCC7A78F116C4EAFBAB4DE3D18EF7856"> <enum>(xx)</enum> <text>mastectomy; and</text>

                                    <enum>(xxi)</enum>
 <text>any plastic, cosmetic, or aesthetic surgery that feminizes or masculinizes the facial or other body features of an individual.</text>
                                </clause>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="ID604633FC8445467D912D179E8009192C">
                                <enum>(B)</enum>
 <text>Any placement of chest implants to create feminine breasts or any placement of erection or testicular prostheses.</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="ID09145F5EEAD046A5913AC399B5133F25">
                                <enum>(C)</enum>
 <text>Any placement of fat or artificial implants in the gluteal region.</text>

                            <enum>(2)</enum>
                            <header>Exception</header>
 <text>Paragraph (1) shall not apply to the following when furnished to an individual by a health care provider with the consent of such individual's parent or legal guardian:</text>
                            <subparagraph id="ID963CB5F489DD46EFAF5EE753F5853C8A">

 <text>Puberty suppression or blocking prescription drugs for the purpose of normalizing puberty for an individual experiencing precocious puberty.</text>
                            </subparagraph>
                            <subparagraph id="IDC66581AD1AE44ECEB97D716958D82369">
                                <enum>(B)</enum>
 <text>Medically necessary procedures or treatments to correct for—</text>
                                <clause id="ID90D9F12F41A646F7817DE19170335640">
                                    <enum>(i)</enum>
 <text>a medically verifiable disorder of sex development, including—</text>
                                    <subclause id="ID5B739715A5E7459884AE7AD00ECFA601">
                                        <enum>(I)</enum>
 <text>46,XX chromosomes with virilization;</text> </subclause> <subclause id="IDE32574CB839B48D2942BDB4B03D36E52"> <enum>(II)</enum> <text>46,XY chromosomes with undervirilization; and</text>
                                    </subclause>

                                        <enum>(III)</enum>
 <text>both ovarian and testicular tissue;</text> </subclause> </clause> <clause id="IDEFCDF1E2DBD34F779C24B6E1A15A842F"> <enum>(ii)</enum> <text>sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex hormone action, if determined to be abnormal by a physician through genetic or biochemical testing;</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="IDF621AB0C094448C9A8224AA82FC82808">
                                    <enum>(iii)</enum>
 <text>infection, disease, injury, or disorder caused or exacerbated by a previous procedure described in paragraph (1), or a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of a major bodily function unless the procedure is performed, not including procedures performed for the alleviation of mental distress; or</text>
                                </clause>
                                <clause id="IDCFDEAA8EF9A24BEDA9E6D1EE7F47D67F">
                                    <enum>(iv)</enum>
 <text>procedures to restore or reconstruct the body of the individual in order to correspond to the individual's sex after one or more previous procedures described in paragraph (1), which may include the removal of a pseudo phallus or breast augmentation.</text>
                                </clause>
                            </subparagraph>
                        </paragraph>
                        <paragraph id="ID08FB78569A8943BA9C65D9066C6D18E3">
                            <enum>(3)</enum>
                            <header>Sex</header>
 <text>For purposes of paragraph (1), the term <term>sex</term> means either male or female, as biologically determined and defined in paragraphs (4) and (5), respectively.</text>
                        </paragraph>
                        <paragraph id="ID135744F3C7954966A9F7F410E9B0845D">
                            <enum>(4)</enum>
                            <header>Female</header>
 <text>For purposes of paragraph (3), the term <term>female</term> means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes eggs for fertilization.</text>
                        </paragraph>
                        <paragraph id="IDCB346F2F5D6C4E8DB656417B001FD121" commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline">
                            <enum>(5)</enum>
                            <header>Male</header>
 <text>For purposes of paragraph (3), the term <term>male</term> means an individual who naturally has, had, will have, or would have, but for a developmental or genetic anomaly or historical accident, the reproductive system that at some point produces, transports, and utilizes sperm for fertilization.</text>
                        </paragraph>

            <action-date date="20250611">June 11, 2025</action-date>
            <action-desc><sponsor name-id="S429">Mr. Banks</sponsor> introduced the following bill;
                which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSHR00">Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and
