        <legis-type>A BILL</legis-type>
        <official-title>To amend title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to prohibit
            discrimination against employees on the basis of expression that describes, asserts, or
            reinforces the binary or biological nature of sex.</official-title>
    </form>
    <legis-body>
        <section id="S1" section-type="section-one">
            <enum>1.</enum>
            <header>Short title</header>
 <text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Restoring Biological Truth to the Workplace Act</short-title></quote>.</text>
        </section>
        <section id="id7edc23da6ed242e891229f2ba270986c">
            <enum>2.</enum>
            <header>Prohibited unlawful employment action</header>
 <text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 703 of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2000e-2">42 U.S.C. 2000e–2</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following:</text>
            <quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id0421afde7dde49bfb15071bee8a06196">
                <subsection id="id577aac2c2dde45dba613c3e3d5daf178">
                    <enum>(o)</enum>
                    <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="yes-display-inline" id="id42a2e94c255a417c88919581ec11d9e4">
                        <enum>(1)</enum>
 <text>It shall be an unlawful employment practice for an employer to take an action described in subsection (a) because an employee engages in covered expression, that describes, asserts, or reinforces the binary or biological nature of sex. For purposes of this paragraph, the term <quote>covered expression</quote> means expression, inside or outside of a workplace, through means including speech, writing, or a depiction, or owning or using an item that contains speech, writing, or a depiction, and includes the use of pronouns.</text>
                    </paragraph>
                    <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id829fec5d86ba48ca8a0c84a78f9f1352" indent="up1">
                        <enum>(2)</enum>
 <text>It shall be an unlawful employment practice for an employer to take an action described in subsection (a) because an employee requests or uses a single-sex area that is a bathroom, changing area, or other area where physical privacy is desirable.</text>
                    </paragraph>
                    <paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id235915e82944464595e80d880b83cffc" indent="up1">
                        <enum>(3)</enum>
 <text>It shall not be a defense to the use of a practice described in paragraph (1) or (2) that use of the practice is job related for the position in question or consistent with business necessity.</text>
                    </paragraph>
                </subsection>
                <after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block>
            </quoted-block>
        </section>
        <section commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" section-type="subsequent-section" id="idcca417869f334929af752e6b5613acd4">
            <enum>3.</enum>
            <header>Prohibited retaliation</header>
 <text display-inline="no-display-inline">Section 704(a) of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2000e-3">42 U.S.C. 2000e–3(a)</external-xref>) is amended by inserting <quote>, including an unlawful employment practice prohibited under section 703(o)</quote>after <quote>by this title</quote>.</text>
        </section>
    </legis-body>
</bill>

<bill bill-type="olc" bill-stage="Introduced-in-Senate" dms-id="A1" public-private="public" slc-id="S1-BOM25052-082-6F-RKS"><metadata xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">

<dc:title>119 S204 IS: Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act</dc:title>
<dc:publisher>U.S. Senate</dc:publisher>
<dc:date>2025-01-23</dc:date>
<dc:format>text/xml</dc:format>

<distribution-code display="yes">II</distribution-code><congress>119th CONGRESS</congress><session>1st Session</session><legis-num>S. 204</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action><action-date date="20250123">January 23, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S365">Mr. Scott of South Carolina</sponsor> (for himself, <cosponsor name-id="S378">Mr. Lankford</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S398">Mr. Cramer</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="S317">Mr. Barrasso</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSJU00">Committee on the Judiciary</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title>To protect the right of parents to direct the upbringing of their children as a fundamental right.</official-title></form><legis-body style="OLC" display-enacting-clause="yes-display-enacting-clause" id="H2E096C5B97094DEF94497361C563FC0D"><section section-type="section-one" id="H44482939E5EB433FA74DD4434C75AD53"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="H77B4A1E1DA454E64BD4060D390C40185"><enum>2.</enum><header>Congressional findings and declaration of purposes</header><subsection id="HC81556516ACE49C98C556CD9B3156FDF"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Findings</header><text>Congress finds the following:</text><paragraph id="H0C9282C8C6AD4CADA9D859F469459B8B"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The nature of the parent-child relationship endows parents with the primary responsibility and obligation to care for their child.</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H7D7268450FBF49CDB3C4C904E06C0E1D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>From these responsibilities and obligations comes the pre-political, natural right of parents to care for their children. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H333F4F9F631440FCBD24505EFBC581C3"><enum>(3)</enum><text>The role of parents in the raising and rearing of their children is of inestimable value and deserving of both praise and protection by all levels of government.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H584651EF3145427AB5F063C03AE51BEA"><enum>(4)</enum><text>This right as recognized in the traditions of western civilization recognizes that parents have the responsibility to love, nurture, raise, and protect their children.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H6EDD29E60CE04925B3EE9B2EA6FB7ABB"><enum>(5)</enum><text>The right encompasses the authority of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children according to the dictates of their conscience, to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children in their own beliefs and religion, and to be the primary decision maker for their child until the child reaches adulthood.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H7850BB5D96274821AE42FA8DBCDE0699"><enum>(6)</enum><text>The Supreme Court has consistently recognized the primary role of parents in caring for children, concluding the following: </text><subparagraph id="HB3AC37B397654A29BD17CB35B0B9014C"><enum>(A)</enum><text><quote>[T]he child is not the mere creature of the state; those who nurture him and direct his destiny have the right, coupled with the high duty, to recognize and prepare him for additional obligations.</quote> Pierce v. Soc’y of the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus &amp; Mary, 268 U.S. 510, 535 (1925).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H6A506652BB594641A37C7377CE25A135"><enum>(B)</enum><text><quote>[I]t is the natural duty of the parent to give his children education suitable to their station in life.</quote> Meyer v. Nebraska, 262 U.S. 390, 400 (1923).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HA23016F69E074D55890C23758B4D6EE8"><enum>(C)</enum><text><quote>It is plain that the interest of a parent in the companionship, care, custody, and management of his or her children comes to this Court with a momentum for respect lacking when appeal is made to liberties which derive merely from shifting economic arrangements.</quote> Stanley v. Illinois, 405 U.S. 645, 651 (1972).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H19DD7750FFBE44F6BACE7A2F3F12F71E"><enum>(D)</enum><text><quote>The history and culture of Western civilization reflect a strong tradition of parental concern for the nurture and upbringing of their children. This primary role of the parents in the upbringing of their children is now established beyond debate as an enduring American tradition.</quote>Wisconsin v. Yoder, 406 U.S. 205, 232 (1972).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H5AA0C302B8FD4DCC93419C256C28EEB2"><enum>(E)</enum><text><quote>Our jurisprudence historically has reflected Western civilization concepts of the family as a unit with broad parental authority over minor children. Our cases have consistently followed that course.</quote> Parham v. J. R., 442 U.S. 584, 602 (1979).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HC2C41C3044AF47049058F0D0C8131A00"><enum>(F)</enum><text><quote>We have recognized on numerous occasions that the relationship between parent and child is constitutionally protected.</quote> Quilloin v. Walcott, 434 U.S. 246, 255 (1978).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HC107775396104F76B4187E6D98AD5A81"><enum>(G)</enum><text>The Supreme Court has explained that the liberty specially protected by the Due Process Clause includes the right <quote>to direct the education and upbringing of one’s children.</quote> Washington v. Glucksberg, 521 U.S. 702, 720 (1997).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H6D7900639D7F4ECCBB82EA6AC1054EB4"><enum>(H)</enum><text><quote>[W]e have recognized the fundamental right of parents to make decisions concerning the care, custody, and control of their children . . . In light of this extensive precedent, it cannot now be doubted that the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment protects the fundamental right of parents to make decisions concerning the care, custody, and control of their children.</quote> Troxel v. Granville, 530 U.S. 57, 66 (2000) (plurality op.).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H6BDE361BF8AF4F89A4ECA9E23BAF9527"><enum>(I)</enum><text><quote>[T]he Due Process Clause does not permit a State to infringe on the fundamental right of parents to make child rearing decisions simply because a state judge believes a <quote>better</quote> decision could be made.</quote> Troxel, 530 U.S. at 72–73 (plurality op.).</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H8489B6B6255A415CB0E7A2C6BD81596B"><enum>(7)</enum><text>Some decisions of Federal courts have failed to recognize the fundamental right of parents, resulting in an improper standard of judicial review being applied to government conduct that adversely affects parental rights and prerogatives.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H00AF3764BA674E90801E6DF91781F3E0"><enum>(8)</enum><text>Government agencies have increasingly intruded into the legitimate decisions and prerogatives of parents in situations that do not involve abuse or neglect but simply an agency’s disagreement with parenting choices based on decent and honorable religious or philosophical premises.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H29E81BC981A344FB862C11C7FEAD3297"><enum>(9)</enum><text>Government’s involvement in parenting should prioritize the parent’s role as the child’s primary educator and should support, not supplant, the parent’s rights and responsibilities.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HE8C3A526D23448F9A198A006DFC0978C"><enum>(10)</enum><text>Government should not interfere in the decisions and actions of parents without compelling justification.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC1536C42BFFC4C0FB74CD7420CCC3EFF"><enum>(11)</enum><text>The strict scrutiny test used by courts to evaluate cases concerning fundamental rights is the correct standard of review for government actions that interfere with the right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children, and it appropriately balances the interests of parents, children, and government.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="HE9AAB80AD2514231B06ED275DF54BD12"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Purposes</header><text>The purposes of this Act are—</text><paragraph id="H1C3B7B207CC840B1AAD7C1AB0F4210FB"><enum>(1)</enum><text>to protect the right of parents to direct the upbringing of their children as a fundamental right; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H0CD0F34E044E4BD48D46BB380BEB221A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>while protecting the right of parents, to acknowledge that the rights involve responsibilities and specifically that parents have the responsibility for the education, nurture, and upbringing of their children as specified by the Supreme Court in Meyer v. Nebraska, 262 U.S. 390, 400 (1923), Wisconsin v. Yoder, 406 U.S. 205, 232 (1972), and Washington v. Glucksberg, 521 U.S. 702, 720 (1997), and have the high duty to recognize and prepare their children for additional obligations as specified by the Supreme Court in Pierce v. Soc’y of the Sisters of the Holy Names of Jesus &amp; Mary, 268 U.S. 510, 535 (1925).</text></paragraph></subsection></section><section id="H962403E2B9F54068BFDA37A8227509DB"><enum>3.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="HF68E6DB3C5594158BDDA5A3A2E8038BC"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Government</header><text>The term <term>government</term> includes a branch, department, agency, instrumentality, and official (or other person acting under color of law) of the United States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and each territory and possession of the United States.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H491547237B6D49049C66D68F559240B7"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Parent</header><text>The term <term>parent</term> means a biological parent of a child, an adoptive parent of a child, or an individual who has been granted exclusive right and authority over the welfare of a child under State law.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HDF4995FDA2A14FADB5C95A99C3683314"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Child</header><text>The term <term>child</term> means an individual who has not attained 18 years of age.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC1B7A5D1F5AE43CE8111CD3D98D0662C"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Substantial burden</header><text>The term <term>substantial burden</term>—</text><subparagraph id="H7671614BFD4B4866B2953AEEA7CA59C6"><enum>(A)</enum><text>means any action that directly or indirectly constrains, inhibits, curtails, or denies the right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their child or compels any action contrary to the right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their child; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H62A9A578286B433FA7AA6A4CAE7DF399"><enum>(B)</enum><text>includes withholding benefits, assessing criminal, civil, or administrative penalties or damages, or exclusion from governmental programs.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></section><section id="HD934DA7CB6A6498B9DB22A4519E76DFC"><enum>4.</enum><header>Protection of parental rights</header><subsection id="H0D12920312D942CB9D97E217A2532533"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><paragraph id="HF983780211F1461880B29F854E9DDCA0"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Fundamental right</header><text>The liberty of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children is a fundamental right.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H54115A144E7C4C4BA9552893F1A6BF38"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Limits on government interference</header><text>Government shall not substantially burden the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children without demonstrating that the infringement is required by a compelling governmental interest of the highest order as applied to the parent and the child and is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest. The fundamental rights protected include, without limitation, the following rights and responsibilities:</text><subparagraph id="HBED458004721443DA8F3F73380E19471"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">To direct the education of the child.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H7F2C25CA0F7241A3B1194EAF6C3A7464"><enum>(B)</enum><text>To direct the moral or religious upbringing of the child.</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="HE8A0BADA9619423EB6BD3E01C0B5B31A"><enum>(C)</enum><text>To access and review all medical records of the child and to make and consent to all physical and mental health care decisions for the child.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H4C4A2E8A020A4A29B22E6A7AD017D84C"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Effect of this Act on other rights</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Unless legally waived or legally terminated, parents have inalienable rights that are more comprehensive than those listed in this section. This Act does not prescribe all rights of parents, nor does it preempt or foreclose claims or remedies in support of parental rights that are available under any other Federal law, State law, the United States Constitution, or a State constitution.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H826F8603402349DCB8C2EE2C3ACFF021"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Exceptions</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">This section does not apply to a parental action or decision that would result in serious physical injury to the child or that would end life.</text></subsection><subsection id="HF5C3DE6A5AF9403DBF342A7462383D46"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Judicial remedy</header><text>Any parent may raise a violation of this Act as a claim or a defense in an action in a Federal or State court or before an administrative tribunal and obtain appropriate relief against a government. Standing to assert a claim or defense under this section shall be governed by the general rules of standing under article III of the Constitution. </text></subsection></section><section id="HCF504A6A48DF4A05BBB624F9AE9313B4"><enum>5.</enum><header>Attorneys fees</header><subsection id="HE6D05361B32F43BE8FF8430C6346DD6F"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Judicial Proceedings</header><text>Section 722(b) of the Revised Statutes (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1988">42 U.S.C. 1988(b)</external-xref>) is amended by inserting <quote>the Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act,</quote> before <quote>title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964</quote>.</text></subsection><subsection commented="no" id="HAB7190D937584F5E95A5E4F7C7DC01E3"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Administrative Proceedings</header><text>Section 504(b)(1)(C) of title 5, United States Code, is amended by striking <quote>the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993</quote> and inserting <quote>any adjudication under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993 or the Families’ Rights and Responsibilities Act</quote>. </text></subsection></section><section id="H86938AEFD08E447EB101311D3DE8848A"><enum>6.</enum><header>Applicability</header><subsection id="H2895FAEF3D504894851F3E894B0F9C6D"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In General</header><text>This Act applies to each Federal law, and the implementation of any such law, whether statutory or otherwise, and whether adopted before or after the date of enactment of this Act.</text></subsection><subsection id="HF3CF8FF41FE54AD186839110C22492AB"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><paragraph id="HC98CF8DD11D64BD8AA4BF9DC7DCB8804"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Additional rights</header><text>The protections of the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children afforded by this Act are in addition to the protections provided under Federal law, State law, and the State and Federal constitutions.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HA8010FF4A17E43B6977B751311CDB35C"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Broad protection</header><text>This Act shall be construed in favor of a broad protection of the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H7B5F4870FF014CF39A410605DBCDDA2F"><enum>(3)</enum><header>No government burden</header><text>Nothing in this Act shall be construed to authorize any government to burden the fundamental right of parents to direct the upbringing, education, and health care of their children. </text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H92CEEBB8F8124529ABB9DCFB02EF2CFE"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Subsequently enacted laws</header><text>Federal statutory law adopted after the date of the enactment of this Act is subject to this Act, unless such law explicitly excludes such application by reference to this Act.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></legis-body></bill>

<form>
<distribution-code display="yes">II</distribution-code><congress>119th CONGRESS</congress><session>1st Session</session><legis-num>S. 209</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action><action-date date="20250123">January 23, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S374">Mr. Cotton</sponsor> (for himself, <cosponsor name-id="S429">Mr. Banks</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S435">Mr. Sheehy</cosponsor>, and <cosponsor name-id="S419">Mr. Mullin</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSJU00">Committee on the Judiciary</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title>To protect children from medical malpractice in the form of gender-transition procedures.</official-title></form><legis-body display-enacting-clause="yes-display-enacting-clause"><section section-type="section-one" id="S1"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Protecting Minors from Medical Malpractice Act of 2025</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="id485D8C8BF32746DAA7C880062F8856A1"><enum>2.</enum><header>Private right of action for a gender-transition procedure performed on a minor</header><subsection id="id20fdb775a39d4259bddbb91c15e65368"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>A medical practitioner, in any circumstance described in subsection (c), who performs a gender-transition procedure on an individual who is less than 18 years of age shall, as described in subsection (b), be liable to the individual if injured (including any physical, psychological, emotional, or physiological harms) by such procedure, related treatment, or the aftereffects of the procedure or treatment.</text></subsection><subsection id="id6940121aeffe47c5a8f86af59af2ed6b"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Private right of action</header><text>An individual covered by subsection (a) who receives a gender-transition procedure from a medical practitioner (or a representative, including a legal guardian, on behalf of such individual) may, not later than the day that is 30 years after the date on which the individual turns 18 years of age, bring a civil action against such medical practitioner in a court of competent jurisdiction for—</text><paragraph id="id01D37B9E8A7D424898A8498CBA8560D6"><enum>(1)</enum><text>declaratory or injunctive relief; </text></paragraph><paragraph id="idD29DF47597E44EEC85851B2B856D35D8"><enum>(2)</enum><text>compensatory damages;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id68D80CC376574457AA6B1CFB90A67100"><enum>(3)</enum><text>punitive damages; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id8A99349D16344BE79B327924A8C9E745"><enum>(4)</enum><text>attorney’s fees and costs.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="id86ea96df8e1d40259ce00342cf43fbe7"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Circumstances</header><text>For the purposes of subsection (a), the circumstances described in this subsection are that—</text><paragraph id="id74be3a36ace3459d8401b0d83e975aa8"><enum>(1)</enum><text>the medical practitioner or the individual receiving the gender-transition procedure traveled in interstate or foreign commerce, or traveled using a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a); </text></paragraph><paragraph id="id36e0aea52c4040439c0645fa0e8eae6f"><enum>(2)</enum><text>the medical practitioner used a means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id6c20f0aa280d45f99f8846b9a877625c"><enum>(3)</enum><text>any payment of any kind was made, directly or indirectly, in furtherance of or in connection with the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id22bf8be8c72d4c6895dca9b7e0b5bfb2"><enum>(4)</enum><text>the medical practitioner transmitted in interstate or foreign commerce any communication relating to or in furtherance of the conduct described in subsection (a) using any means, channel, facility, or instrumentality of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means or in any manner, including by computer, mail, wire, or electromagnetic transmission;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="idee12c6a0a1924c7686b02612a1d18dd5"><enum>(5)</enum><text>any instrument, item, substance, or other object that has traveled in interstate or foreign commerce was used to perform the conduct described in subsection (a);</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id99b474a0c7d641e98b9b11371024fef8"><enum>(6)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) occurred within the special maritime and territorial jurisdiction of the United States, or any territory or possession of the United States; or</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ida11f5a96fa8543e8a825ea7fcc4ae14d"><enum>(7)</enum><text>the conduct described in subsection (a) otherwise occurred in or affected interstate or foreign commerce. </text></paragraph></subsection></section><section id="id158a7e039f8e4b51bd128c08f9854599"><enum>3.</enum><header>Preserving freedom of conscience and medical judgement for medical providers</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no provision of Federal law shall require, or be construed to require, a medical practitioner to perform a gender-transition procedure. </text></section><section id="idA12FD8ED4F6942A4A9FE5C69BBE9A64D"><enum>4.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for certain States</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any State that requires medical practitioners to perform any gender-transition procedure on an individual in the State shall be ineligible to receive any Federal funding from the Department of Health and Human Services. </text></section><section id="id34148F950343488B9FAE88D2B19B16B1"><enum>5.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">In this Act:</text><paragraph id="idcb2b7dd6d83e4231bd34de73b85efa83"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Biological sex</header><text>The term <term>biological sex</term> means the genetic classification of an individual as male or female, as reflected in the organization of the body of such individual for a reproductive role or capacity, such as through sex chromosomes, naturally occurring sex hormones, and internal and external genitalia present at birth, without regard to the subjective sense of identity of the individual.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id4a713fe847e94d008d4f273d2584799a"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Gender-transition procedure</header><subparagraph id="id2f15d828e5bc46babc41ecc24d8f7cc7"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> means—</text><clause id="idd1d2df915af84a9dbd8de9d8e4c0ab3b"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of puberty-blocking drugs for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual's biological sex;</text></clause><clause id="id1b04d6b632714650a3e5b10ebdd5f1ff"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of cross-sex hormones for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex; or</text></clause><clause id="id24383c87a22441e1a6a4badcdd26d110"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>a surgery to change the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex. </text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id580f7edc518d467786c8459490f3bc1d"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> does not include— </text><clause id="id14127F619246495781A84D5D557BEA1A"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an intervention described in subparagraph (A) that is performed on—</text><subclause id="idAE793661CC0D4A8F9CB321D11D21F03C"><enum>(I)</enum><text>an individual with biological sex characteristics that are inherently ambiguous, such as those born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or having both ovarian and testicular tissue; or</text></subclause><subclause id="idE75844D2D6684793B79CBF3B59F49800"><enum>(II)</enum><text>an individual with respect to whom a physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action, for a biological male or biological female;</text></subclause></clause><clause commented="no" id="id0CD81E68602F4BD8BDF92DF53265B75C"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused or exacerbated by the performance of an intervention described in subparagraph (A) without regard to whether the intervention was performed in accordance with State or Federal law or whether the intervention is covered by the private right of action under section 2; or</text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idA850FF5304C848199CDFF1A1F3E31F39"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idA2D6CB19C0E94B6F8847F99CAE994C47"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Medical practitioner</header><text>The term <term>medical practitioner</term> means a person who is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized by the laws of a State to administer health care in the ordinary course of the practice of the person’s profession.</text></paragraph></section><section id="id31761657b89049cb949d34f643d3b578"><enum>6.</enum><header>Effective date</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act shall take effect on the date of enactment of this Act. </text></section></legis-body></bill>

<bill bill-type="olc" bill-stage="Introduced-in-Senate" dms-id="A1" public-private="public" slc-id="S1-BOM25545-NHG-PP-T0H"><metadata xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">

<dc:title>119 S2385 IS: Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History Act</dc:title>
<dc:publisher>U.S. Senate</dc:publisher>
<dc:date>2025-07-22</dc:date>
<dc:format>text/xml</dc:format>
<dc:language>EN</dc:language>
<dc:rights>Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.</dc:rights>

<form>
<distribution-code display="yes">II</distribution-code><congress>119th CONGRESS</congress><session>1st Session</session><legis-num>S. 2385</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action><action-date date="20250722">July 22, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S429">Mr. Banks</sponsor> introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSEG00">Committee on Energy and Natural Resources</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title>To codify Executive Order 14253 relating to restoring truth and sanity to American history, and for other purposes. </official-title></form><legis-body style="OLC" display-enacting-clause="yes-display-enacting-clause" id="H4CE6BE86D37245A7908B6C1645AB6AEA"><section id="idc028798ef26d47aeb8b045441ff9725d" section-type="section-one"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Restoring Truth and Sanity to American History Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="H02F3A34F1AFA4C48BE0769F3B1EB1F85"><enum>2.</enum><header>Codification of Executive Order 14253</header><subsection id="HD59EB2AF3D374BBB98024FDA893C942A"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Findings</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Congress finds the following:</text><paragraph id="H7BED9BB5498B45989DDCDC794C3B454D"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Over the past decade, Americans have witnessed a concerted and widespread effort to rewrite our Nation's history, replacing objective facts with a distorted narrative driven by ideology rather than truth. This revisionist movement seeks to undermine the remarkable achievements of the United States by casting its founding principles and historical milestones in a negative light. Under this historical revision, our Nation's unparalleled legacy of advancing liberty, individual rights, and human happiness is reconstructed as inherently racist, sexist, oppressive, or otherwise irredeemably flawed. Rather than fostering unity and a deeper understanding of our shared past, the widespread effort to rewrite history deepens societal divides and fosters a sense of national shame, disregarding the progress America has made and the ideals that continue to inspire millions around the globe. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="HFC1CD10581624DD484818995C821171D"><enum>(2)</enum><text>The prior administration advanced this corrosive ideology. At Independence National Historical Park in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania—where our Nation declared that all men are created equal—the prior administration sponsored training by an organization that advocates dismantling <quote>Western foundations</quote> and <quote>interrogating institutional racism</quote> and pressured National Historical Park rangers that their racial identity should dictate how they convey history to visiting Americans because America is purportedly racist. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H9E0838F1C32E470C813B24DA73549C4D"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Once widely respected as a symbol of American excellence and a global icon of cultural achievement, the Smithsonian Institution has, in recent years, come under the influence of a divisive, race-centered ideology. This shift has promoted narratives that portray American and Western values as inherently harmful and oppressive. For example, the Smithsonian American Art Museum today features <quote>The Shape of Power: Stories of Race and American Sculpture</quote>, an exhibit representing that <quote>[s]ocieties including the United States have used race to establish and maintain systems of power, privilege, and disenfranchisement.</quote> The exhibit further claims that <quote>sculpture has been a powerful tool in promoting scientific racism</quote> and promotes the view that race is not a biological reality but a social construct, stating <quote>Race is a human invention</quote>.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H8D3A60B502144DB68701329F68BC676E"><enum>(4)</enum><text>The National Museum of African American History and Culture has proclaimed that <quote>hard work</quote>, <quote>individualism</quote>, and <quote>the nuclear family</quote> are aspects of <quote>White culture</quote>. The forthcoming Smithsonian American Women's History Museum plans on celebrating the exploits of male athletes participating in women's sports. These are just a few examples.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H2E5F220A64E04BB293D4FDBF508FF097"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Policy statement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">It is the policy of this Act—</text><paragraph id="HF2448064E80E411A9E134D1E0C2718A4"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to restore Federal sites dedicated to history, including parks and museums, to solemn and uplifting public monuments that remind Americans of our extraordinary heritage, consistent progress toward becoming a more perfect Union, and unmatched record of advancing liberty, prosperity, and human flourishing;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HC7CDD644FF2E4A9A827354C6814E923A"><enum>(2)</enum><text>that Museums in our Nation's capital should be places where individuals go to learn—not to be subjected to ideological indoctrination or divisive narratives that distort our shared history; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HF63FA5C459CA4192A062D8EFF1C339BE"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to restore the Smithsonian Institution to its rightful place as a symbol of inspiration and American greatness—igniting the imagination of young minds, honoring the richness of American history and innovation, and instilling pride in the hearts of all Americans.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="H82D2ECF6461E40E691932B0093DFFAC1"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Saving our Smithsonian</header><paragraph id="HA54D7115CD83496F93BA509A8386A30D"><enum>(1)</enum><header>In general</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Vice President, in consultation with the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and the Special Assistant to the President and Senior Associate Staff Secretary, shall—</text><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idafc72569d09a4e26ba7f924cf6764dba"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">work to effectuate the policies of this Act through the Vice President's role on the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution with respect to the Smithsonian Institution and its museums, education and research centers, and the National Zoo, including by seeking to remove from such properties anything that—</text><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ide09c222c42a84ba890bfe8f7b698120b"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">violates the policy of this Act as articulated in subsection (b) or Federal civil rights laws; or</text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idb0cf1496bf324c93a1e634edc519062e"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">divides Americans based on race; and</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ida076ff3c625545e0af8a7e9d4f7e9903"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">recommend to the President any additional actions necessary to fully effectuate such policies.</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H9D17C90BD1A440CE9FB33CE196B8E603"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Future appropriations</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Vice President and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall work with Congress to ensure that future appropriations to the Smithsonian Institution—</text><subparagraph id="HD92C69F5920742DBB9AD82C3EE537E36"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">prohibit expenditure on exhibits or programs that—</text><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id6cfb63bb120045c0960b4fde0d64c2b8"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">degrade shared American values;</text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id3a8ecded20bd4c1f8252a54177087c58"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">divide Americans based on race; or</text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id2e23471032b04c139c78d94345d6dcf7"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">promote programs or ideologies inconsistent with Federal law, the policy of this Act as articulated in subsection (b), or Federal civil rights laws; and</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H04C5701C0BAF476DA3B9D364B3D36B7C" commented="no"><enum>(B)</enum><text>celebrate the achievements of women in the American Women's History Museum and do not recognize men as women in any respect, including by—</text><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id2fa36941a40d4594a057760b9b5e8178"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">promoting, celebrating, or favorably depicting biological males competing in women’s sports, winning awards designated for women, dressing as women, or entering private facilities designated for women; </text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id46c04ac70a5b4e3bab5f8aef238a464b"><enum>(ii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">promoting, celebrating, or favorably depicting gender-affirming medicine, especially for minors; or </text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id7381e4e6df5d4178b15f44e8b95ce2d4"><enum>(iii)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">including any other material that degrades the biological nature of sex or violates Federal civil rights laws.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="H7CEBEC2E8E884C678A34C14F88C53A6C"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Other measures to promote policy</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the Secretary of the Interior shall take any other measures within their authority to promote the policy of this Act.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H0A50481B77C24AC398D39DF93409B53B"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">As appropriate, the Vice President shall, in consultation with the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy and Special Assistant to the President and Senior Associate Staff Secretary, work with the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the Majority Leader of the Senate to seek the appointment of citizen members to the Board of Regents of the Smithsonian Institution committed to advancing the policy of this Act.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="HFEFC3A987D6249EBA8A040CFA67ACD47"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Restoring Independence Hall</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">The Secretary of the Interior shall provide sufficient funding, as available, to improve the infrastructure of Independence National Historical Park, which shall be complete by July 4, 2026, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.</text></subsection><subsection id="HBD8BF9A6FBA24686B3A9A4E3B13E44AB"><enum>(e)</enum><header>Restoring truth in American history</header><text>The Secretary of the Interior shall—</text><paragraph id="HEB7680ABCA904F6F8351744A9D84A33D"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">determine whether, since January 1, 2020, public monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties within the Department of the Interior's jurisdiction have been removed or changed to perpetuate a false reconstruction of American history, inappropriately minimize the value of certain historical events or figures, divide Americans based on race, recognize men as women, or include any other improper partisan ideology; </text></paragraph><paragraph id="H24565831DCF9448EBCD0ED62B9527575"><enum>(2)</enum><text>take action to reinstate the pre-existing monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties, as appropriate and consistent with section 437 of the Revised Statutes (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/43/1451">43 U.S.C. 1451</external-xref>), division A of subtitle I of title 54, United States Code, and other applicable law; and </text></paragraph><paragraph id="HF574501D5EDE42CEBFEF7B7AC26DED45"><enum>(3)</enum><text>take action, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, to ensure that all public monuments, memorials, statues, markers, or similar properties within the Department of the Interior’s jurisdiction—</text><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id2e7eec02cd6b4d6fb90f2454159e0281"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">do not contain descriptions, depictions, or other content that inappropriately disparage Americans past or living (including persons living in colonial times), divide Americans based on race, or recognize men as women; and </text></subparagraph><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id51c943cc17114adaa127de3d5e5e2bee"><enum>(B)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">instead focus on the greatness of the achievements and progress of the American people or, with respect to natural features, the beauty, abundance, and grandeur of the American landscape.</text></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="HF693A2E2528E4FCCB81272CD6688B82B"><enum>(f)</enum><header>Rule of construction</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in this Act shall be construed to—</text><paragraph id="H84CEA3F5BFB84293BC9F9485722839C0"><enum>(1)</enum><text>impair or otherwise affect—</text><subparagraph id="H227A07B7BC4F41EAAF4DFE0A9CB29FF3"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H1114D7490F7E4A20A1881773A6D774B1"><enum>(B)</enum><text>the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals; or</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="HB2B4E34B2F3148A9B913463E8999E1CC"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.</text></paragraph></subsection></section></legis-body></bill>

<distribution-code display="yes">II</distribution-code><congress>119th CONGRESS</congress><session>1st Session</session><legis-num>S. 312</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action><action-date date="20250129">January 29, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S399">Mr. Hawley</sponsor> (for himself and <cosponsor name-id="S355">Mr. Cruz</cosponsor>) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the <committee-name committee-id="SSJU00">Committee on the Judiciary</committee-name></action-desc></action><legis-type>A BILL</legis-type><official-title>To establish a Federal tort against pediatric gender clinics and other entities pushing gender-transition procedures that cause bodily injury to children or harm the mental health of children.</official-title></form><legis-body display-enacting-clause="yes-display-enacting-clause"><section section-type="section-one" id="S1"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Jamie Reed Protecting Our Kids from Child Abuse Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="ida7c7e2e645f14b43aead23ace740c368"><enum>2.</enum><header>Federal tort for harm to children caused by gender-transition procedures</header><subsection id="id270b8c347b9e4d0aa7142e1703f3ca26"><enum>(a)</enum><header>Definitions</header><text>In this section: </text><paragraph id="idF0DF039A259C467487AE7D8714017EC6"><enum>(1)</enum><header>Gender transition procedure</header><subparagraph id="idA73ACF6151DA4B96A19D94D5E0417C56"><enum>(A)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> means—</text><clause id="id0ECCDA9A73F94C4DB2EE4D8626DC5F89"><enum>(i)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists or any other puberty-blocking drugs for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual's biological sex of male or female;</text></clause><clause id="id42E3DF7A7E584031B93D17F4EEEC152E"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the prescription or administration of testosterone (when prescribed to a female) or estrogen (when prescribed to a male) for the purpose of changing the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex of male or female; or</text></clause><clause id="id110E88FACF69454FB038F5EEB22FB8C2"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>a surgery to change the body of an individual so that it conforms to the subjective sense of identity of the individual, in the case such identity is at odds with the individual’s biological sex of male or female.</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph id="id688C33ED08B146EE9D1795B4D8A64B45"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Exception</header><text>The term <term>gender-transition procedure</term> does not include—</text><clause id="id5B8FC7BFA0104D50AD381BA47D87A259"><enum>(i)</enum><text>an intervention described in subparagraph (A) that is performed on—</text><subclause id="idCD0A622EEE8D458AABE8DABEC95DE322"><enum>(I)</enum><text>an individual with biological sex characteristics that are inherently ambiguous, such as those born with 46 XX chromosomes with virilization, 46 XY chromosomes with undervirilization, or having both ovarian and testicular tissue; or</text></subclause><subclause id="idC04B304995E6426DA1A4A617EA9A310F"><enum>(II)</enum><text>an individual with respect to whom a physician has determined through genetic or biochemical testing that the individual does not have normal sex chromosome structure, sex steroid hormone production, or sex steroid hormone action, for a biological male or biological female;</text></subclause></clause><clause id="idF57E39CF82704746A6583C7CF70CFAB4"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused or exacerbated by the performance of an intervention described in subparagraph (A) without regard to whether the intervention was performed in accordance with State or Federal law or whether the intervention is covered by the private right of action under subsection (c); or</text></clause><clause id="id66C1C4FC4B9E47AC9D67D3171C9D65CC"><enum>(iii)</enum><text>any procedure undertaken because the individual suffers from a physical disorder, physical injury, or physical illness that would, as certified by a physician, place the individual in imminent danger of death or impairment of major bodily function unless the procedure is performed. </text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph id="idF0B4A998D650442BA46911606F054246"><enum>(2)</enum><header>Hospital</header><text>The term <term>hospital</term> has the meaning given such term in section 1861(e) of the Social Security Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/1395x">42 U.S.C. 1395x(e)</external-xref>).</text></paragraph><paragraph id="idb8fb20c8993441ff868a9cd6003d5e07"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Institution of higher education</header><text>The term <term>institution of higher education</term> has the meaning given such term in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1001">20 U.S.C. 1001</external-xref>).</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id23534fbd639444a0925e5383835d1c40"><enum>(4)</enum><header>Medical practitioner</header><text>The term <term>medical practitioner</term> means a person who is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized by the laws of a State to administer health care in the ordinary course of the practice of the person’s profession.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id134d4e0acd484f1ab70c8bc3099cc078"><enum>(5)</enum><header>Minor</header><text>The term <term>minor</term> means an individual who has not yet reached 18 years of age.</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id3b0c17afc3f140608c06d703ae6be9ec"><enum>(6)</enum><header>Pediatric gender clinic</header><text>The term <term>pediatric gender clinic</term> means a medical facility that specializes in the diagnosis or treatment of gender discordance and gender dysphoria in minors, including medical interventions such as therapeutic diagnosis of gender dysphoria and performance of (or referral for) gender-transition procedures on minors.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="id2a3f64beb72f45f58980bbdd1b2f6da5"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Liability</header><text>The following individuals and entities shall be liable in accordance with this section to any individual who suffers bodily injury or harm to mental health (including any physical, psychological, emotional, or physiological harm) that is attributable, in whole or in part, to a gender-transition procedure performed on the individual when the individual was a minor:</text><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id29dea102547e45e18e52e7103f015766"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id882fc1686dec49c695e351721f6bcd10"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any medical practitioner who administered health care, at the time of the particular procedure, at the pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id727c4a97d4f7461388338b7ddc65d338"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">An institution of higher education that hosts, operates, partners with, provides funding to, or is otherwise affiliated with the pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idd794411316bc4e85a5ff1daf184deaed"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">A hospital that hosts, operates, partners with, provides funding to, or is otherwise affiliated with the pediatric gender clinic where the gender-transition procedure was provided.</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id00eacf231b1e48f8a6bd64fece31b05d"><enum>(5)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Any medical practitioner who performed the gender-transition procedure on the individual. </text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="id5725aaa7ff1f4a1c849e2f889544b7cf"><enum>(c)</enum><header>Private right of action</header><text>An individual who suffers bodily injury or harm to mental health that is attributable, in whole or in part, to a gender-transition procedure provided to the individual when the individual was a minor may, not later than 30 years after the date on which the individual turns 18 years of age, bring a civil action against an individual or entity described in subsection (b), in an appropriate district court of the United States or a State court of competent jurisdiction for—</text><paragraph id="id2e8445264db24202a4a510121f19a459"><enum>(1)</enum><text>compensatory damages;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id6abe5314eb224655b72d369ef69d0518"><enum>(2)</enum><text>punitive damages; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id696b2553ff244f28bc7158b70e67bb30"><enum>(3)</enum><text>attorney’s fees and costs.</text></paragraph></subsection><subsection id="id44ce96f70f254aa6885683acba24ed45"><enum>(d)</enum><header>Affirmative defense</header><text>It shall be an affirmative defense to an action brought by or on behalf of an individual upon whom a gender-transition procedure was performed under subsection (c) that the pediatric gender clinic or medical practitioner who performed the gender-transition procedure on the individual, at all relevant times, did not know and had no reason to know that the individual in question was a minor.</text></subsection></section><section id="ide617d512332a410b9811139f1d3bbdf3"><enum>3.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No Federal funds may be made available—</text><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id9907c41beb8548f4b57aeda5d9edb82f"><enum>(1)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">to a pediatric gender clinic;</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="ida4ff2c864cc74d2d87ab32409f5d867b"><enum>(2)</enum><text>to an institution of higher education or hospital that hosts, operates, partners with, provides funding to, or is otherwise affiliated with, a pediatric gender clinic; or</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id0da936e0cdb94cb7998ca4e92a4d1f13"><enum>(3)</enum><text>for any gender-transition procedure performed on a minor.</text></paragraph></section><section id="id4C53B78E188C4879AD89E8A415AB76AF"><enum>4.</enum><header>Effective date and retroactive application</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act shall—</text><paragraph id="id89a99013ffe24329a5ed1dd129132c78"><enum>(1)</enum><text>take effect on the date of enactment of this Act; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id98d6a50abf0e46dab3293a5944d050ae"><enum>(2)</enum><text>apply to any gender-transition procedure that took place before, on, or after the effective date under paragraph (1). </text></paragraph></section><section commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id6dcbcc746eb14243bcd4f2033b77ce04"><enum>5.</enum><header>Severability</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">If any provision of this Act, or the application of such provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be unconstitutional, the remainder of this Act, and the application of the remaining provisions of this Act, to any person or circumstance, shall not be affected.</text></section></legis-body></bill>

display-inline="no-display-inline">The Civil Rights Act of 1964 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/2000a">42 U.S.C. 2000a et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following:</text><quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id77175F2FEAE34EE2874191A35D483E43"><title id="ideada87ded9c84c879c3005b1046f3f35" style="OLC"><enum>XII</enum><header>Prohibited diversity, equity or inclusion practice defined</header><section display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H85FC53EB8B3C4747A4F4FE9FAC6BC311"><enum>1201.</enum><header>Prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">For purposes of references to this section, the term <quote>prohibited diversity, equity, or inclusion practice</quote> means—</text><paragraph id="H590A8938FFA14835A4295CBD1B031F7A"><enum>(1)</enum><text>discriminating for or against any person on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, religion, biological sex, or national origin;</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" id="H3DB1AC842E1C4F088ECB574CC1DC8B8A"><enum>(2)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">requiring as a condition of employment, as a condition for promotion or advancement, or as a condition for speaking, making a presentation, or submitting written materials, that an employee undergo training, education, or coursework, or other pedagogy, that asserts that a particular race, color, ethnicity, religion, biological sex, or national origin is inherently or systemically superior or inferior, oppressive or oppressed, or privileged or unprivileged; or</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H4A04C1957ACE4E15AEBFD17DA679752E"><enum>(3)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">requiring as a condition of employment, as a condition for promotion or advancement, or as a condition for speaking, making a presentation, or submitting written materials, the signing of or assent to a statement, code of conduct, work program, or plan, or similar device that requires assent by the employee that a particular race, color, ethnicity, religion, biological sex, or national origin is inherently or systemically superior or inferior, oppressive or oppressed, or privileged or unprivileged.</text></paragraph></section></title><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section><title subsection (c), no flag that is not the flag of the United States may be flown, draped, or otherwise displayed—</text><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" building at which the flag is displayed;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="HE88479A98C5942CA8822C707605652C8"><enum>(4)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">in the case of a Member of Forces;</text></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="iddd2e668c8b1d478a800d55d59e2d24b9"><enum>(6)</enum><text>any flag of historical significance to the United id="id92fa5713eefc427a9239cc45b3c96199"><enum>(1)</enum><text>The people of the United States deserve an excellent and efficient Federal workforce that attracts the highest caliber of civil servants id="id61557db0e79947a8b2bffdaf3a959298"><enum>(2)</enum><text>As of the date of enactment of this Act, the appointment practices of the Federal Government are broken, insular, and outdated and no id="id2a253fe153a64d789a4a9a944a37d53a"><enum>(3)</enum><text>Appointments in the Federal Government should not be focused on impermissible factors, such as a commitment to— </text><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id65bfb4f52fc645b4b9689bc58b273e23"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">illegal racial discrimination under the guise of id="id996881fac50449c5a7740c66260eb83d"><enum>(4)</enum><text>Inserting factors described in paragraph (3) into the Federal appointment process subverts the will of the people of the United States, puts critical Government functions at risk, and risks losing the best-qualified candidates.</text></paragraph></section><section commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id77a492d2163247ceb87a57d6b348c46c"><enum>4.</enum><header>Federal Hiring Plan</header><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idf7aeb430879744178895ff96418706c7"><enum>(a)</enum><header>In general</header><text>Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, and the Administrator, shall develop and submit to the head of each agency a Federal Hiring Plan that brings to the Federal workforce only highly skilled people of the United States who are dedicated to the furtherance of the ideals, values, and interests of the United States.</text></subsection><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id9c51d93149cf4dd197adc91a0e93a98b"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Contents</header><text>The Plan </text><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id3c96235eee194dd49b717d618313181e"><enum>(A)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">committed to— </text><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id8b4243e1d02b4b8ba722375006cee1a4"><enum>(i)</enum><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">improving the efficiency of the Federal Government; and</text></clause><clause commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idf7be3c7919eb48d1a177885211aabf6c"><enum>(ii)</enum><text>upholding the rule of law and the Constitution of the United States; and</text></clause></subparagraph><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idfc5d34f9713f4295be8e668732288c16"><enum>(B)</enum><text>passionate about the ideals of the United States;</text></subparagraph></paragraph><paragraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="idf0cd077d5a4848619f127be619e9a461"><enum>(2)</enum><text>prevent the appointment, by an agency, of any individual—</text><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id5e9d408e2f1343e59f58eaeab4772125"><enum>(A)</enum><text>based on the race, sex, or religion id="idec80bf8b054c4c96922329f076c3f458"><enum>(3)</enum><text>implement, to the greatest extent possible, technical and alternative assessments described in subparagraphs (A) and (B), respectively, of opportunities with respect to appointments; and</text></subparagraph><subparagraph commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="id9086088f92b048c69ccf06b230a72613"><enum>(B)</enum><text>by of gender identity expressed by any minor if such claimed identity is inconsistent with such minor’s biological sex from receiving funding under such Act.</official-title></form><legis-body style="OLC" display-enacting-clause="yes-display-enacting-clause" id="H63954C3C8B10458EB2D3741DDC8A976C"><section section-type="section-one" id="H14B2618073E04A3586DE246430439C89"><enum>1.</enum><header>Short title</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">This Act may be cited as the <quote><short-title>Guaranteeing Unalienable and Anatomical Rights for Dependents Act</short-title></quote> or the <quote><short-title>GUARD Act</short-title></quote>.</text></section><section id="H8DD17CAC9AC04FEC8C8313FC3B4C772E"><enum>2.</enum><header>State grant requirements</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">The Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/5101">42 U.S.C. 5101 et seq.</external-xref>) is amended by inserting after section 3 the following:</text><quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HD825473AC61F48429102BFD0363500AB"><section id="HA176242DB5FD4C949A3F139115675F8A"><enum>4.</enum><header>State grant requirements</header><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="H1D10FD58ED62486C842D1E40DB536738"><enum>(a)</enum><header display-inline="yes-display-inline">In general</header><text>Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no State may receive funding under this Act if such State takes any adverse action or otherwise discriminates against parents, guardians, or legal representatives who oppose medical, surgical, pharmacological, psychological treatment, or other medical intervention, or clothing, name or pronoun use, or other social changes or practices related to transitioning to or affirming the claims or expressions of gender identity of any minor under the charge, care, or supervision of the parent, guardian, or legal representative, if such gender identity is inconsistent, in such parent's, guardian's, or legal representative's estimation, with such minor’s biological sex, as determined definitively at or before birth, regardless of any medical diagnosis or indication of gender dysphoria, body dysphoria, dissociative identity disorder, or social anxiety disorder.</text></subsection><subsection commented="no" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HB4B4A8EABF71445382DB62ECB2CEF4A7"><enum>(b)</enum><header>Enforcement</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In the case of an award made by the Secretary under this Act in violation of subsection (a), any parent, guardian, or legal representative who experienced an adverse action or other discrimination described in subsection (a) by a State receiving funding under this Act may bring an action, in an appropriate Federal district court of the United States or State court, against the Department of Health and Human Services, seeking to enjoin the Secretary from continuing such award to such State and to require the State awarded amounts in violation of subsection (a) to return such funds to the Treasury.</text></subsection></section><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></section></legis-body></bill>

Limitation on Federal facilities and employees. </toc-entry><toc-entry level="section" idref="HB672573A8BDB4BDEA74C40B6554FCB7B">304. Construction relating to separate coverage. </toc-entry><toc-entry level="section" idref="H6CB9520898244D3B8531BF311FC34376">305. Construction relating to the use of non-Federal funds for health coverage. </toc-entry><toc-entry level="section" idref="HA5B2E8930C7F475A8D139ECABC2A3F9F">306. Definitions. </toc-entry></toc><section id="HA07074918092475091E3EAF2AC1C39B6"><enum>301.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No funds authorized or appropriated by Federal law, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are authorized or appropriated by Federal law, shall be expended for any gender transition procedures.</text></section><section id="H195BC353E3E443E1A77779D73C740F8A"><enum>302.</enum><header>Prohibition on funding for health benefits plans that cover gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No funds authorized or appropriated by Federal law, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are authorized or appropriated by Federal law, shall be expended for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of gender transition procedures.</text></section><section id="H39127A4AA4324232A427209B0CF20A59"><enum>303.</enum><header>Limitation on Federal facilities and employees</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">No health care service furnished—</text><paragraph id="H5A4B7A956E344E84802395D62EE12BDA"><enum>(1)</enum><text>by or in a health care facility owned or operated by the Federal Government; or</text></paragraph><paragraph id="H851FA455E9BC4334B645098FF8477DBA"><enum>(2)</enum><text>by any physician or other individual employed by the Federal Government to provide health care services within the scope of the physician’s or individual’s employment,</text></paragraph><continuation-text continuation-text-level="section">may include gender transition procedures. </continuation-text></section><section id="HB672573A8BDB4BDEA74C40B6554FCB7B"><enum>304.</enum><header>Construction relating to separate coverage</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as prohibiting any individual, entity, or State or locality from purchasing separate coverage for gender transition procedures or health benefits coverage that includes gender transition procedures so long as such coverage is paid for entirely using only funds not authorized or appropriated by Federal law and such coverage shall not be purchased using matching funds required for a federally subsidized program, including a State’s or locality’s contribution of Medicaid matching funds.</text></section><section id="H6CB9520898244D3B8531BF311FC34376"><enum>305.</enum><header>Construction relating to the use of non-Federal funds for health coverage</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as restricting the ability of any non-Federal health benefits coverage provider from offering coverage for gender transition procedures, or the ability of a State or locality to contract separately with such a provider for such coverage, so long as only funds not authorized or appropriated by Federal law are used and such coverage shall not be purchased using matching funds required for a federally subsidized program, including a State’s or locality’s contribution of Medicaid matching funds.</text></section><section id="HA5B2E8930C7F475A8D139ECABC2A3F9F"><enum>306.</enum><header>Construction relating to complications arising from gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="no-display-inline">Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to apply to the treatment of any infection, injury, disease, or disorder that has been caused by or exacerbated by the performance of a gender transition procedure. </text></section><section id="HB118F4BA1FCC43C19DDEC48968FD9D39"><enum>307.</enum><header>Definitions</header><text legal, or physical changes. </text></paragraph><paragraph id="id33a80afcd82141e986eff5bd00f81c64"><enum>(3)</enum><header>Gender transition procedure</header><subparagraph health plan</term> does not include any health plan that includes coverage for gender transition procedures, as defined in section 307 of title 1, United States Code (other than any procedure described in section 306 of such title).</text></subparagraph><subparagraph id="H633B515D7B4547C3AA9B25F7ABA8C388"><enum>(B)</enum><header>Separate coverage or plan for gender transition procedures described in such subparagraph, or a health plan that includes such gender transition procedures, so long as no credit is allowed under this section with respect to the employer contributions for such coverage or plan.</text></clause><clause id="H53CF98624B674DDD9B0CDB339D68A174"><enum>(ii)</enum><header>Option to offer coverage or plan</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">Nothing in subparagraph (A) shall restrict any non-Federal health insurance issuer offering a health plan from offering separate coverage for gender transition procedures described in such subparagraph, or a plan that includes such gender transition procedures, so long as such separate coverage or plan is not paid for with any employer contribution eligible for the credit allowed under this section.</text></clause></subparagraph></paragraph><after-quoted-block>.</after-quoted-block></quoted-block></subparagraph></paragraph></subsection><subsection Law 111–148</external-xref> (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/42/18054">42 U.S.C. 18054(a)</external-xref>) is amended by adding at the end the following new paragraph:</text><quoted-block style="OLC" display-inline="no-display-inline" id="HE4D1F5923F6C49D8AF184D18C4D4EDCC"><paragraph id="H1FEE24B6C9D842E69F6B97CDFE494033"><enum>(8)</enum><header>Coverage consistent with Federal policy regarding gender transition procedures</header><text display-inline="yes-display-inline">In entering into contracts under this subsection, the Director shall ensure that no multi-State qualified health plan offered in an Exchange provides health benefits coverage for which the expenditure of Federal funds is prohibited under <external-xref legal-doc="usc-chapter" subsection (a) shall apply to taxable years ending after the date that is 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, but only with respect to plan years beginning after such date, and the amendment made by subsection (b) shall apply to plan years beginning after such date. </text></subsection></section></title></legis-body></bill>

RES. 22</legis-num><current-chamber>IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES</current-chamber><action display="yes"><action-date date="20250113">January 13, 2025</action-date><action-desc><sponsor name-id="S317">Mr. Barrasso</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S384">Mr. Tillis</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S384">Mr. Sheehy</cosponsor>, <cosponsor name-id="S412">Mr. Tuberville</cosponsor>, and women’s sports.</official-title></form><preamble><whereas><text>Whereas athletic participation has an important positive impact on young girls, improving their physical, emotional, and psychological health, self-confidence, and discipline;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas women have been responsible for some of the greatest athletic feats in the history of sports in the United States, from the Olympic games to professional competition, through opportunities to compete in collegiate sports;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas the enactment of title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (<external-xref legal-doc="usc" parsable-cite="usc/20/1681">20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.</external-xref>) (referred to in this preamble as <quote>title IX</quote>) marked a pivotal moment in the and enduring biological differences between males and females that put females at a competitive disadvantage in sports and jeopardize their safety during competition against athletes;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas the National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (referred to in this preamble as the <quote>NAIA</quote>) has instituted new policies to protect biological women in sports and ensure that only student athletes whose biological sex is female will be allowed to compete on NAIA-sponsored women's sports teams;</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas it is imperative that opportunities for collegiate women to compete athletically are protected on the basis of sex; and</text></whereas><whereas><text>Whereas member institutions of the National Collegiate Athletic Association have an obligation under title IX to ensure equality of benefits and opportunities in athletic programs on the basis of sex: Now, therefore be it </text></whereas></preamble><resolution-body><section id="S1" display-inline="yes-display-inline" section-type="undesignated-section"><text>That the Senate—</text><paragraph id="id2aabbd6a36b84c28bf6d337b2b75ff2a"><enum>(1)</enum><text>calls on the National Collegiate Athletic Association (referred to in this resolution as <quote>NCAA</quote>) to revoke its transgender student-athlete eligibility policy that directly discriminates against female student athletes;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id6632c85f4f474577a6b8efc7e6fc6a9a"><enum>(2)</enum><text>implores the NCAA immediately to protect the integrity of collegiate women’s sports by forbidding transgender-identifying males to compete on any women’s sports roster or in any collegiate competition;</text></paragraph><paragraph id="id3d1ab531d0d14d88a74a2b853ff856c7"><enum>(3)</enum><text>urges the NCAA to require its member conferences to conform to a biological sex-based policy across all sports and all divisions; and</text></paragraph><paragraph id="idf34b4b64f1c646029c48aeb785c12c11"><enum>(4)</enum><text>calls on all sports-governing bodies in the United States to protect the category of women’s sport for biological women and girls. </text></paragraph></section></resolution-body></resolution>

<dc:title>119 SRES 295 IS: Supporting the designation of the week of June 23 through June 29, 2025, as “National Women’s Sports Week” to celebrate the anniversary of the enactment of title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 and the growth of women’s sports. </dc:title>
